features.summary: Web pages that let a company reach the team: /enterprise describes the Enterprise offer and sends visitors to /contact-sales (an email page); /contact drafts an email; /support lists channels; a dialog stores an Enterprise follow-up email; /partners emails partner applications. Mobile About has support links. The CLI has no contact entry found.

purpose.what_it_does: Presents the Enterprise offering and gives several ways to start a conversation: an email address, a mail-draft composer, a stored email request with consent, and a partner application form that emails the team (apps/web/app/enterprise/page.tsx:64-299; apps/web/app/contact-sales/page.tsx; apps/web/app/partners/PartnerApplicationForm.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: Enterprise is contract-priced and not self-serve (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:219-224), and the company states there is no partner program yet but wants to hear from integrators (apps/web/app/partners/page.tsx:68).
purpose.who_uses_it: Company buyers, security reviewers, integration builders, consultancies, and any visitor needing support.
problems_solved: Buyer needs a sales route for SSO, retention and governance
Partner or plugin builder needs a way to apply
Visitor needs honest support channels and response commitments per plan (apps/web/features/marketing/components/pages/company/support-content.ts:13-36)
Consent for storing an email must be recorded (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/public/route.ts:166)
use_cases: A security lead reads /enterprise, clicks Contact sales and emails the sales inbox with team size and review needs (apps/web/app/contact-sales/page.tsx:43-60).
A visitor on /desktop clicks 'Discuss Enterprise access', enters an email, ticks consent and presses 'Request a follow-up' (apps/web/app/desktop/page.tsx:53-56; WaitlistDialog.tsx:116, 172).
A plugin builder fills the partner form and gets a reference like PA-XXXXXXXXXX (apps/web/app/api/partners/apply/route.ts:21-24).
A logged-in user raises a ticket from Settings > Help rather than email (apps/web/app/support/page.tsx:111).

where_to_find_it: Web: footer Product > Enterprise, Company > Partners, Company > Contact, Resources > Support (apps/web/features/marketing/components/system/nav.ts:165-225).
Web: 'Contact sales' on /enterprise and on the Team band of /pricing (enterprise/page.tsx:77, 289; pricing/page.tsx:1206).
Web: 'Discuss Enterprise access' button on /desktop and /mobile hero (desktop/page.tsx:54; mobile/page.tsx:102).
Web: Apply to partner at /partners#apply (partners/page.tsx:126-137).

Mobile: About screen > Support section: Help Center, Service Status, Send Feedback, Contact Support (only when signed in and in Cloud mode), Email Support (apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx:115, 275-331).

CLI: /feedback and /bug commands send feedback to the team (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:194-199; apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs:5); one error message points to agiworkforce.com/support (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:1582). No sales or contact page entry found. The brief cites tui_app.rs:3531, which is status-footer code, not a contact entry.
Desktop, VS Code, Chrome: none found.
prerequisites: None for web pages and the dialog.
Mobile Contact Support needs sign-in and Cloud mode (about.tsx:115).
CLI feedback needs the CLI cloud feedback endpoint (apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs:5); sign-in rules not opened.
screens_and_controls: /enterprise: hero with 'Contact sales', sections on identity, policy, audit, retention and compliance, an audit-export sample, closing 'Contact sales' (enterprise/page.tsx:64-299).
/contact-sales: title 'Talk to sales.', 'Email <address>' and 'See what Enterprise includes' buttons, a 'Which door you need' table (contact-sales/page.tsx:43-65).
/contact: Name, Email, Subject, Message fields; the button opens a prefilled draft in the visitor's mail app (contact/page.tsx:17-40, 79).
/support: channels, support-by-tier table, buttons 'Email a bug report', 'Raise a ticket', 'Check service status', 'Open the contact page' (support/page.tsx:99-120).

Enterprise dialog: eyebrow 'Enterprise · contract access', title 'Discuss Enterprise access', Email address, consent checkboxes, submit 'Request a follow-up', close button (WaitlistDialog.tsx:112-176).
/partners: fields Your name, Work email, Company, Website (optional), 'What do you want to build with us?' select, 'Tell us about it', 'Send application' (PartnerApplicationForm.tsx:99-199).
journey: Open /enterprise (or /pricing Enterprise card) and read what is implemented.
Press Contact sales; /contact-sales opens with an email link.
Email the address with team size, surfaces, review needs and timeline.

Or on /desktop or /mobile press 'Discuss Enterprise access', fill email, tick the required consent, press 'Request a follow-up'; the dialog says a person will contact you (WaitlistDialog.tsx:100-110).
Or on /partners press 'Apply to partner', fill the form and send; the page shows 'Application sent.' with the reference (PartnerApplicationForm.tsx:82-86).
feedback_and_outputs: Dialog success: 'You're on the list.' with a withdrawal link to /privacy/requests (WaitlistDialog.tsx:95-110).
Dialog errors: 'Enter a valid email address.' or 'Tick the box agreeing to your email being stored before joining.' (WaitlistDialog.tsx:51-60).
Partner success: reference starting PA- (route.ts:21-24); errors 'Your application was not sent, so nothing reached us. Try again.' and a rate-limit message (PartnerApplicationForm.tsx:16, 67).
/contact: 'Email draft opened.' status, nothing stored (contact/page.tsx:76-80, 110-120).
settings: Withdrawal of a stored address: /privacy/requests, no account needed (WaitlistDialog.tsx:105-110).

Operator: AGI_SUPPORT_FALLBACK_EMAIL, RESEND_API_KEY and AGI_SUPPORT_FROM_EMAIL decide where partner mail goes and whether it can be sent (apps/web/lib/support/handoff/resend-client.ts:324-334; config.ts:87).

working: /enterprise exists and its Contact sales buttons go to /contact-sales (enterprise/page.tsx:77, 289).
/contact-sales is an email-only page (contact-sales/page.tsx:43-100).
/contact is a mail-draft composer; nothing is sent or stored by the site (contact/page.tsx:30, 79).

The Enterprise dialog validates the email, requires the Enterprise consent, posts through joinPublicWaitlist with consent surface web-waitlist-modal (WaitlistDialog.tsx:51-71) to /api/waitlist/public, which checks CSRF bound to an anonymous session, a rate limit, consent decisions, honours Global Privacy Control, writes the consent ledger and upserts cloud_managed_waitlist on (email, source) (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/public/route.ts:95-198).

The partner form exists, posts to /api/partners/apply and the route checks CSRF, rate limit and schema, then emails the team inbox with a reply-to and returns a reference; it stores nothing in the database (apps/web/app/api/partners/apply/route.ts:27-81). The brief's 'web missing' for S2.37 is out of date.
Partner page states honestly that no partner program exists yet (partners/page.tsx:68).
Mobile About shows Email Support always and Contact Support when signed in on Cloud (about.tsx:115, 313-331).
incomplete: The stored Enterprise request is not on the Enterprise sales path: /enterprise and /pricing go to the email page, while the dialog is opened from /desktop and /mobile (apps/web/app/desktop/page.tsx:53; apps/web/app/mobile/page.tsx:101). Whether other pages mount it is unknown beyond SurfaceSections (features/marketing/components/SurfaceSections.tsx:16).
Partner applications are emailed only; there is no record, status or admin view in the database [inferred from route.ts:27-81].
Developer 'listing' submissions go through the plugin directory, not the partner form (partners/page.tsx text 'List a plugin in the directory'); not opened further.
disconnected_or_disabled: If the email provider is not configured the partner route answers that the application could not be sent (route.ts:68-79; resend-client.ts:327-334).
not_available: CLI: no sales, contact or partner page entry found in apps/cli/src.
Desktop, VS Code, Chrome: nothing found.
Mobile: no sales or partner form.

established.statement: A public page presents the Enterprise offering with a sales path.
A contact or support page lets a visitor reach the company.
A form lets a prospect request an Enterprise conversation and the request is stored.
Partners and developers can submit a listing or partnership application through a form.
Enterprise dialog says a person will contact the visitor about contract-scoped access; consent is required before submit; submit goes through the waitlist client with surface web-waitlist-modal.
Enterprise capabilities are contract scoped and reached through sales; there is no dedicated capacity.

acceptance_criteria: Every Contact sales button on /enterprise and /pricing opens /contact-sales with a working mailto link.
The dialog refuses an invalid email and refuses submit without the required consent, and sends nothing in either case.
A valid dialog submit creates one cloud_managed_waitlist row (idempotent per email and source) and a consent record.
Partner form with fewer than 20 message characters is refused before any request.
A valid partner application returns a PA- reference and an email arrives at the team inbox with reply-to set.
/contact never stores the visitor's text.
Mobile Contact Support is hidden when signed out or in Local mode.
inferred: The stored Enterprise request should be reachable from the Enterprise page to meet 'the request is stored' for S2.36 [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Open the Enterprise dialog from /enterprise and /pricing, or state that email is the only route.
[proposed] Store partner applications with a status so none is lost if mail fails.

steps.what_happens: Settings panel fetches GET /api/settings/devices.
Server runs registry, legacy and sign-in grant queries for the user and computes presence from last seen.

The CLI and the desktop app post heartbeats that upsert the registration (on user_id, surface, install_id) and last seen time; the route needs a user-scoped DB, CSRF and a schema-valid body. Heartbeats from mobile, VS Code and Chrome were not found, so that every client app posts them is unverified.

Unlink first propagates revocation to live sessions and remote work (registered devices only, outside the transaction). Then, in one transaction, it revokes the device's refresh credentials and deletes the device_registrations, mobile_devices and desktop_devices rows.
Mobile remote viewing sends control messages through the paired connection store to the computer; the computer hosts the session.

features.summary: One shared set of named corner sizes, four named shadow levels (different values for light and dark) and one named stacking ladder, so dialogs, menus, toasts and tooltips sit in a fixed order and look consistent. Web and Desktop share the ladder. Mobile, VS Code and Chrome keep their own smaller copies.

purpose.what_it_does: It gives every surface named values for how round a corner is, how deep a shadow is, and which layer sits on top. Components pick a name such as corner-field, shadow-e3 or z-modal instead of a number. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:270-279, 318-340, 358-361)
purpose.why_it_exists: Without a shared ladder, each component invents its own number and layers collide (a menu hidden behind a dialog) or corners look uneven. The foundation file says the ladder exists so consumers never invent a numeric rung. (packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:315-317)
purpose.who_uses_it: Designers and engineers building UI on all apps that draw their own visuals (Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code, Chrome). End users never set it; they only see it. The CLI has no corners, shadows or layers.
problems_solved: Menus and popovers appearing behind dialogs.
Corners and shadows that differ from screen to screen.
Dark mode shadows that are too faint to see (dark theme has its own stronger shadow values). (foundation.css:524-527)
Raw numeric z-index values creeping into components (a repo guard rejects them). (scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs:155-170)
use_cases: A Dialog opens over the page at z-modal with the e4 shadow and large rounded corners. (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Dialog.tsx:28,115)
A dropdown menu opens from inside a dialog and stays on top because the popover rung (350) is above the modal rung (300). (foundation.css:335-336; DropdownMenu.tsx:104)
A mobile toast shows above screens at the notification layer. (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/Toast.tsx:181)
A VS Code sidebar model menu opens on its own popover layer. (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:222,1347)

features.summary: Asks before the assistant uses a device capability. Explains microphone use on mobile and Chrome, asks before computer or browser control and before reading or writing a folder, shows each tool call for approval, and pairs a phone by code or QR. Scopes are wider than one call in several apps, and mobile pairing is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Gates device powers behind a question the person can answer, remembers the answer, and lets them revoke it. Also links another device to a desktop.
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can click, type, read files and run commands. People must stay in control of what it may touch, and a phone should only join a desktop the person owns.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using voice, computer use, browser control, folder tools, code agents or remote control.
problems_solved: Unexpected microphone or screen use
Agent touching folders without consent
Repeated stacked prompts
Pairing a stranger's phone
use_cases: First voice dictation on Chrome shows a notice, then the browser asks
Desktop asks before the assistant controls the mouse and keyboard
Approve one shell command in the CLI
Show a pairing QR on desktop to link a phone

working: Desktop requestPermission asks once, stores the answer, returns the stored state and joins an open question for the same key (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts:318, :334)
Computer-use commands map to capability computer.use and are gated before running (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:1100, :3418)
Folder commands are gated per workspace root with a separate agent-first check (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3447)
High-impact permissions last only until quit (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts:387)

The capabilities computer.use, host.remote, shell.execute, application.control, browser.cdp and git.destructive are all high-risk, so computer-control prompts never offer 'Always allow' and last only until the app quits (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/capabilities.ts:67-74)

Chrome browser control needs both an in-extension record and the browser's site permission, per normalized origin, and refuses the account origins (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/browserControlConsent.ts:120, :133)
Chrome microphone notice shows once and stores an acknowledgment (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/voice.ts:28, :104)

Pairing is gated by remoteControlStandingRefusal, which runs three checks in order: the workspace feature gate, the plan (403 plan_upgrade_required unless canUseBillingPlanCapability(plan,'remote_control'); the capability maps to PAID_TIERS, so Free is refused), then the screen-share kill switch. The same check runs on initiate and claim, and a plan lookup failure returns 503. Mobile also checks the plan client-side (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:62-125, packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352, apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:66)

established.statement: Permission asks once, records the answer, does not re-prompt after refusal; a repeat request joins the open question.
Each tool approval covers one call.
Pairing is bound to the signed-in account and fails clearly on a wrong or expired code.
Browser control is granted per site origin and can be revoked.
Execution boundaries are explicit; nothing silently crosses Local, own key or Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: First computer-control request shows one dialog naming the action; a second request while it is open does not add a dialog
After Deny the same request in that session returns permission-denied without a new dialog
Removing a Chrome site's browser control stops runs on it
A folder not yet approved is not read by the assistant
Approve on one tool card runs that call only, if the policy is ask every time
A wrong or expired pairing code fails with a clear message
A phone on another account cannot claim a code
Mic refused on mobile shows how to turn it on
inferred: Brief 'covers one call' conflicts with session and always scopes that the same dialogs offer [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Show an explanation dialog before the first microphone request on web and desktop
[proposed] Fix the stale mobile pairing copy
[proposed] Offer a persistent Deny so a refusal sticks across sessions

steps.what_happens: A command arrives at the desktop runtime and is mapped to a capability
If the state is 'prompt', a native dialog asks; the answer is recorded; Deny records a session denial
Granted: the command runs; single-use grants are consumed
Pairing: desktop calls /api/pair/initiate; the server runs the standing check (workspace gate, paid plan, kill switch) and mints a code bound to the account
Phone scans the code and calls /api/pair/claim; the same standing check runs; account mismatch returns 403
Desktop asks again to allow the phone itself before it connects

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model decides these permissions. The approvals gate what a model-driven agent may do on the device. Remote Control reads and steers coding sessions from the phone.

access_and_usage.account: Pairing needs a signed-in account on both devices, and the account must be on a paid plan. Other permissions work without an account for device-local actions [inferred].
access_and_usage.permissions: Per capability and scope on desktop (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts:334); per origin on Chrome; per workspace root for folders; per tool identity in VS Code (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/permissions/approvalScope.ts:60).
access_and_usage.subscription: Pairing needs a paid plan (every tier in PAID_TIERS), passing the workspace policy gate, and the screen-share switch being open. The same standing check (remoteControlStandingRefusal) runs on initiate and claim; Free is refused with 403 plan_upgrade_required, and a plan lookup failure returns 503 (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:62-125, packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352, apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:66). Mobile also reads a plan check for remote control (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:108).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Pairing requests rate limited under 'device-link' (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:63); code lifetime 30 to 900 seconds, default 300 (route.ts:20, :25).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: none found in the code
access_and_usage.local_mode: Desktop and CLI permissions are local and need no subscription. Pairing and Remote Control use the AGI relay, so they are cloud account features and need a paid plan.

aliases: Get started with AGI Code (VS Code walkthrough)
features.summary: Short first-run flows on each app. Web has a two-step wizard at /welcome with starter prompts. Mobile has hero, about-you and device-setup screens. The CLI has a terminal setup wizard. VS Code has a walkthrough and a first-run panel. Chrome opens a Welcome page on install. Each can be skipped.

purpose.what_it_does: Greets a first-time person, asks for light personalization or setup, and then lands them in the first chat. Web asks for a preferred name and work description, then offers starter prompts. Mobile asks to accept terms, collects name and work, then offers a local model download or sign in to Cloud. (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:36) (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:280)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says first-time users are shown a short introduction to key features before or at their first chat (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/012-new-chat-experience.md, S12.22). Mobile requirements: onboarding shows brand and privacy summary, explains Local, BYOK and Cloud, checks local model readiness and never blocks Local use (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, M-ONB-001 to M-ONB-005).
purpose.who_uses_it: New users on every app.
problems_solved: Empty new-chat screens do not tell a new person what to do.
Personal details (name, work) make the first replies fit the person.
Setup of how to connect (account, own key, local model) must happen once.
use_cases: After sign-up on web, answer 'What should we call you?' and pick a starter prompt that fills the composer.
Install the mobile app, tap 'Start chatting', accept the notice, download the recommended local model, and land in chat.
Run the CLI for the first time and choose how to connect.
Install the Chrome extension and read the Welcome page.

features.summary: Shows each attachment before sending as a chip: a thumbnail for images, an icon with kind and size for documents, and a remove control. Web and desktop, phone, VS Code and Chrome have chips; the CLI lists staged items in text. Only the phone opens an image full screen. No app replaces a file in place.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person see what is attached, tell files apart, and take one out before the message goes.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be sure the right files go to the model and must be able to undo a mistake. Brief items S14.16 to S14.18, S14.22, S14.28 to S14.30.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who attaches files on any app.
problems_solved: Sending the wrong file
Not knowing whether a file is still uploading or ready
Telling several files with similar names apart
use_cases: Drop two pictures on web, see two thumbnails numbered in image-edit mode, remove one.
Phone: tap a picture chip to look at it full screen, then remove it.
CLI: run /attach list to see what is staged, /attach remove 2 to drop one.
VS Code: drag a file in, see its icon and size, press the X.

features.summary: While a reply is running, a message you type waits in a queue (shown as a Queued row with Edit and Cancel) and is sent when the reply ends. Unsent text is also kept as a draft per conversation. Web syncs drafts across devices. VS Code marks each message Sending, Queued, Running, Steered, Not sent or Cancelled.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds follow-up messages written during a running reply, shows them as waiting, and sends them when the turn ends. Keeps unsent composer text for each conversation so leaving and returning does not lose it (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3951-3972,4342-4420).
purpose.why_it_exists: People think of the next question while the model is still answering. They also leave chats half-written. Without a queue and a draft the text is lost or the send is blocked. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats; developers on VS Code, CLI and Chrome use the same ideas in their own forms.
problems_solved: A second message typed during a reply is not lost.
Unsent text survives switching chats, reloads and, on web, other devices.
A failed or cancelled send is visible as its own state (VS Code).
use_cases: Type a follow-up while a long answer streams; it appears as 'Queued: <text>' and goes out when the answer ends.
Click Edit on a queued row to change it, or Cancel to drop it.
Half-write a message, open another chat, come back and find the text there.
Edit the same draft on two web tabs and choose which version to keep.

where_to_find_it: Web composer: a list labelled 'Queued messages' above the input with rows 'Queued: <text>' (or 'Queued 1 of 2: <text>'), and buttons Edit and Cancel, and Steer when the running reply can take it (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5009-5063).

steps.what_happens: Person presses send while a turn is active; the composer stores the send arguments with the conversation id and clears the box.
When the turn ends, the composer sends the first queued item in the same conversation; items for another conversation become a draft and a notice.
Draft text is parked in the web chat store and in browser storage as the person types.
After the debounce the sync hook PUTs the draft with its revision to the conversation route; the server writes draft and draft_updated_at or answers 409 with the current draft.
A conflict opens a toast and dialog; the person keeps this version or the other.
Mobile saves drafts in on-device storage; Chrome in session storage; VS Code in webview state; CLI in memory.

features.summary: Shows a reference like [^1] as a small raised marker tied to a note at the bottom of the answer. Web, desktop and Chrome link the marker to a footnotes list with a back-link. Mobile shows a numbered marker, a bottom list, and an alert on tap. VS Code and CLI have no footnote support.

purpose.what_it_does: Links a marker in the text to a note, so an answer can carry side comments without breaking the sentence.
purpose.why_it_exists: Models sometimes use Markdown footnotes. Without support the reader sees literal [^1] text (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/020-markdown-and-text-rendering.md S20.14).
purpose.who_uses_it: Readers of answers that cite or annotate with footnotes.
problems_solved: Raw [^1] markers do not litter the text.
Notes are reachable and the reader can return to the spot (web, Chrome).
Two messages on one page do not clash ids (web).
use_cases: Read an answer with a definition note.
Jump from a marker to its note and back.
Tap a marker on mobile to read the note.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Tauri): markers and a footnotes section at the end of the message (remark-gfm output, MarkdownContent.tsx:339-343, 891-894).

Mobile: marker in text, tap opens an alert titled 'Footnote <n>' unless the caller passes onFootnotePress, in which case that handler runs and no alert shows (MarkdownInline.tsx:49, 157-159, 410-430), and a 'Footnotes' list at the end of the message (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:876-925, 1672-1675).
Chrome: raised number linking to a section labelled 'Footnotes' with a back-link (markdown.ts:217-246; test side-panel-markdown-parity.test.ts:216-260).
prerequisites: A reply with a footnote reference and a definition line like [^1]: text.
screens_and_controls: Web and Chrome: click the marker to jump; click the back arrow to return.
Mobile: tap the marker (button role when a note exists).
journey: Reply has [^1] and [^1]: text.
Marker is drawn raised.
Reader activates it.
Web and Chrome jump to the list item; mobile opens an alert, or runs the caller's onFootnotePress handler instead when one is supplied (MarkdownInline.tsx:49,413,424).
feedback_and_outputs: Raised numbered marker.
Footnotes list at the bottom.
Mobile alert with the note's plain text (default; replaced by the onFootnotePress handler when supplied).
settings: None found.

working: Web and desktop: footnote links stay in the same tab and their target id gets the sanitiser prefix so the jump lands (MarkdownContent.tsx:335-343, 371-378). A per-message scope keeps ids unique (891-894; test MarkdownContent.render.test.tsx:329).

Streaming: a settled block that uses a footnote label is not trusted until the definition arrives; the whole message folds into one unit (StreamingMarkdownContent.tsx:22-47, 89-103; test StreamingMarkdownContent.test.tsx:221-235).

Mobile: footnote nodes parse, number and, on tap, open an alert titled 'Footnote <n>' via Alert.alert(`Footnote ${n}`, inlinePlainText(note)) as the fallback (MarkdownInline.tsx:157-159, 410-430). If context.options.onFootnotePress is supplied it is called with the label instead and no alert shows (MarkdownInline.tsx:49,413,424; test MarkdownInline.render.test.tsx:545 exercises it with a jump callback). A Footnotes section lists referenced notes (MessageContentRenderer.tsx:1634-1636, 1672-1675).
Chrome: markdown-it-footnote with custom renderers, a labelled section, and a back-link labelled with the note number (markdown.ts:217-246).

Web footnote parsing is not a footnote-specific plugin: REMARK_PLUGINS holds remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks, remarkLosslessTables and remarkAssistantFenceIdentity (remarkPlugins.ts:71-77). Footnote ids use a clobberPrefix built from footnoteScope (MarkdownContent.tsx:891-894); unscoped callers get an empty prefix, so id uniqueness depends on the caller.
incomplete: Mobile list items have no back-link (renderFootnoteSection draws number and text only, MessageContentRenderer.tsx:876-925).

features.summary: When the assistant needs permission for an action, an approval card shows what it will do, a risk label and the parameters, with Allow and Deny choices. When it needs facts from you, a question card lets you pick options or type an answer and send. Each app has its own version.

purpose.what_it_does: Approval cards stop a tool call until the person allows or denies it (once, for this chat, or always where the scope is offered). Question cards (clarify.v1) show up to four questions with up to four options each and an optional 'something else' box; the answers go back to the assistant as the next turn input. (apps/web/features/chat/components/approvals/ToolApprovalCard.tsx:57-140; apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts:12-16; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ClarifyCard.tsx:86-229)
purpose.why_it_exists: Consent must be explicit before an action that changes things, and a vague request is better answered with a few structured questions than with a guess. (doc: AGENTS.md section 9; area brief S22.28, S22.29)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using an agent that calls tools (all six apps) and anyone whose request is vague (the model-driven clarify tool is offered on web, desktop via hosted web, mobile and Chrome; VS Code has its own separate 'AGI asks' question card that does not come from clarify.v1; CLI shows tool-server questions). [apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1278-1291; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:7262-7300]
problems_solved: The person sees the tool name, risk tier, destructive notice and parameters before saying yes.
The assistant does not guess missing details; it asks.
A tool server can ask for typed input (CLI elicitation) without leaving the terminal.
use_cases: A cloud tool wants to send data to a connector; the card shows the parameters and the person presses Allow once.
A vague request 'plan my trip' triggers a card with questions about dates and budget; the person picks options and presses Send answers.
In the CLI, a command run asks 'Apply this patch?' with y/n keys.
An MCP server asks for a token; the CLI overlay shows a masked field with Accept, Decline, Cancel.

steps.what_happens: The model calls the clarify tool or a tool needing approval; the server builds a card and streams it with the reply. The clarify tool is offered only on web, mobile and chrome surfaces, to tool-capable models, on streamed requests whose client declares clarify.v1.
The app validates the card, shows it, and blocks sending while streaming or in a temporary chat.

The person's answer is posted to the respond route, which authenticates the user, requires a CSRF token, applies the chat-message rate limit, then either returns composed message text (answer-ui card with payload.kind 'message', nothing stored) or settles the clarify card with a compare-and-set update of the stored message (matches the old metadata with 'is not distinct from'; 409 if no row changed).
The paused turn resumes with the answer.
CLI approval and elicitation are answered on the device and returned to the local agent loop or MCP server.

access_and_usage.permissions: Approvals gate tool execution; risk tier and destructive flag come from a review object (tool-approval-presentation.ts:8-14). Unreviewed tools default to high risk, destructive, once-only.

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Max 4 questions, 4 options, option label 60, question text 200 characters (clarify-tool-service.ts:15-20); header chip max 32; other-answer text capped at 500 characters (CLARIFY_OTHER_MAX_LENGTH, packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts:84; imported at ClarifyCard.tsx:14). Interactive cards are capped at 4 per message and 12,000 serialized characters (interactive-cards.ts:13-14). The clarify tool is offered only for non-research messages of 1 to 400 characters with no attachment, no URL and no code fence, and (outside AGI Work mode) not starting with an explicit-command verb such as search, write, explain, fix, list (clarify-tool-service.ts:17,20,22-40,53-63). The respond route uses getUserScopedDb auth, requireCsrfToken and withRateLimit with the 'chat-message' bucket (route.ts:93-103).

access_and_usage.local_mode: CLI approval overlay works on the device. Question cards come from a server tool, so a fully Local chat would not show them [inferred]; not verified.

aliases: Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox in Library
features.summary: The Library cannot browse Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox, refresh external file metadata, save external content as a copy, or mark a row as an external reference. Every Library row is an owned stored file. Drive and OneDrive features exist elsewhere in the web app, in connectors and project knowledge, not in the Library.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let people browse connected cloud drives from the Library, refresh the details of linked files, save an external file as an owned copy and tell references from owned files.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires connected-file browsing and clear separation of owned and external files (S24.37 to S24.40), as leader products do. (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:178 notes connected storage expanding in a leader's Library)
purpose.who_uses_it: People whose documents live in Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox. Nobody can use it in the Library yet.
problems_solved: Planned: using cloud documents without manual download.
Planned: keeping linked file details current.
Planned: knowing which files are only linked.
use_cases: Browse a Drive folder and add a doc to a chat.
Save a Drive file as an owned copy.
Refresh the title of a linked file.
See an 'external' badge on a linked file.

where_to_find_it: Not available in the Library on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome.

Nearby but separate: a Google Drive picker endpoint and save-to-Drive and save-to-OneDrive endpoints for artifacts exist in the web app (apps/web/app/api/connectors/google-drive/picker/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/save-to-drive/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/save-to-onedrive/route.ts); where they appear in the UI: unknown.
prerequisites: None for the Library; the feature does not exist there.
screens_and_controls: Library filters are the tab and surface filters over owned files only; origin is 'uploaded' or 'generated' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/library.ts:5).

No connected-storage control in the Library header or New menu (the shared packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:975-985 is a hidden file input, not the menu; in the web host, Create folder navigates to Projects, apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:148, and upload is wired through uploadChatAttachments at :179-180).

In the web host, Add to project copies the library file into project knowledge via readLibraryItemFile (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:234-237); this is a copy of an owned file, not a connected-storage action.
journey: Open the Library.
Look for a connected drive source: none appears.
Workaround: import a Drive file into a project through Projects (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/[fileId]/refresh/route.ts shows a Drive refresh exists there).
feedback_and_outputs: No output in the Library.
settings: Connector availability is controlled elsewhere (assertConnectorsReleased is called by the Drive picker route: apps/web/app/api/connectors/google-drive/picker/route.ts:19).

working: Every Library row is an owned media_assets row; origin is only 'uploaded' or 'generated' (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:66-89; library.ts:5).

Drive picker configuration route (returns 'not-configured' without the picker key and app id) (picker/route.ts:20-30). When configured it returns status 'ready' with the Drive access token, developer key and app id to the caller, so file selection runs in the browser against Google (picker/route.ts:44-52).

Drive import and refresh for project knowledge exist in project knowledge code (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/[fileId]/refresh/route.ts:1-20; importDriveFileIntoProject in apps/web/lib/server/project-drive-import.ts:121).

CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE in packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14 is 'coming_soon', and Drive and Dropbox are not in SELECTIVELY_RELEASED_CONNECTOR_IDS, so as the code stands the picker route is blocked [read from the constant; deployed behaviour not run].

steps.what_happens: Person asks for a PDF; the server detects creation intent and adds the file tool to the turn (the request must be streaming and the model tool-capable, else HTTP 422 office_creation_stream_required / office_creation_model_unsupported)
The chat model calls the tool with filename, title and content
The server validates and builds the PDF in process with jsPDF
If verify_render is set, a sandbox converts and rasterises it for a receipt; with no sandbox the call fails

The tool loop saves the bytes with persistGeneratedFileBytes (provider 'agi-managed-office', origin 'managed-office-tool', tied to the conversation) and attaches the file to the reply for download, returning file name, uri, mime and byte_count; if saving fails the reply is 'The Office file could not be attached.'
Artifact PDF on Web: built in the browser and saved by the browser
Mobile: the system print service writes a PDF file, moved to an export path

features.summary: Rules for what memory may hold and use. People list terms to never remember; credentials and other prohibited facts are refused for every source; sensitive topics need opt-in for automatic saves. Temporary chats neither read nor save memory. Web and mobile show which memories a reply used. The server applies one memory context to every model.

purpose.what_it_does: Enforces privacy rules on memory: a never-remember list of terms, automatic refusal of credential-like and other prohibited facts, an opt-in for sensitive topics, temporary chats that skip memory completely, a 'Memory · N' indication on replies that used memory, and the same memory for every model and every signed-in client.
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to stop sensitive information being remembered and see when memory shaped a reply. Brief S39.27 to S39.32 and docs/product/requirements.md:765 require temporary chats to neither update nor reference memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who uses memory; privacy-minded people; workspace admins relying on policy; testers.
problems_solved: Passwords, payment details or identifiers ending up in memory.
Private topics being remembered without consent.
Not knowing whether an answer came from memory.
Memory working on one model or app and not another.
use_cases: Add 'home address' to Never remember; a later attempt to save a fact containing it is refused with a message naming the term.
Start a temporary chat and tell the assistant a fact; it is not saved and no memory is read.
Open a reply's 'Memory · 3' control to see which saved facts were used.

steps.what_happens: Person adds a term; the client saves it in the account's memory settings namespace.
Any memory write reaches the server, which loads the list (failing closed on error), then runs the content and policy gate.
For a chat turn the server checks if the conversation is temporary; if so it uses a disabled memory policy and loads no memory or past chats.
Otherwise it loads memories filtered by user, workspace, project and suppressed sources, ranks them against the question, takes up to 30, and places them in the prompt fenced as untrusted data.
The model provider receives the prompt; the reply stream carries memory citations back to the app.
The app shows 'Memory · N' from the citations.
After the turn, automatic saving extracts facts, applies the exclusions and the eligibility gate and writes rows.
Other clients pull the new rows by delta sync.

data.synced: Read by every client of the account
data.retained_or_deleted: Until the person removes them; existing memories containing a term are not deleted (MemoryExclusions.tsx:162 copy)

data.where_stored: table user_memories; citations travel in the reply metadata and are stored on the assistant message
data.retained_or_deleted: Deleted memories keep a text-less tombstone (managed-memory-context-service.ts:391)

Purged by a scheduled job, which the route's delete queries target at web_conversations flagged temporary after RETENTION_DAYS = 30 (purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:24,44-83); mobile banner says normally deleted after 30 days (TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:11-12)
Cleared by the person or by data deletion (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Memory is added by the server for every model and provider and no model identifier enters the query (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128). Auto-extraction may use a utility model route when the environment flag is on and the turn is not zero-data-retention (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:36-58). On Local-model turns on web and desktop the device asks for account memory and injects it itself (useChatStream.ts:4479); in own-key and Local modes content outside Managed storage is never saved to user_memories (trust_mode_outside_managed_storage, managed-memory-context-service.ts:540,654).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: At least 3 characters per term and at most 50 terms per account (the 100-character cap is a web input limit only; the server does not enforce it: MemoryExclusions.tsx:186, managed-memory-context-service.ts:283-298); 30 memories and 8,000 characters per prompt; at most 5 automatic memories per turn (managed-memory-context-service.ts:67-72 MAX_AUTO_MEMORIES_PER_TURN); mobile reads up to 5 local facts per turn (chatExecutionStore.ts retrieveMemoryContext(content, 5)) only when memory reads are enabled and the app, not the server, assembles the context (chatExecutionStore.ts:2798-2803); in Cloud mode the server builds the context.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION for model-based auto extraction; user switches memory, generateFromHistory, searchPastChats, includeSensitiveTopics, allowToolAssistedGeneration (readUserMemoryCapabilities, managed-memory-context-service.ts:258).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Same for every model; no capability check was found. Tool-assisted memory generation has its own switch.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Memory is not saved from turns in own-key or Local trust modes (managed-memory-context-service.ts:654). Content tied to Google user data is excluded from memory reads (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1170 memoryFreeOfGoogleUserDataSql).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode keeps memory on the device, always refuses credential-like and other prohibited facts, refuses sensitive topics only for learned (automatic) saves unless the person opted in (explicit saves of sensitive topics go through), skips memory in temporary chats, and has no never-remember term check (localMemoryWriter.ts:30-39). CLI Local sessions do not receive account memory; only Managed sessions do (apps/cli/src/cloud/memory.rs:1-7). Desktop Tauri has a Local-mode temporary chat that skips memory (apps/desktop/src/features/chat/useTemporaryChat.ts:1-15).

steps.what_happens: The request passes CSRF validation, the adult-eligibility (18 and over) age gate and the rate limit, then the managed compute gate, organization policy and the workspace spend cap check.

The server estimates cost and reserves it atomically against the plan. A 402 or 429 raised by reserveManagedUsageRequest is mapped to insufficient_quota (managedUsageErrorResponse, lines 118-132); only a failure that is not a ManagedUsageRequestError becomes 503 billing_unavailable (757-766).

After the attempt, the reservation is finalized at the settled cost, or released at zero charge to the account for failure, refusal or cancel. For unsaved output the provider cost is recorded as undelivered cost.
The client shows a refusal message only; no figure is returned to display. The client is the browser on Web and the app on Mobile and Desktop.

features.summary: Video-generation studio does not let a person pick a frame rate or supply reference audio on any app. The generate request has no field for either. The only audio control the server accepts is a yes/no generate_audio flag, and no client sends it. Both items are missing everywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person choose a clip's frame rate (where a video model supports it) and attach reference audio (a voice or music track) that guides the clip's sound. Today neither exists. The server accepts only prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, a generate_audio flag, provider, model, candidate count and image inputs (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:193-217).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists both as parts of a complete video studio: S46.09 (frame rate where the model supports it) and S46.14 (reference audio where supported) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md). Competitor guidance tells engineers to inspect audio behaviour and references in video workflows (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.17, item 132).
purpose.who_uses_it: People making short clips in the Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome video modes who want smoother or cinematic motion, or a specific voice or soundtrack. CLI and VS Code have no video mode, so they do not apply (brief status n/a).
problems_solved: Today: none, because the feature is not built.
If built: a person could match a clip's motion rate to their project and keep a consistent voice or music across clips.
use_cases: Pick 24 or 30 frames per second for a social clip (not possible today).
Attach a narration voice sample so the generated characters speak in that voice (not possible today).
Attach a music track as the mood reference for a clip (not possible today).

where_to_find_it: Not available on Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome. The Web video controls are the video model menu, 'Select video aspect ratio', 'Select video quality' and 'Select video length', with no frame-rate or audio control (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6561, :6614, :6668, :6857).

Mobile 'Create video' sheet offers 'Video model' and aspect, resolution and duration pickers, with no frame-rate or audio control found (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:943, :966).
CLI and VS Code: no video mode (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md).
prerequisites: Not applicable: nothing to use. Video generation in general needs a signed-in account on a plan that includes video generation (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1001-1012, :1102-1115).
screens_and_controls: No frame-rate control and no audio-upload control exist. A search of apps and packages for frame-rate and reference-audio names found no matches in TypeScript or TSX sources.
journey: A person opens video mode and writes a prompt.
They can set model, aspect ratio, quality and length, but no frame rate or audio file.
They send. The request carries no frame rate or audio reference.
feedback_and_outputs: No related feedback exists. The clip comes back at whatever frame rate the provider chooses; the app never states one [inferred from the absent field].
settings: None. generate_audio is a request field the server accepts but the Web client's request type omits it (apps/web/features/media/services/media-api-service.ts:41-51).

working: The server decides audio on its own: generate_audio defaults to the model's supportsAudio flag, or true for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1207-1208).
The server refuses audio when the model does not support it and refuses audio-off for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:469-474).
Generated audio is passed to OpenRouter as generate_audio (apps/web/lib/services/openrouter-video-provider-service.ts:147).

Candidate count n (1 to MANAGED_MEDIA_MAX_VIDEO_CANDIDATES) makes one durable job and one billed reservation per candidate, so metered video_seconds scale with n (managed-media.ts:204; route.ts:1239-1246).
Runway has its own prompt cap of 1,000 characters (route.ts:1209-1210) and its own submission path (generateWithRunway); this is an option difference between providers.
incomplete: The model catalog describes video models with durations, output sizes, audio support and seed support only; there is no frame-rate field (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:213-219).
disconnected_or_disabled: generate_audio exists in the shared request schema (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:199) but no app UI sends it (media-api-service.ts:41-51; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:126; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:610-613).

Reference-audio input: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Both: CLI and VS Code (no video mode).

established.statement: A person picks the frame rate of the clip where the model supports it.
A person supplies reference audio (voice or music) for the clip where supported.
Advertised video options must produce real decodable media, and unsupported configurations must show an honest disabled state.

acceptance_criteria: When a video model declares supported frame rates, the composer shows a frame-rate control listing only those rates; models that declare none show no control.
The generate request carries the chosen frame rate and the server rejects a rate the model does not list, in the same way it rejects an unsupported duration (route.ts:446-481 pattern).
A model that accepts reference audio shows an audio attach control; a model that does not shows it disabled with a reason.
Reference audio is validated for type and size before upload and is covered by the same content-safety checks as prompts and images.

steps.what_happens: The person writes a prompt and sets model, aspect ratio, quality and length in the video composer; no frame-rate or audio file step exists.

The Web client posts prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, provider, model and optional images (first_frame_image, reference_images) to the Cloud route, along with conversation_id and assistant_message_id. The route schema extends the shared strict schema with conversation_id and assistant_message_id.

The server validates the body against the shared schema (unknown fields are rejected because the schema is strict), then resolves audio, checks model limits, billing allowance and starts a durable job.
The job calls the video provider (Runway, Google or OpenRouter) with the chosen model; frame rate and audio reference are never sent.

features.summary: Lets a person leave live voice and keep going in the same chat by typing. On web the voice screen also has a typed field that sends a normal text turn while the call stays open. iPhone has 'Type instead' to leave the call. In the CLI, spoken text can be edited before sending, and Esc returns to the same typed session.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a way to move between speaking and typing without losing the conversation. Voice turns are saved as messages in the same chat as typed ones, so ending a call leaves a normal chat to continue (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6739-6790).
purpose.why_it_exists: Voice fails or is unwelcome at times: noisy rooms, limits reached, no microphone, sensitive text. The brief requires that unfinished work can continue in text (S48.38). The brief calls typing during voice and transcript editing not applicable, but the code has both on web and the CLI.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop users in a voice call, iPhone users in a live call, CLI users in /voice.
problems_solved: A usage limit or error ends the call but the task is not finished.
Names, numbers and code are hard to speak.
A wrong transcript is sent to the assistant (CLI lets the person fix it first).
use_cases: Ask something by voice, then type a precise follow-up in the voice screen on web.
Hit the voice limit, press 'Continue in text', and keep the same chat.
On iPhone tap 'Type instead' to bring up the keyboard in the same chat.
In the CLI press 'e' to edit the transcribed sentence, then Enter to send.

where_to_find_it: Web and public Desktop: the voice screen's pill composer with a text field placeholder 'Type' (aria-label 'Type a message to send as a normal turn') and a round close button 'End voice session' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceComposer.tsx:9-17, 101-110, 133-145). 'Continue in text' appears in the usage-limit and voice-unavailable rows (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:330-344).

iPhone: 'Type instead' button (accessibility label 'Switch to text for this chat') at the bottom of the live bar, and 'Type a message instead' inside an error box (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:418, 704-718).
CLI: /voice (alias /v) in the TUI or REPL; Esc leaves voice mode (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6352-6368; apps/cli/src/voice.rs:178-186).
prerequisites: A started voice session (web: managed Cloud chat; iPhone: Cloud chat; CLI: build with the voice feature, i.e. macOS or Windows release builds) (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:124-132; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:240-278).
screens_and_controls: Web: text field, mic mute button, close button, 'Add' button 'Open this chat panel' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceComposer.tsx:11-17, 87-146). Enter sends typed text; Space toggles mute only while the field is empty; Escape ends voice (lines 57-77).
iPhone: 'Type instead', route button, mute, 'End live voice' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:704-757).
CLI prompt: '[ENTER to send, 'e' to edit, 'r' to re-record, ESC to discard]' (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:231-236).
journey: Web typing during a call: 1. Start voice mode. 2. Click the 'Type' field and write a message. 3. Press Enter. 4. The call stays open; the message is sent as an ordinary chat turn and the reply is written, not spoken [inferred from apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:893-896].

Web leaving voice: 1. Press the close button, or Escape, or 'Continue in text'. 2. The session closes and settles usage (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:501-506). 3. The normal composer returns in the same chat (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7665-7675, 7793-7805).
iPhone: 1. Tap 'Type instead'. 2. The live bar hides and the chat input gets focus (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1779-1782). 3. Type in the same chat.

CLI: 1. Run /voice. 2. Hold Space to record, release. 3. Choose Enter, e, r or Esc. 4. Press Esc at the prompt to return to the typed prompt in the same session (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7556-7580). Esc means different things by prompt: at the record prompt it exits voice (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:574), and at the confirm prompt it discards only that sentence and stays in voice (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:599).

steps.what_happens: Web: Enter in the voice field calls submitTyped, which always forwards the text to the chat send path. The state moves to streaming only from listening, muted, transcribing, sending, speaking or error; in other states it stays as it was. A failed send dispatches fail.
The typed message goes through the normal chat pipeline on our servers to the chat's model.
Each final spoken turn is added to the list and saved to the conversation without a model call.
Leaving voice closes the realtime connection, then records the session close and its usage.

CLI: audio is recorded locally, then transcribed by the signed-in AGI account, the OpenAI transcription API, or a local whisper binary; the text is sent to the agent session like typed text.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Spoken turns on web use the realtime model from the voice_live routing slot (on a managed provider route) for speech and the plan's backend slot model for delegated work (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:189-193, 311-318). A typed turn uses the chat's selected model, or the 'Chat intelligence' choice set in Voice settings (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceSettingsModal.tsx:45). CLI transcription uses AGI managed, OpenAI Whisper API with OPENAI_API_KEY, or a local whisper binary (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-6).

access_and_usage.account: iPhone live voice needs a Cloud chat and a signed-in user (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:19-28). Web voice is gated by the route's auth and scoped-db check (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts). CLI managed transcription needs 'agi login'; other backends need a key or binary (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:127-143).
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone permission. CLI asks for agreement before recording and states where audio goes (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:379-420).
access_and_usage.subscription: Opening voice needs a managed-compute subscription state that is allowed, the canUseVoice capability and a plan with allowVoice (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:279-318, 336-348). Free has allowVoice with 10 minutes a calendar month (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1234-1259; apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-52). Paid plans are charged against the usage budget. Typing has no separate rule.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Voice minutes are metered per call (see F048-10). Free plan voice is capped at 10 minutes per calendar month (voiceMinutesPerMonth: 10), and a session started on that allowance keeps it for its whole length; this is why the 'Continue in text' row exists (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1255-1257; apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-65). Typing and the typed model turn follow normal chat limits, not voice minutes [inferred]. The CLI records at most 120 seconds and ignores clips under 300 ms (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:33-39).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Live voice on web is blocked for chats on a local model or non-managed provider; those chats keep the text composer (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:5907-5911). The web gate requires that the chat's model use a managed provider mode (ManagedGateway or ManagedNative) (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:189-193). The route also refuses with 403 'model_may_train' when a user's stored chats may train models, the live or backend model does not keep inputs out of training, and the chat holds Google user data (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:320-340).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Web live voice needs a chat on a managed provider route (not necessarily OpenAI). The live model comes from the voice_live slot, and the backend model from the plan's backend slot (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:189-193). CLI transcription may use OpenAI, AGI managed or local whisper.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web: no voice entry in a Local chat; typing continues as normal. iPhone: 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-18). CLI Local privacy mode: cloud transcription is refused unless AGIWORKFORCE_VOICE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1; a local whisper binary works with no egress (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:62-72, 481-483).

features.summary: On web and desktop (hosted web), 'Customize' makes your own editable copy of an installed, turned-on plugin's skills, then turns the original off. 'Edit plugin' changes the copy. In chat, asking to build a plugin or skill can show a draft card with a Save button. Copy and edit are the only fork path found.

purpose.what_it_does: Copies the skills and companion files of an installed plugin into a new personal plugin that keeps the original's name and has key '<key>-custom', stored under an authored source named '<name> (custom)'; installs and enables it, turns the original off, and opens the editor. features.summary: A run can pause on several tool calls at once. The server only resumes when it gets one decision for every pending call, then resumes once. Tasks screens apply one Approve or Deny to all calls. The CLI has Allow All and Deny All for the rest of a turn.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person answer all pending calls of one run together so the run resumes a single time (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1964-1972).
purpose.why_it_exists: A model can ask for several tools in one step; asking one by one would need many resumes, and the server refuses a partial answer.
purpose.who_uses_it: People managing background work on Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code and the CLI.
problems_solved: No half-answered step: the server rejects a decision set that does not match the pending set (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1964).
No repeated prompts for the rest of a CLI turn (apps/cli/src/tui/approval_broker.rs:325-326).
use_cases: Tasks page: a run waits on three calls; the person presses Approve once.
Mobile run detail: Reject all pending calls.
CLI: press t (Allow All) to allow the rest of the turn except high-risk calls.
VS Code: command 'Approve and continue' on a cloud task.

where_to_find_it: Web, Desktop (hosted web app) and shared Tasks page: 'Waiting for your approval' card, buttons 'Approve' and 'Deny' (TasksPage.tsx:891-900).
Mobile: Tasks screen run detail sheet with approve and reject, store action resolveApproval (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/store.ts:311, apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/CloudTasksScreen.tsx:840).
CLI: 'd Deny All' and 't Allow All' buttons (approval_overlay.rs:5-21, :95-118).
VS Code: commands agi-workforce.approveCloudTask and agi-workforce.rejectCloudTask, confirmation 'Approve and continue' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudRunApproval.ts:38-41).

Web chat card: calls of one step are answered one by one on their cards; the request is sent when the last one is decided (useChatStream.ts:~5565-5585). Any call left undecided is sent as 'rejected' (useChatStream.ts:~5592).
prerequisites: A signed-in account with a paused cloud run.
For CLI: an interactive terminal.
screens_and_controls: The list of calls with a short preview of each (argsPreview) (TasksPage.tsx:892-896).
Optional guidance box 'Add guidance to steer this run (optional)' (TasksPage.tsx, after line 891).
journey: 1. Open Tasks and filter to runs that need you.
2. Read the list of pending calls.
3. Press Approve or Deny; one decision is applied to every call (TasksPage.tsx:471-480).
4. The list reloads; the run shows running or done.
feedback_and_outputs: The Approve button shows pending while sending (TasksPage.tsx:901).
On a race: 'Another device already answered this approval.' (TasksPage.tsx:178).
VS Code: 'your decision could not be sent, another device already answered this one' (cloudRunApproval.ts:30-32, :157).
settings: none specific; CLI Allow All respects the high-risk exception in code (approval_broker.rs:196).

working: Server accepts 1 to 32 decisions and demands the exact pending set (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1920-1972; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-resume.ts:34).

The Tasks page sends the same decision for every call in the run (TasksPage.tsx:476-480); Mobile does the same (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/store.ts:326-332); VS Code does the same (cloudRunApproval.ts:22-26).

Web and Mobile chat cards collect one decision per call and send the request once decisions.size equals calls.length (useChatStream.ts:~5565-5585; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:4420). The send loop treats any undecided call as 'rejected' (useChatStream.ts:~5592).
A saved Deny in the permission store overrides an approval in the batch (approve/route.ts:516-523).

An approved call whose tool is no longer offered gets 'Tool X is not available and was not executed.' and the batch continues; rejected calls get the denied message (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:6575-6600).
CLI broker supports deny_all and allow_all for a turn (approval_broker.rs:325-326, :401, :437); Allow All excludes high-risk and some kinds (approval_broker.rs:196-215).
CLI Deny All resolves requests as Cancel, not as a per-call denial, and it latches for the rest of the turn because the broker is per-turn and discarded at turn end (approval_broker.rs:429-445, 325).
incomplete: Tasks, Mobile and VS Code cannot mix decisions in one answer (all approve or all reject); mixed decisions are possible only on chat cards (TasksPage.tsx:476, useChatStream.ts:~5565-5585).
Chrome: brief says unverified; per-call buttons exist (bubbles.ts:1004) but no batch control was found.

not_available: Batch control in the Chrome side panel was not found.

features.summary: Per-agent memory, routines, a private workspace and a responsibility list. The brief calls all four missing. The code has two partial pieces on web and mobile Cloud: routines that run as an agent (Deployments), and up to 20 reference files per agent. No per-agent memory, no private computer and no responsibility list were found.

purpose.what_it_does: Would give each agent its own memory, scheduled routines, a workspace for its files and a list of what it owns. Today Cloud agents can own scheduled routines and carry reference files; nothing else of the four is built.
purpose.why_it_exists: S61.06, S61.07, S61.10 and S61.12 describe agents that persist over time like a team member (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and mobile Cloud users who want an agent that runs on a schedule or reads fixed files; future users of persistent agents.
problems_solved: Running the same agent on a schedule without opening a chat.
Giving an agent reference material once instead of attaching it each chat.
use_cases: Add a weekly routine that runs a research agent every Monday.
Upload a style guide as Knowledge so a writing agent always has it.
See the agent's recent chats and routines under Activity.

CLI: none. Chrome, VS Code, Tauri desktop: none found.

working: Cloud agent knowledge files: add, list, remove; stored with content and hash; injected into every turn as agent_file blocks treated as material, not instructions (custom-agent-service.ts:755-826; agent-turn-config.ts:111-137).

Cloud routines as an agent: scheduled_tasks has an agent_id column; the schedule service validates the agent; the scheduled executor loads the agent turn config and applies its model, web, code and connector settings (apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:143-148; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:922-924, 1006; apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:918-958).

A routine as an agent also applies the agent's web search, code execution, connector selection and allowed or blocked web domains, not only its model (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~938-960).

Routine runs are gated by evaluateManagedComputeAccess for 'schedules' with the user's entitlement plan, and are skipped with 'Scheduled execution skipped: ...' when denied (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~889-912).

Per-agent dailyTurnLimit and monthlyCreditLimit (owner-set) are enforced on routine runs and on chat turns, with the messages 'reached its limit of N messages a day' and 'used the N credits its owner allows each month' (apps/web/lib/agents/agent-turn-config.ts:78-95).

Pausing or retiring an agent stops its routines (AgentManagePanel.tsx:208-216 dialog text; scheduled-agent-executor.ts:921 throws ScheduledAgentUnavailableError) [inferred for pause].

Activity lists chats and routines; it is not a list of responsibilities the agent owns (custom-agent-service.ts:640-688).

Routine runs count against the agent's daily message limit and monthly credit limit, and are refused when either is reached; only the check made when a routine is created or edited skips the count (schedule-service.ts:922-924 passes countTurns:false; scheduled-agent-executor.ts:~899-901 uses the default countTurns:true; agent-turn-config.ts:58-95).

features.summary: Explains and handles runs that did not happen on time or failed. The Cloud sweep decides a run is missed when it starts more than two sweep intervals late and then runs it late once or skips it, as the owner chose, and the run history says so. Failed or timed-out runs retry with doubling waits. Holding runs for usage resets and repairing expired connectors are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Records why an occurrence ran late or was skipped, applies the owner's 'If A Run Is Missed' choice, retries failed or timed-out runs a chosen number of times with doubling waits, and writes an audit event for missed runs. On Electron Desktop, Local routines have their own missed-run choice and a 2 minute grace.
purpose.why_it_exists: The Cloud sweep runs about every 15 minutes, machines sleep, and models fail. People need to see what happened to an occurrence instead of guessing (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md, S63.33 to S63.35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners reading run history on any app; operators reading audit events.
problems_solved: A routine fired hours late: the history says 'Ran late: scheduled for X, started Y later.'
A stale occurrence should not run: choose skip and see 'Skipped the run scheduled for X'.
A flaky run: retries try again before the routine moves on.
A skipped run must not use up the run limit: the slot is given back.
use_cases: Morning digest that is pointless after noon: set 'Skip it and wait for the next occurrence'.
Billing report that must still happen: keep 'Run it once, late'.
Flaky external site: Retries After A Failed Run 3, first retry after 5 minutes.
Check why a routine did not run overnight in the run history.

Policy: skip finalizes the run as cancelled with {missedExecution, skipped:true}, returns the run slot; run_once continues and stores the missed details in the result; both write an audit event (schedule-service.ts:2256-2268, :2120-2138, :2156-2166).

A run resumed after approval skips both missed detection and the condition check (`if (!options.resume)`) (schedule-service.ts:2256-2257).

Retries: failed or timeout, scheduled triggers only, while retriesSpent is below retryMaxAttempts, no cap reached and the expiry not passed; delay is backoff doubled per retry, exponent capped at 10, capped at one day; a retry claims under its own key and does not spend a run (schedule-service.ts:1643-1647, :1713-1735; :1381-1382).

A reached credit cap stops retries: when a retry would otherwise fire, the cap pauses the routine instead, via isCreditCapReached in the retry predicate and the pauseForCreditCap path (schedule-service.ts:1643-1647, :2130-2250).

A run is missed when it starts more than twice the sweep interval late; run_once runs it late, skip records it and gives the run slot back; both write an audit event.

acceptance_criteria: A scheduled occurrence started more than 30 minutes after its due time (normal mode) is treated as missed; one started within 30 minutes is not.
With 'Run it once, late' the run executes and its history note reads 'Ran late: scheduled for <time>, started <duration> later.'
With 'Skip it...' no model call happens, the run shows as skipped with the skip note, and the routine's run counter is not increased by that occurrence.
Both policies create a schedule_missed_execution audit event.
With Retries After A Failed Run 2 and first retry 5 minutes, a failed run is tried again after 5 minutes, then 10 minutes, then the routine moves on; a manual run is not retried.
A retry does not reduce the Maximum Runs allowance.
Run history on Web, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome shows the same note text for the same run.
A Local routine on Electron with skip and a due time more than 2 minutes old shows state 'skipped'.

steps.what_happens: Vercel cron calls /api/cron/run-schedules every 15 minutes; in low-power mode it returns early after minute 15 of the hour.

The sweep cancels expired approvals, recovers expired leases, then claims due routines (enabled, active, next run due, not past expiry, under run limit unless retrying, owner allowed to run unattended and active in the workspace). The claim inserts a run row with an idempotency key built from the due time and retry number.

For each claim, the cap check runs; then missed detection compares now with the due time; skip policy finalizes the run as cancelled, run_once continues. A run resumed after approval skips missed detection and the condition check.
The executor runs the routine (model call to the provider); on error the status becomes failed, on timeout timeout, on outside cancel cancelled.

finalizeScheduleRun writes the run result and decides the next time: retry with doubling delay, or next occurrence, or completed/expired, or pause at cap (a reached credit cap pauses the routine instead of retrying); failed and timed-out runs queue a notification, cancelled ones do not.
Clients list runs; the shared function turns the stored missedExecution and skipped fields into the note text.
Electron Local routines: the on-device engine ticks every second and applies its own missed rule with a 120 second grace.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The missed and retry logic does not depend on a model. A retried or late run goes through normal route selection; retries of a failed provider call use the same managed path. Nothing in this feature switches model or provider on failure (no such code found in the retry branch). The on-screen text for Electron Local routines says the model may still run in the cloud, so a Local routine's model call can leave the device (LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:199).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account to read history; the sweep acts for the routine owner and skips owners whose account state forbids unattended work or who left the workspace (schedule-service.ts:1366-1368, :1317-1335).
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner reads their own runs. Workspace admin visibility of skipped work: only a server log line (schedule-service.ts:1328-1335).
access_and_usage.subscription: A run for an account without managed compute access is cancelled by the executor with a reason (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:889-915). A usage-allowance hold: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Retries 0 to 5; backoff 60 to 86,400 seconds, default 300; retry delay doubles with the exponent capped at 10 (schedule-service.ts:86-89, :1643-1647). Retries do not spend a run (schedule-service.ts:1381-1382). A reached credit cap stops retries and pauses the routine (schedule-service.ts:1643-1647, :2130-2250). Sweep batch limits are in the cron route (not detailed).

access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code for these rules.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Cloud sweep, retries and the missed policy do not apply in Local mode. Electron Local routines have a skip-or-run missed rule with a 2 minute grace, run only while the Desktop app is open, and have no retry code (a grep for 'retry' in localRoutine*.ts found nothing) (localRoutineEngine.ts:145, :511-537; LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:199, the text 'Runs while the Desktop app is open'). The same on-screen text adds that the model may still run in the cloud, so a Local routine's model call can leave the device (LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:199).
