features.summary: The signed-in chat page of the AGI Workforce web app at /chat. A person types in the composer and gets a streamed reply. A Chat | Work toggle switches to Work mode, which runs multi-step tool tasks. Work is offered only on Premium or higher; below that the toggle is hidden and the server refuses it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a person a place in the browser to chat with the assistant. It streams replies, shows tool activity, and lets the person switch the composer between Chat and Work. Work mode sends work_mode 'agiwork' plus an optional goal and plan with the message (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4663-4670).
purpose.why_it_exists: The web app is the main Cloud surface and is the product that the Desktop app shows inside its window (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). Work mode exists so paid users can hand off multi-step jobs that use tools, files and reviewable results (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:329-332; packages/contracts/types/src/interaction-modes.json:50-85).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web users. A signed-out visitor gets a limited guest chat at /chat only when there is no user, no browser session cookie, the path is a guest chat page, and the guest chat is open; any other signed-out case redirects to sign-in or session-expired (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:41-62). Work is for Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium and Enterprise accounts (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,354).
problems_solved: One place to ask questions and run tool tasks without installing anything.
Keeps paid agent work behind the plan check on the server, so hiding a button in the browser is not the only guard (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3538-3556).
Lets a person start in Work from a direct address (/agi-work) or from a project (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:5-19; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1217-1231).
use_cases: Ask a quick question in Chat mode and read the streamed answer.
Switch to Work and ask for a multi-step task such as gathering sources and producing a document.
Open /agi-work to land directly in Work mode.
Open a project and start a new chat in it, which lands an eligible account in Work.

where_to_find_it: surface:web: the address /chat (new chat) and /chat/<id> (an existing chat) (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:1-19; apps/web/app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx:12-14).

surface:web: the address /agi-work is rewritten to /chat for a signed-in browser session and opens in Work mode; the address bar keeps /agi-work (apps/web/proxy.ts:109-133; apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:5-19).
surface:web: /cowork redirects permanently to /agi-work (apps/web/next.config.ts:136).

The Chat | Work toggle sits on the composer face. Its buttons are labelled 'Chat' and 'Work' (translation keys composer.modeChat and composer.modeAgiWork) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:316-320; packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/chat.json:169,193). Hover text for Work is 'Work: multi-step tasks with tools, files, and reviewable deliverables' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:326-329).

Other apps: the area brief gives no status for desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome for this item (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/069-web-application.md S69.01). The Desktop app shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
prerequisites: Signed in, accepted the current terms, and passed the adult eligibility check, or the page redirects (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:56-58).

For Work: a plan of Premium or higher, billing policy loaded, not a free trial, the Work capability granted, and the toggle shown only when the composer has a project picker and no image or video mode is on (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066, 6171).
screens_and_controls: Composer text box and send control (ChatComposerNew.tsx).
Chat | Work segmented toggle, data-testid composer-work-mode (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6171-6208). It is disabled while a turn runs or the composer is disabled (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6184).
In Work mode an approval-mode control appears next to the toggle (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6211-6213).
Slash command /code turns on cloud code execution for one message (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3247-3265).
journey: Open /chat while signed in. The page shows the empty new-chat surface and saves nothing yet (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2356).
Type a message. For Work, press the 'Work' button first (handler ChatComposerNew.tsx:2806-2815).
Press send. If the browser is offline the send is refused with a notice (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3588-3590).
The first send creates the conversation and the address becomes /chat/<id> (WebChatPage.tsx:2679, 5792).
The reply streams in. Tool activity arrives as tool status frames and shows as running, completed or failed steps (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3470-3500).
In Work mode the server opens a durable work plan for the run when a goal is supplied (apps/web/lib/workflows/steps/work-plan-steps.ts:17-40).
feedback_and_outputs: Streamed assistant text and tool status lines (useChatStream.ts:3470-3500).
Offline notice: 'You are offline. Your draft is saved here and can be sent after you reconnect.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:717).
Other reasons the send control is shut are read out to assistive technology, for example usage limit reached, trial run out, model unavailable (ChatComposerNew.tsx:707-718).

If a Work request reaches the server on a plan below Premium, the response is HTTP 403 with code agi_work_plan_required and the message 'Work requires Premium or higher.' (request-processor.ts:1484-1500, 3538-3556; label from billing-catalog.ts:193-195).
settings: Default work mode: a stored setting defaultWorkMode sets the starting mode for a new chat when the account may use Work (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1233-1237).
Kill switch for Work, set by operators, not by the person (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/kill-switches.ts:31,40).

working: Chat page route, loading skeleton and guest or sign-in gate exist (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:41-65; apps/web/app/chat/loading.tsx).
Chat | Work toggle is built and gated by canUseAgiWork (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066, 6171-6208).
Server refuses Work below the Premium tier with code agi_work_plan_required and status 403 (request-processor.ts:1484-1500, 3538-3556).
Server also checks the Work kill switch before a Work turn (request-processor.ts:5217-5219).

Work turns are routed as the agentic task type (request-processor.ts:1040). Any turn that can enter the tool loop (Work, tools, web search or code execution) holds a 24-hour managed-usage lease; other turns hold 15 minutes (request-processor.ts:1525-1535). The 24-hour lease and the tool-loop route are not Work-only: any request with tools, web_search or code_execution gets them (request-processor.ts:1525-1535).
A new chat is not saved until the first send (WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2356).
The composer returns to Chat if the account loses the Work capability (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1226-1228).
The Work approval flag agi_work_plan_approval is sent as true whenever no plan steps are supplied (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4668-4669).
incomplete: The draft said Work needs 'a paid plan'. The code needs the Premium tier or higher; Basic is a paid plan but does not get Work (billing-catalog.ts:333-341,354).
Send failure paths were not traced end to end; the page has a chat error state and a turn failure notice (WebChatPage.tsx:6857-6862) but each cause was not followed.
Whether Work and the server plan check apply to a Local-model turn on the web page was not traced (WebChatPage.tsx:2436-2455).
disconnected_or_disabled: The capability handshake removes Work if no model in the catalog is marked agentic (capability-handshake-service.ts:101). Whether the live catalog has one is unknown.
not_available: Plain-browser Local mode: WebChatPage has a Local-model turn path (it reads useLocalModelSelection). When a local model is selected through the desktop host, the send skips the server session authority, is forced temporary, skips the free-trial limit, and is refused when it would start a conversation in a project (WebChatPage.tsx:1282-1287, 2436-2455, 2203; apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/local-model-selection.ts:15-22). The store is a plain zustand store, so the page does not show that only the desktop bridge sets it. A normal browser rarely reaches this path. [inferred]
Work for Local-only and Local + BYOK plan tiers: those tiers are not in the Work tier list (billing-catalog.ts:341,354).

established.statement: Signed-in user opens the web app in a browser, chats, and switches the composer to AGI Work for multi-step tool runs.
Work mode is offered only when the plan allows it; a free-trial account never sees it.
The server refuses Work below the Premium tier with error code agi_work_plan_required.
Interaction modes are defined in a contract: Work needs streaming, tools and agentic model abilities, per-tool approval, synced across devices, and a queued draft only when offline.
Every subscription capability on every app connects to one AGI Subscription system.
established.source: task brief for this knowledge base

acceptance_criteria: On a Free account the Chat | Work toggle is not shown.
On a Premium or higher account the toggle shows 'Chat' and 'Work' and switching to Work changes the placeholder and shows the approval control.
A direct POST of work_mode 'agiwork' for a Basic account returns 403 with code agi_work_plan_required.
Opening /chat saves no conversation until the first send; after send the address is /chat/<id>.
Offline, pressing send shows the offline notice and the draft is kept.
Opening /agi-work while signed in shows the chat page with Work selected.
inferred: Work availability should read the same entitlement on every app, so the Premium-or-higher rule is the one shared rule [inferred from billing-catalog.ts:354 being a shared contract].
proposed: [proposed] Show a short reason on the page when Work is hidden (for example 'Work needs Premium'), instead of hiding the toggle without explanation, so a free user can learn why.
[proposed] Add one test that checks the composer hides Work for Basic as well as Free.

steps.what_happens: Browser loads /chat; the layout checks identity, terms and adult eligibility, then renders the chat page.
The composer decides if Work is offered from plan, billing policy and capability, and shows the toggle.
On send the client builds the request with work_mode and goal and posts it to the managed chat endpoint. The agi_work_plan_approval flag is sent as true whenever no plan steps are supplied.
The server checks the Work plan rule (403 if below Premium), then the Work kill switch, then routes the turn as agentic.

The server opens a durable work plan when a goal is given and runs the tool loop; frames stream back. Any request with tools, web_search or code_execution, not only Work, gets the tool-loop route and the 24-hour lease.
The model call goes to the chosen provider through the managed route.

The model and provider are chosen by the managed routing slots and the person's model picker; this page names no model. The page also has a Local-model turn path: when a local model is selected through the desktop host, the send bypasses the server session authority and is forced temporary; it is refused when starting a conversation inside a project (WebChatPage.tsx:1282-1287, 2436-2455, 2203; local-model-selection.ts:15-22). Guest chat is rendered only for a visitor with no user, no browser session cookie, on a guest chat page, when the guest chat is open; any other signed-out case redirects to sign-in or session-expired (layout.tsx:41-62). Work is never available to guests; this follows from the missing sign-in and is enforced by the server, not in this file.

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Usage accounting key is chat, billing key agi_work (interaction-modes.json:75-77). Any turn that can enter the tool loop (Work, tools, web search or code execution) holds a 24-hour managed-usage lease; other turns hold 15 minutes (request-processor.ts:1525-1535).

WebChatPage has a Local-model turn path: when a local model is selected through the desktop host, the send skips the server session authority, is forced temporary, skips the free-trial limit, and is refused when it would start a conversation in a project (WebChatPage.tsx:1282-1287, 2436-2455, 2203; local-model-selection.ts:15-22). features.summary: How the AGI Mobile app moves between chats, lists and settings. Phones get a slide-out drawer plus stack pages with back gestures. Windows 1000 points wide or more get a permanent side panel. Camera and scan pages do not show the permanent panel (on a phone they keep the swipe-open overlay drawer) and the voice page turns the drawer swipe off. Phones stay in portrait. Tablets may rotate. Mobile only.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the Mobile app its frame. A drawer holds the Local/Cloud mode switch, search, new chat, destinations (projects, library, images, schedules and others), recent chats, settings. Stack pages open on top. The layout changes with the window width, and the screen orientation is locked for phones.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief asks for native patterns: a swipeable drawer plus stack routes with back gestures (S71.01), a wider tablet layout that adapts to split view (S71.25), foldable adaptation (S71.26) and landscape adaptation (S71.27). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who uses AGI Mobile on a phone or tablet, in Local mode or Cloud mode.
problems_solved: Reach chats and tools with one thumb on a phone.
Use the room on a tablet instead of a stretched phone layout.
Stop the drawer swipe from fighting the Back swipe on settings pages or the voice screen.
Keep the camera and voice pages full screen.
use_cases: Swipe from the left edge on a phone, then tap a recent chat to open it.
Open Settings and swipe from the left edge to go Back.
Use a large iPad window where the drawer stays open beside the chat.
Watch a video full screen in landscape on a phone, then return to portrait.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: the whole app shell. The menu control is the round button with accessibility label 'Open navigation drawer' (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/DrawerButton.tsx:70-95).

Mobile drawer rows: Search, 'New chat', destination rows, Recents, 'See all chats', Settings (keys drawer.newChat, search, drawer.recents, drawer.seeAllChats, settings) (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:631-912).
Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not part of this feature (brief gives a status for the mobile app only).
prerequisites: None for Local mode. The drawer lists only rows allowed in the current mode (isShownInMode) and by feature flags (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:563-573).

Some rows need Cloud mode, a signed-in account, or a plan capability: Images needs Cloud mode and a signed-in account; AGI Work tasks need Cloud mode, the plan and the granted capability (DrawerContent.tsx:337-349, 563-573).
screens_and_controls: Drawer (overlay on narrow windows, permanent panel on wide ones) with a Local/Cloud mode switch, Search, New chat, a 'More' fold, Projects, Recents list with long-press actions, 'See all chats', Settings and (only in Cloud mode, signed in, on a free plan, where native purchases are enabled) an Upgrade row (DrawerContent.tsx:323-420, 631-912).
Menu button with an unread-notification pip; on a permanent sidebar it becomes a blank slot and shows only a pip link 'Open notifications, N unread' (DrawerButton.tsx:50-95).
Settings stack: Back by edge swipe or back control.
Camera and scan pages: full window; they are drawerType 'front', so there is no permanent sidebar, but on phones the swipe-open overlay drawer is kept (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:23-28).
Voice page: always dark, drawer swipe off.
journey: Open the app. On a phone the chat shows with the drawer closed.
Swipe from the left edge (40 points on iOS, 64 on Android, drag of at least 60 on iOS or 96 on Android) or tap the menu button.
Tap a chat, a destination or Settings. The drawer closes and the page opens.
In Settings, swipe from the left edge or tap Back to return one page.
On a window 1000 points wide or more, the drawer is already open at 280 points wide and the menu button is gone.
Rotate an iPhone or an Android phone: the screen stays portrait, except while a video or a presentation viewer is open.
feedback_and_outputs: The drawer slides over the page with a scrim (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:55-70).
The active chat row is highlighted and unread chats show a dot (DrawerContent.tsx:500-560).
Unread count shows on the menu button and is read out in its label (DrawerButton.tsx:77-84).
settings: Chat list arrangement: 'In one list' or 'By project' (drawer.inOneList, drawer.byProject) stored in the settings store (DrawerContent.tsx:358-380).
The 'More' fold and the folded Projects section remember their state (DrawerContent.tsx:352-357).

working: Drawer type is 'front' (overlay) on narrow windows and 'permanent' when the window is 1000 points wide or more (280 drawer + 720 content) (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-9, 24-47; apps/mobile/src/features/shell/drawerGestures.ts:23-45).

The draft's 768 and 1024 are not the drawer switch. A window width of 768 gives size class 'tablet' and a window width of 1024 or more gives size class 'regular'. isTablet is true when the screen's larger side is 1024 or more (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts:5-6, 40-50).
Split view is detected as a window narrower than the screen by at least 8 points on a tablet-size screen (useTabletLayout.ts:9, 51).
Settings pages turn the drawer swipe off so the edge swipe means Back (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:20-22, 122).
Camera and scan are drawerType 'front' even where a sidebar is permanent, so on phones they keep the swipe-open overlay drawer. Only the voice route turns the swipe off (_layout.tsx:23-28, 130-134).
A leftover open state is closed when the window grows to the permanent width (_layout.tsx:30-41).

Phones are locked to portrait at app start by lockPhonePortrait (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:122, 129; apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:23-25). A phone is any non-iPad iOS device or an Android device whose smaller side is under 600 dp (useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:11-16).

Only the video player and the presentation deck viewer free rotation while open (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/VideoPlayerModal.tsx:47; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/presentation/PresentationDeckView.tsx:161).

iPad lists all four orientations and multitasking is on (supportsTablet true, requireFullScreen false) (apps/mobile/app.config.js:156-186). A native Android plugin lets screens with smallest width 600 dp or more rotate and re-decides when the size changes (apps/mobile/native/android/withAGITabletOrientation.cjs:14-34).

Message list and composer keep a reading column up to 720 points wide on large windows (apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts:3-25; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.tsx:367-370).
The drawer shows only DRAWER_RECENT_LIMIT recent chats (pinned first) and at most 6 projects in Cloud mode [apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:446-470, 481-493].
incomplete: Landscape on phones: the brief wants the chat re-laid out in landscape (S71.27) but the code locks phones to portrait. Only two viewers rotate. (apps/mobile/app.config.js:158; useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:23-52)

Foldables: only window-size changes are handled, through the Android orientation plugin and the width-based layout. No hinge or fold event code was found. (apps/mobile/native/android/withAGITabletOrientation.cjs; search for fold/hinge in apps/mobile returned only a test case name)
disconnected_or_disabled: The Upgrade row in the drawer shows only in Cloud mode, signed in, on a free plan tier, and when storePurchases.json sets nativePurchases true (NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE). FEATURES.billing is not part of that check, and this page does not say what the JSON value is. (DrawerContent.tsx:396-402, 910-915; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts:3)
Companion pages are registered as drawer screens but FEATURES.companion is false. (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16; _layout.tsx:110-114)
not_available: Hinge-aware layout on any app.
Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: not applicable to this feature.

established.statement: The phone app navigates with native patterns: a swipeable drawer plus stack routes with back gestures.
On tablets the app uses a wider layout (persistent drawer, multi-column grids) and adapts to split view.
On foldables the layout adapts when the device folds or unfolds, ideally around the hinge. The brief status is not applicable anywhere.
Rotating the phone to landscape re-lays out the chat usefully.
The design contract names breakpoints: compact phone, phone, tablet, narrow desktop, desktop, wide desktop.

acceptance_criteria: On a phone, a swipe from the left edge opens the drawer and a tap on a recent chat opens it and closes the drawer.
On Settings pages the edge swipe goes Back and does not open the drawer.
With a window 1000 points wide or more the drawer is permanent and the menu button is not shown. Narrowing the window below 1000 closes any stale open state and the overlay drawer works.
Opening camera or scan shows no permanent sidebar (on a phone the swipe-open overlay drawer remains); opening voice shows no drawer and voice does not react to an edge swipe.
An iPhone and a small Android phone stay in portrait when turned; an iPad and an Android tablet rotate.
Opening a video or a presentation on a phone allows landscape and closing it returns to portrait.
inferred: The brief status 'done' for S71.27 conflicts with the portrait lock, so the status is either stale or means tablets only. [inferred]
A tablet in portrait between 768 and 999 points gets the overlay drawer, not a permanent one. [inferred from useResponsiveLayout.ts:24-47]
proposed: [proposed] Decide and record whether phone landscape is a product requirement. If yes, unlock rotation for the chat and re-lay out the composer. If no, change S71.27 to match the code.
[proposed] Add a posture or hinge signal for foldables only if a target device needs it.

features.summary: Main chat of the AGI Workforce VS Code extension. It lives in the AGI Code activity-bar view or in an editor tab titled AGI Chat. It sends turns to a local developer runtime on the machine and shows loading, setup-needed, trust and error states with retry. Only the VS Code app has it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the VS Code extension a graphical chat. A person types a request, the extension starts a turn on a local runtime (the AGI CLI run as an app server) for the open folder, and the reply streams back into the panel. The same chat can sit in the side panel or open as a tab beside code. It also shows what the runtime is doing: checking, needing setup, waiting for a folder, or blocked by workspace trust.
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers want to talk to the assistant without leaving the editor, with the code and the folder they already have open. The brief requires a sidebar chat, an editor-adjacent chat and clear loading, setup-needed and error states with retry (brief S73.01, S73.02, S73.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the AGI Workforce VS Code extension. Testers of the extension. Not available in Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI or Chrome as this feature.
problems_solved: No need to switch to a browser or terminal to ask about code.
A setup problem (no CLI, no folder, untrusted folder) is shown as a state with a button instead of a silent failure.
A failed turn gets an error category and a retry when resending could work.
use_cases: Open the AGI Code view and ask how a function works.
Open the chat in an editor tab beside the file being changed.
Open a folder that is not trusted yet and be told to trust it before chat can start.
Hit a rate limit or provider error and press retry.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the AGI Code view; VS Code resolves the webview provider.

Host probes the local runtime for the active workspace folder and posts runtimeStatus to the webview. The runtime is spawned with --workspace-consent (folder and consent time), optionally --no-memory when memory is disabled, and optionally --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions.
Person sends text; webview posts sendMessage; host calls _handleSendMessage then runtime.startTurn with cwd and inputs.

The runtime sends the prompt to the selected model. For an on-device model this stays on the machine; for own-key it goes to that provider; for Managed Cloud to AGI infrastructure (picker descriptions).

steps.what_happens: Reply events stream back and are posted to the webview; on failure errorPresentation maps the error.
Stop posts cancel and interrupts the active turn.

features.summary: Lets a person attach pictures and PDFs to chat. The catalog records which models read pictures and PDFs, how many pictures one request may carry, and which detail levels are accepted. Apps warn early; the server refuses a picture turn for a model that cannot read pictures instead of rerouting.

purpose.what_it_does: Checks every picture or PDF turn against the chosen model: picture ability, picture count, detail level and native PDF handling. Auto routing sends picture turns to vision models.
purpose.why_it_exists: Providers reject a request that carries media the model cannot read. Checking against the catalog gives a clear message before money or time is spent.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone attaching photos or PDFs on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, Chrome and VS Code; API developers sending image_url parts.
problems_solved: A picture sent to a text-only model is refused with a clear message.
Too many pictures are caught before sending.
A PDF goes native only where the model and route accept it; otherwise it is turned into text.
A detail value the model does not accept is refused.
use_cases: A user photographs a receipt and asks a question on Mobile.
A user attaches a PDF on Web and the model reads it natively.
A CLI user attaches a screenshot and is told to switch to a vision model.
A developer sends image_url parts with detail low or high to the API.

Picture count limit: the model row wins, else the route's harness limit (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/media-input.ts:60-66); refusal too_many_images (request-processor.ts:5128-5144). The count check is skipped when the limit is null (request-processor.ts:5128-5129).

established.statement: The registry records image input per model; the product shows it and refuses or reroutes image turns to models that cannot read images (S76.03).
The registry records how many images a model accepts in one request and requests are checked against it (S76.04).
The registry records which models support high-detail inspection and the product requests high detail where supported (S76.05).
The registry records native PDF input per model and PDFs go natively to models that accept them (S76.06).
Web and desktop, mobile and the CLI must not silently route Local content to cloud; a Local-to-BYOK move is an explicit fork.

With Auto and a picture attached, the answering model has image input.
Attach a PDF to a model that lists pdf input: the PDF is sent natively; to one that does not, its text is sent instead.
On Mobile attach more pictures than the model limit: send is refused with the 'can read up to N images' message.

The server refuses on missing vision, count or detail (skipped for uncatalogued models and when the count limit is null); otherwise it decides native PDF versus text.
The provider adapter maps image parts and detail to the provider format and the provider answers.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Image and PDF ability comes from the catalog row; the route's harness sets default limits. Provider adapters translate parts. Own-key (BYOK) and Local paths in the CLI keep PDFs native only when the model flag allows (agent/chat.rs:763-766); in Managed privacy mode the CLI does not keep PDFs native (same lines), and uploads files to AGI Cloud (agent/chat.rs:3756-3775).

access_and_usage.account: Cloud turns need sign-in. Local mobile turns with images need no account for the image check itself.
access_and_usage.permissions: Picture URLs are checked by an egress policy ('image_url blocked by egress policy', request-processor.ts:606-612).
access_and_usage.subscription: Attachment byte limits depend on the plan on Web (ChatComposerNew.tsx:949-951) and Mobile (attachmentValidation.ts:34-48). Free promotional models may accept images only or text only (model-compatibility.ts:128; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1549, 5434-5445).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Picture count per request from model or route (media-input.ts:60-66). PDF pages from model or route (media-input.ts:80-100). Request size cap MAX_CHAT_COMPLETION_REQUEST_BYTES is 2,000,000 (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-call-limits.ts:8).
access_and_usage.flags: Free-trial capability gate applies when free trial is enabled (request-processor.ts:4366); it also runs for free-region fallback and promotion turns and before the general vision check (request-processor.ts:3680-3686, 4366-4400).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs the vision flag for pictures and pdf in inputModalities for native PDF.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Harness documentMediaTypes lists the PDF media type per route; routes without it get text fallback (media-input.ts:80-100).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web with a local model: attachments are refused and the person is offered 'Switch to a cloud model' or remove (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1589, 5333-5360). Mobile Local: files up to the device ceiling, no per-message count or byte limit (attachmentValidation.ts:34-40); local model rows show 'Vision' when the on-device model reads pictures (service.ts:147). CLI: documents are uploaded to AGI Cloud only in Managed privacy mode (agent/chat.rs:3756). In other modes the PDF stays native if the model supports it, or becomes text on the device; a file already uploaded (a block with an asset_id) is replaced by the notice '[this file was uploaded to AGI Cloud and is not available in this mode]' outside Managed mode (agent/chat.rs:3725-3775).

features.summary: A workspace owner or admin can set a monthly credit limit with a mode of Off, Notify or Block. Only Block refuses members' Cloud turns once the month's spend reaches the limit. Decisions are cached for 60 seconds. A separate policy cap and a personal spend limit also exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Caps managed spend for a workspace per calendar month and optionally alerts at a percentage threshold.
purpose.why_it_exists: Finance owners need a budget ceiling (S82.31). Notify lets them watch before enforcing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins who hold the policy.manage permission; members feel the refusals.
problems_solved: Uncontrolled team spend
No early warning before a budget is hit
use_cases: Owner sets a cap, 80 percent alert and Notify to observe first.
Owner switches to Block; members' new Cloud turns stop at the cap.
Owner raises the cap and members are freed at once.
Owner removes the limit.

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted desktop: workspace console usage page /workspace/usage, card 'Monthly spend limit' (apps/web/app/workspace/usage/page.tsx; apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceUsageAnalytics.tsx:377; WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:186-198).
Second control: Settings > workspace policy, 'Monthly spend cap' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:630).
Personal limit (a different thing): Settings > Usage card 'Monthly spend limit' with 'Manage' (UsageSection.tsx:707-720).
prerequisites: Workspace membership in a Team or Enterprise workspace and the policy.manage permission to change (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:69; apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts:70-90).
The component renders nothing for a caller who cannot administer the limit (WorkspaceSpendLimit.test.tsx:133).
screens_and_controls: Usage bar and text '<spent> of <cap> used this month', '· over the limit' or '· past the N% alert' (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:196-222).
Fields 'Cap (credits)', 'Alert at' %, select 'Spend limit enforcement' with Off, Notify, Block (lines 228-270).

Help text per mode: Off 'Recorded only. Nothing acts on the cap.'; Notify 'Crossing the cap is reported, but no turn is refused.'; Block 'Managed turns stop at the cap, up to about a minute of spend late.' (lines 76-80).
Buttons 'Set limit' or 'Update limit', and 'Remove limit' (lines 291-322).
journey: Open the workspace usage page.
Enter a cap in credits, an alert percent and a mode.
If choosing Block when it was not Block, read the inline notice that new turns will be declined (line 278-289).
Click 'Set limit' or 'Update limit'.
To remove, click 'Remove limit' and confirm the dialog 'Remove the workspace spend limit?'.
A member over the cap sees the refusal message.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal text: 'This workspace has reached its monthly spend limit. An owner or admin can raise it, or wait until the limit resets at the start of next month.' (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:187-190).
Policy-cap refusal uses the policy's reason with code organization_spend_cap_reached and status 402 (managed-usage-request-service.ts:399).
Save errors appear as an alert next to the buttons (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:325-335).
settings: Monthly cap (credits), enforcement (off/notify/block), alert threshold percent (spend-limit route PutSchema, lines 40-46).

working: Limit CRUD: GET (state), PUT (upsert) and DELETE. PUT and DELETE check CSRF, rate limit and policy.manage. PUT audits admin_policy_changed with severity critical whenever the saved mode is block (not only when switching to block), otherwise warning. DELETE audits a warning only when a row existed. GET is rate limited and membership checked only and writes no audit event (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:50-175; PUT/DELETE audit at lines 98-156).

Enforcement: evaluateSpendLimit allows unless configured, mode block and spend >= cap; decision cached 60 seconds; unreadable state is treated as allowed (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:53-60, 161-206). A raised cap or delete clears the cache for this server process (lines 212-214, 245-275).

Gate applied before managed work in chat completions, embeddings, audio transcription, voice live sessions, image and video generation and resume routes (callers of buildSpendLimitGateResponse in apps/web/app/api/...); the gate answers 402 with type insufficient_quota (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:511-545).
Crossing announcements via dispatchSpendAlertIfDue (spend-limit-service.ts:205-210).
Separate policy cap in the managed request path: refusal writes audit event spend_cap_exceeded and throws organization_spend_cap_reached (managed-usage-request-service.ts:338-399, 779).
Web UI with confirm dialog for removal.
Web chat voice code has client handling for both over_cap and organization_spend_cap_reached (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts; apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts).
incomplete: The confirmation dialog covers only removing the limit. Saving a change to Block shows an inline warning note, not a dialog (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:278-322). The brief says the change is confirmed by the dialog.

Only the policy-cap path writes an audit event per refused request. The Block path writes a warning log line only (managed-compute-gate.ts:527-530). The brief's line 'each refused request writes an audit event' is true only for the policy cap.
The 60-second cache is per server process (Map in memory, spend-limit-service.ts:67); across several instances enforcement lag can differ. This is read from the code, not tested [inferred].
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no controls (brief n/a). They show the refusal text only. Mobile's no-model-switch list has organization_spend_cap_reached but not over_cap, so over_cap would offer a model switch on mobile (apps/mobile/services/apiErrors.ts:99-109). How the CLI, VS Code and Chrome treat code over_cap was not established.

established.statement: An owner can set a spending cap that stops managed usage once reached.
Modes are off, notify and block; only block refuses.
Decisions are cached 60 seconds, so enforcement is eventual and may overshoot by about one window of spend.
If spend cannot be read, the request is allowed.
Product requirement: Usage settings must include a monthly spend limit.
An action a user cannot undo asks first, naming the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: With mode Block and spend at or above the cap, a member's next Cloud turn is refused with status 402 and the monthly spend limit message.
With mode Notify or Off, turns continue even above the cap.
Raising the cap frees members immediately on that server.
A member cannot see the set or remove controls.
Removing the limit shows a confirmation naming the consequence and then removes it.
Changing to Block records a critical audit event.
If the spend lookup fails, the turn is allowed and an error is logged.
inferred: Overshoot of about a minute of spend is acceptable and is stated to the admin in the UI copy [inferred from WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:79].
proposed: [proposed] Put switching to Block behind the confirmation dialog, since it starts refusing work.
[proposed] Merge the two cap mechanisms (limit table and policy cap) or document which wins.
[proposed] Write an audit event on each Block refusal.

steps.what_happens: Admin saves the limit; browser PUTs with bearer token and CSRF header.
Server checks membership, the Team or Enterprise plan and policy.manage, upserts the row, clears the cache, writes an audit event, returns the new state.

A member sends a managed request; the route calls the gate which resolves the funding organization and evaluates the limit (cache 60 s). The budget is resolved from the user's first governing organization and ignores the x-agi-organization-id header, so a member cannot escape the cap by sending 'personal'.
The month-to-date sum of completed requests for the whole organization is read with the privileged database adapter.
If blocked, the route answers 402 with the message; the client shows the refusal.

features.summary: On the phone, Settings, Permissions shows whether AGI may use the microphone and the camera, reading the answer from the operating system. If not yet asked, the person can trigger the system prompt; if denied, an Open Settings button leads to the device settings. AGI cannot change device permissions itself.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists device permissions with their current level and opens a detail screen per permission that reads the system status, offers the system request when undecided and sends the person to device Settings otherwise (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/Detail.tsx:50-107, 154-167; registry.ts:51-79).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to see and change what the app can use. The operating system owns the decision; AGI shows the truth and a path to change it.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every phone user, especially those using voice input or document scanning.
problems_solved: Voice or camera does nothing and the person does not know why.
Not knowing what is allowed.
Stale status after changing it in device Settings.
use_cases: Check the microphone is allowed before dictating.
Allow the camera so a document can be scanned.
After denying by mistake, tap Open Settings and re-enable.
Return from device Settings and see the new status.

where_to_find_it: Phone: Settings, then the 'Device' group, then 'Permissions' (also reachable from Safety & Security and Capabilities), then 'Microphone' or 'Camera'. The row sits in the Device group directly above and separate from the 'Safety & Security' row, not nested under it; the list screen title is 'Permissions' with an 'App Permissions' header (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:668-735; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/index.tsx:180-191; safety-security/index.tsx).
Other apps: not applicable; Desktop shows Microphone in its system permission rows under F086-11 (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-privacy.ts:3).
prerequisites: The phone app. No sign-in or plan requirement found in the permissions code.

iOS also lists Speech Recognition, Photos & Files, Reminders and Face ID; Notifications and Calendar on both platforms (registry.ts:251-259). Device-dependent rows (those with an isAvailable check, such as Face ID) are hidden until the device reports them available (permissions/index.tsx:25-27, 123-125, 137-150).
screens_and_controls: List row per permission: label, access level label (Never, Ask, While using, Always), accessibility text '<label> permission. Access level: <level>. Tap to manage.' (index.tsx:49; types.ts:20-25; registry.ts:276-284).

Detail: title, headline (Access Granted, Not Requested, Access Denied), description ('Used for voice input and audio recording.' or 'Used for photo capture and document scanning.'), explanation, one action button, note 'AGI can’t change device permissions for you.' (Detail.tsx:154-167, 254-322; types.ts:27-37; registry.ts:163-189).
The list screen carries a help link to https://agiworkforce.com/help?q=permissions+microphone+camera (permissions/index.tsx:20).
journey: Open Settings, Device, Permissions.
Tap Microphone or Camera.
Read the status.
If 'Not Requested', tap 'Allow Microphone' or 'Allow Camera' and answer the system prompt.

working: Status is read when the screen gains focus and again whenever the app returns to the foreground (Detail.tsx:56-84).
The list screen also re-reads every permission on focus and on app foreground return (permissions/index.tsx:117-165, AppState listener at ~161).
Microphone status uses the camera module's microphone permission calls; camera status uses its camera permission calls (registry.ts:51-59, 71-79).

features.summary: On authenticated web API requests, the server turns the verified sign-in subject into one AGI account id and then refuses the request if the account is locked, in recovery, suspended, banned, or deleted. A scheduled deletion is still allowed so the person can cancel it. Clerk is the only identity provider the code can select. The status gate is reached through assertAccountActive; the device refresh route applies the same decision separately.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps a provider sign-in (a subject string) to one AGI account id, reads the account's standing, and either lets the request through or answers 403 with a reason and a recovery path. The provider sits behind one interface so the rest of the web app never talks to Clerk directly (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts:1-53).
purpose.why_it_exists: The account must outlive the sign-in method, and a closed account must stop working everywhere at once. One check at the API layer covers Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and both extensions because they all call the same API [inferred from the shared API layer]; account standing is enforced on several separate paths, so each auth path needs tracing before claiming full coverage (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:115-120,196-216,244-282; apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:181-188).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person, indirectly. Support and security staff rely on it to make lock, suspend and delete real.
problems_solved: A suspended or erased person cannot keep using a stale session or a stale provider callback (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:179-212).
A locked person gets a path to fix it (password reset) and a suspended person gets an appeal path, instead of a bare error (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).

Swapping the identity provider needs one adapter and an environment change, not edits at each call site (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts comment on getIdentityProvider; packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:36-53).
use_cases: A suspended person opens the web app and sees a suspension notice with an Appeal link instead of their chats.
A person whose account was erased tries to sign in again through a leftover provider session and is turned away.
A person with a scheduled deletion signs in and can still open Settings to cancel the deletion.
An operator replaces the identity provider by adding an adapter in the factory switch.

where_to_find_it: No control. It runs on the server for authenticated API requests through assertAccountActive, which is also called on the cookie path (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:115-120,196-216,244-282). The device refresh route applies the same decision separately (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:181-188). Not every auth path has been traced.

The denial notice titles come from ACCOUNT_DENIAL_NOTICE: 'This account is locked' (action 'Reset your password'), 'Finish recovering this account' ('Continue recovery'), 'This account is suspended' ('Appeal this suspension'), 'This account has been deleted' ('Back to sign-in') (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:32-37).
Recovery pages named in code: /auth/reset-password and /appeal (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:27-28).
prerequisites: A verified sign-in through the hosted identity provider (the only selectable provider is 'clerk') (packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1).
An account profile row; an identity row is linked on first sign-in if the account exists (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:158-168).
screens_and_controls: No screen owns this feature. Clients show the 403 body: message, reason, recoveryPath (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:111-117).
On a device sign-in refresh the denial is returned as error 'account_unavailable' with an optional recovery_url (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts, account_unavailable branch).
journey: The person acts in any app; the app sends a request with a session cookie or bearer token.
The server verifies the token with the identity provider and resolves the subject to an account id.
The server reads the account status (cache first, database second).
If the status is locked, recovery_pending, suspended, banned or deleted the server answers 403 ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE with the reason and recovery path.
Otherwise the request proceeds; a scheduled deletion does not block it.
feedback_and_outputs: 403 with code ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE, reason one of locked, recovery, suspended, deleted, and recoveryPath (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:111-117).
503 'Unable to verify account status. Please try again shortly.' when the lookup fails twice (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:279-282).
Locked message names /auth/reset-password; suspended message cites section 11 of the Terms and says a person reviews every appeal (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:75-95).
settings: AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER selects the provider; unset means clerk; any other value throws a config error (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11-34).
ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN (1, true or on) allows requests when the status lookup fails; default is fail closed (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:269-278).

working: Subject-to-account resolution with a 5 minute key-value cache, database fallback, and an 'erased' outcome distinct from 'unknown' (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:179-212; apps/web/lib/server/request-context-cache.ts:10).

Seven stored statuses; deletion_scheduled and deleted are derived from a deletion date and an erasure tombstone, and erasure outranks everything (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:1-9, 61-66; apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:12-34).
Denial decisions for locked, recovery_pending, suspended, banned (reported as 'suspended'), deleted (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).

Status lookup is cached, tried at most twice (one retry), each try bounded to 2000 ms, and fails closed with 503 unless ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN is set (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:109,120,250-266,279-282).

The account-status cache lives 5 minutes (same constant as the identity cache) and is cleared by invalidateAccountStatusCache(userId); a lock or suspension written without that call takes up to 5 minutes to take effect (apps/web/lib/server/request-context-cache.ts:10,64-86).
An erased subject is logged as an auth failure 'erased_account' and refused (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:293-303).
An unattended-run query refuses owners whose status is a denying one, derived from the same vocabulary (apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:46-52).
incomplete: The brief says adapters cover password, social, passkey and SSO (brief S89.02). The code has one adapter only, Clerk (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:47-52; packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1). SSO connection code at apps/web/lib/server/sso/clerk-enterprise-connections.ts was not opened [unknown how it ties to the adapter].
Sign-in-completion check (accountAccessForSignIn) allows the request on any lookup error, by design, leaving the route gate as the fail-closed layer (apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:38-46).

The workspace lockdown gate in assertAccountActive fails open: a failed or slow workspace lookup is logged as 'not locked' and the request continues, while the bindOrganizationScope path (mfaGateExemptForOwner) fails closed with 503 (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:196-208, 215-242).

Account standing is enforced on several separate paths: assertAccountActive on the cookie path, and the device-token refresh route, which applies its own accountAccessDecision on owner_account_status and returns 403 account_unavailable (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:181-188,281-295). Coverage of every bearer-token or other authenticated route was not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN turns fail-closed into fail-open when set (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:269-278). Its production value is unknown.
not_available: A second identity provider: not available in the code (packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1).
Per-app behaviour: none recorded; the brief marks every app n/a (brief S89.01).

established.statement: A server-side account service maps every authenticated identity to one AGI account record and enforces account state (active, locked, pending deletion) on each request.
Authentication is delegated to identity-provider adapters (password, social, passkey, SSO) behind one server interface that verifies sessions and fetches users.
Security behaviour fails closed.
A lockout is self-service and a suspension is not; they must not share a message; a scheduled deletion stays allowed.

acceptance_criteria: A locked account gets 403 reason 'locked' with recoveryPath '/auth/reset-password' on any authenticated API route.
A suspended or banned account gets 403 reason 'suspended' with recoveryPath '/appeal'.
A deleted or erased account gets reason 'deleted' with recoveryPath null.
An account with a deletion date but status active is allowed.
When the status lookup fails twice, the request gets 503 unless ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN is set.
After erasure, a stale provider session for the old subject is refused and logged as 'erased_account'.
inferred: Because every client calls the same web API, one check protects all six apps [inferred]; Local-mode work that never calls the API is not covered by it [inferred]. Coverage of each auth path (cookie, bearer, device token) has not been traced.
A cached 'allowed' answer can outlive a new lock for the 5 minute cache window unless invalidateAccountStatusCache(userId) is called (apps/web/lib/server/request-context-cache.ts:10,64-86).
proposed: [proposed] Add a second adapter behind the factory, or reword brief S89.02 to say Clerk is the single provider, so the brief and code agree.
[proposed] Record which clients render the denial notice titles, per app, so the notice is checked on all six.

The account status is read from cache or from profiles plus tombstone, bounded to 2000 ms and retried once (two attempts in total).
A denying status throws a 403 ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE error with reason and recovery path.

features.summary: One generated catalog of models, providers, provider routes, capabilities, plan tiers, aliases and lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement). A developer edits curated JSON and runs the sync command. Web, Mobile, the extensions and the server read the compiled output through one TypeScript module; Desktop's Rust code reads a generated mirror.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds every model fact in JSON under packages/ai/model-registry/catalog, compiles it into a registry plus models.json, and exposes lookups (alias to canonical id, provider display, routes, capabilities, tier access, lifecycle) through packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:37, :54, :57; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1446).
purpose.why_it_exists: So no surface keeps its own copy of model ids, prices, capabilities or plan limits, and a model swap never needs a consumer edit (doc: AGENTS.md section 4; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1-18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and operators edit and sync it. Every app and the server read it. End users see only the result: the models in the picker, plan locks, and retirement notices.
problems_solved: Duplicated model lists drifting between apps and server.
A model id typo or retired id reaching a provider.
Plan limits defined in more than one place.
Unknown lifecycle state: whether a model is new, old, or being retired.
use_cases: A developer adds a model to the curation file, runs sync, and every picker shows it.
A model is marked deprecated with a date; routing then refuses to pick it once the date has passed.
A client sends a provider API model id or an old alias; the catalog resolves it to the canonical id.
The server checks which plan a model needs and names it in an error.

Desktop (public Electron app) shows the hosted web app, so it shows the web picker (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

User side: none for seeing the picker; plan decides which rows are locked.

Mobile shows 'Retires <date>' when a model retires within 30 days (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:7, :18).

Developer runs pnpm sync:models; compile.mjs validates against a schema and writes registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and the Rust mirror (scripts/compile.mjs:37-57).
pnpm sync:models:check and pnpm check:model-catalog fail CI if generated files or integrity drift (package.json:387, :361).

working: Compiler reads catalog JSON, validates it and writes generated registry and models.json (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:37-57, :3145).
Alias resolution: canonical ids, provider api model ids and per-provider canonicalization map to one canonical id (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1427-1452).
Provider registry: provider labels, display ids, aliases, default model, surface (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1609-1664).
Route registry: one record per provider and model with harness, trust modes, response formats and commercial status (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:143-157).
Capability registry splits intrinsic and route-dependent capability names (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:190-195).
Plan tiers: TIER_POLICIES per free, pro, max, enterprise with allowed slots and allowed provider surfaces (managed_cloud, byok, local) (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1065, :1413).

Allowed provider surfaces by tier: free is managed_cloud only (:1245); pro is managed_cloud and byok (:1281); max allows managed_cloud, byok and local (:1329); enterprise allows local as well (:1380). BYOK needs pro or above; local is limited to max and enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1245, :1281, :1329, :1380).
Token caps per month differ by tier: free null, pro 40,000,000, max 100,000,000, enterprise null (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1257, :1295, :1347, :1394).

Lifecycle: 11 stages from discovered to removed, with named shortcuts (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/lifecycle-stages.mjs:12-49); deprecation date check (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1181); retired records keep identity and replacement (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1469-1500).

Routing enforces lifecycle: a deprecated model, or one past its deprecation date, is not eligible (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1356-1358); the server passes the past-date set into every managed routing request (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:109).
Which generation of a model family is live is owned by model-families.json; promote or roll back with models:families scripts (doc: AGENTS.md section 4; package.json:394-396).
incomplete: Successor handling is a notice only. A pinned retired or deprecated model is refused, not swapped for its replacement (packages/ai/routing/src/__tests__/retired-model-selection.test.ts:23-30). The replacement is shown only on Mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:30); web and other apps: unknown.

Brief item S91.06 says lifecycle is 'enforced'; the code enforces eligibility in routing, but the stage value itself is only recorded in the registry. Whether any consumer other than the compiler and tools reads the stage: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief line numbers for S91.01 (model-catalog.ts:1367) and S91.05 (:1340) no longer match; the code is at :1121 and :1427-1446. The brief is stale on this point.
not_available: Batch or deferred inference is a separate brief item (S91.30), outside this feature.
Own-key (BYOK) and local trust modes are in the catalog (harness trust modes), but the compiled route data is shared; whether each app uses them: see F091-02 and unknowns.

established.statement: One compiled model registry is the source every surface and the server read for model facts.
A provider registry records each provider (display, defaults, governance, hosts).
A provider-route registry records every model x provider route with harness, trust modes, retention, cache class and price.
A capability registry records intrinsic and route-dependent capabilities per model.
Model aliases resolve to canonical model ids everywhere.
Model lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement, replacement) is managed and enforced.
The model catalog is generated and is the only place a model id may be a literal; never hand-edit models.json.
AGI never claims a model or provider can do something if capability metadata does not prove it.

acceptance_criteria: After editing the curation file and running pnpm sync:models, pnpm sync:models:check passes and models.json changed only through the generator.
Resolving a provider api model id, an alias and a canonical id returns the same canonical id.
A model whose deprecation date is in the past is not selected by Auto and is refused when pinned, on every plan and trust mode.
The picker shows a plan lock for a model the plan does not include, using the tier policy from the catalog.
A message stored with a retired model id still shows a model name.
An inline model id literal in app code fails pnpm check:model-id-literals.
inferred: [inferred] The picker hides or locks models by the same tier policy the server uses, because both read model-catalog.ts.
[inferred] A retired model should show a successor on every app, as Mobile does; only Mobile is evidenced.
proposed: [proposed] Show the retirement notice and replacement on web and extensions, the way Mobile does.
[proposed] Add a test that every surface picker reads the retirement label from one shared helper.

The mobile local picker offers Auto on every plan because on-device routing costs nothing (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:316-325). features.summary: The indexer cuts project files, library files, chats, artifacts, reports and developer sessions into overlapping text chunks and stores them with a text-search column and, when possible, an embedding vector. Embedding is a metered call. If it fails, chunks stay keyword-searchable and indexing retries with growing delays. A cron sweep every ten minutes starts the work.

purpose.what_it_does: Claims a pending retrieval document, loads its source text, cuts it into 1,400-character windows with 200 overlap (max 400 chunks), embeds the chunks in metered batches, writes chunks and settles the document status in one transaction (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-index-service.ts:417-436,479-518,658-785; packages/platform/data-layer/src/search/chunk.ts:10-15).
purpose.why_it_exists: Search by meaning and by keyword needs a prepared copy of the content; 0202 says nothing was embedded before so there was no semantic or hybrid retrieval on managed cloud (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:6-10).

Duplicate work: unchanged text costs nothing (lines 700-717).

steps.what_happens: A trigger on the source table enqueues or marks stale a retrieval document.

Cron reserves due documents (holds them 15 minutes) and starts index workflows. Only the cron sweep and the reindex route start indexing. A document is dispatch-held for 15 minutes (DISPATCH_HOLD_MINUTES) at reservation, separate from the 10-minute lease, so a failed workflow start waits up to 15 minutes, not 10, for retry.

The step claims the document, loads source text, windows it and hashes it. The workflow step runs under createClaimedUserScopedDb with the owner's userId and organizationId, so organization and workspace policy applies to indexing, not just individual accounts.
Embedding call reserves usage, calls the gateway or Google embeddings, settles the cost.
One transaction settles the document and rewrites chunks.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The embedding model comes from routing slot embedding_default; routes must use the vercel_gateway/embeddings or google/embeddings harness and a credentialed managed provider (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:48,68-73,96-115). Providers: provider:vercel-gateway, provider:google. Google-user-data text is limited to providers that keep inputs out of training (lines 215-220). More generally, a no-training provider filter is applied when the user opted out of side-call training, embedding input is truncated per text (MAX_EMBEDDING_INPUT_CHARS) and each call is capped at MAX_EMBEDDING_INPUTS (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:210-220).

access_and_usage.account: Signed in owner; the workflow runs under a user-scoped database (index-retrieval-document.ts:36-41).

access_and_usage.subscription: Free plan passes the subscription check for managed compute (managed-compute-access.ts:74), but workspace policy (managed-compute-access.ts:191) can still refuse. Free has a 200 queries/day cap for query embeddings only; document embedding has no daily cap in this code. Paid plans: no cap in this rule (billing-catalog.ts:737-739). Reservation and entitlement can still refuse: code not_entitled or billing_refused.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Max 400 chunks, 200,000 source characters, 400 chat messages, 50 documents per sweep, 5 attempts (retrieval-index-service.ts:39-48). Embedding input is truncated per text (MAX_EMBEDDING_INPUT_CHARS) and each call is capped at MAX_EMBEDDING_INPUTS (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:210-220). A quota read failure lets the call through (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:391-405).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Vector width fixed at 1536; a different width needs a migration and full re-index (types.ts:12-17; 0202:130).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Needs a managed embedding provider; none means keyword only with message 'Semantic indexing is not configured on this deployment; keyword search still works.'
access_and_usage.local_mode: No Local indexing exists. Local-mode content is not indexed by this feature; chat and project content saved to Cloud is indexed and embedded on our servers, using managed compute regardless of the chat's mode.

features.summary: Keeps older versions of files (project knowledge files, published artifacts, and, in code only, generated files) and lets the owner of a project share it with their organisation as read-only or with named editors. Web and mobile have a sharing screen; versions have no per-file history screen found for files.

purpose.what_it_does: Two linked jobs. First, versioning: a re-uploaded project file with the same name becomes a new version and the old one is marked superseded (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-files.ts:394, :425); a published artifact keeps an append-only history that can be listed, read and restored (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:871, :971, :500; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/versions/route.ts:34); a generated file can point at the file it replaced and at the file it was made from (apps/web/lib/server/generated-file-persist.ts:95, :56). Second, sharing: a project owner or sharing manager shares a project with the organisation and sets per-person access (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:305, :405).
purpose.why_it_exists: Migration 0257 says a file had no history and no parent, a republish overwrote the earlier version, and nobody could answer where an export came from (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:2-20). Sharing exists so a team can work from one project's instructions and files while chats stay private (apps/web/features/settings/sections/OrganizationSharingSection.tsx:196).
purpose.who_uses_it: Project owners, organisation owners and admins, members with the share right, invited editors, and anyone who republishes an artifact. [inferred] from the permission checks (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:91).
problems_solved: A newer upload of a same-named project file no longer destroys the old row; it is superseded, not deleted (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:197-218).
Raising a project's default access can never silently give the whole organisation edit rights; edit is a per-member grant (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:213-217).
A member later moved to Viewer cannot keep using an old edit grant, because the right is checked again on every read (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:264-266).
A health space cannot be shared (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:361).

features.summary: One coding-session service, the AGI CLI's developer-session host, owns coding threads, turns, approvals and history. The CLI, VS Code and Desktop talk to it over a shared JSON protocol. Cloud Code sessions are listed beside local ones but cannot take turns there. Mobile reaches it only through the relay [inferred].

purpose.what_it_does: Holds the state of coding sessions (called threads) in one place: the list of threads, each thread's messages, status, working folder, branch, worktree, trust mode and the single client allowed to write to it. Clients start turns, stream output, steer, interrupt, approve actions and resume threads through one wire protocol. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:2341, crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:1)
purpose.why_it_exists: So that every coding surface shows the same session instead of each keeping a private copy. The protocol file says it is shared by AGI CLI and AGI for VS Code, and v8 exists so an editor client rides the CLI instead of keeping a second copy of each surface. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:1, :32-35)
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the AGI CLI, the AGI VS Code extension and the Desktop app's coding view. Engineers building clients against the protocol. The mobile phone reaches desktop coding sessions through the relay (see F099-99).
problems_solved: Two clients no longer drift apart on the same session: one writer lease decides who may send turns, and others can take over or release it (thread/writer/takeover, thread/writer/release).
A session started in one app can be resumed, forked, searched, archived, pinned or rewound from another.
Cloud Code sessions for the same GitHub repository show up in the local thread list (in Managed privacy mode only), so the person sees all work for a repository in one place.
use_cases: Start a coding thread in the CLI, then reopen it in the VS Code sidebar and continue it.
Open Desktop's coding view, which starts the AGI CLI as its runtime and lists the saved sessions for a folder.
Interrupt a running turn, answer an approval request, then resume after restart.
See a cloud Code session next to local threads and be told to continue it on the web or with agi code teleport.

where_to_find_it: CLI: the command agi app-server (transport stdio, ws, or a bind address such as 127.0.0.1:8788). The ordinary agi chat and TUI use the same host [inferred]. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6700-6760, :870)

Desktop (Electron): Developer session service starts the AGI CLI as the runtime; the binary is chosen from a path the user confirmed in Settings, a bundled copy, or the installed one. (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:373-380)

VS Code: the sidebar chat and chat participant ride the CLI host. Exact visible labels not opened: unknown. (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/chat-participant/chatParticipant.ts)
Web, Mobile, Chrome: no direct use found. Web only receives cloud sessions; mobile uses the relay. [inferred]
prerequisites: The AGI CLI binary must be present and new enough; Desktop refuses a runtime below its minimum version and says to update the AGI CLI or point Settings at a current binary. (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:1322-1356)
A WebSocket server needs the environment variable AGI_APP_SERVER_TOKEN, otherwise it refuses to start. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6727-6737)

Cloud threads are listed only when the account privacy mode is Managed, the user is signed in (agi login), and the git origin remote is a GitHub repository. In Local or BYOK mode the list is empty by design (trust boundary). (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:34-41, :84-97; apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-373)
screens_and_controls: The protocol exposes thread list, read, resume, fork, compact, handoff, archive, pin, search, checkpoints, rewind, plan, delete, reconnect and writer takeover/release methods. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:57-85)

Turn methods: turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt, with notifications turn/started, output_delta, model, completed, failed, interrupted, agent_event, childTask. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:100-116)
Approval round trip: approval/requested and approval/respond; question round trip: userInput/requested and userInput/respond. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:122-126)
Visible control labels in each client: unknown, not opened.
journey: 1. A client starts the host (agi app-server) or Desktop spawns the CLI as a child process.

2. The client sends initialize with its protocol version and gets the server's version and capabilities; an unsupported version is refused with code -32005. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:36-44)
3. The client sends thread/start (or thread/list then thread/resume).
4. The client sends turn/start with text, image, skill or mention inputs; the host bounds the count and size of items. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1650-1700)
5. The host streams turn/output_delta and turn/agent_event; approvals are requested with approval/requested.
6. The turn ends with turn/completed, turn/failed or turn/interrupted.
feedback_and_outputs: Thread summaries carry title, model, working folder, provider, trust mode, status, pinned flag, git branch, worktree root, client, repository and writer. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1615-1640)
Cloud threads carry the id prefix cloud: and provider managed_cloud with trust mode managed. (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:13, :47-60)
A turn sent to a cloud thread is refused with: This is a cloud Code session. Continue it on the web, or bring it here with agi code teleport. (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:22-26)
The refusal of cloud threads covers thread resume and turn steer as well as turn start. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:2948, 4893)
settings: AGI_APP_SERVER_TOKEN: owner token for WebSocket. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6727)
AGI_APP_SERVER_READ_ONLY_TOKEN with --allow-query-token: a separate read-only credential for URLs. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6737-6750)
Default listen address 127.0.0.1:8788; AGI_CLI_SERVER_ADDR is only a fallback used when the listen argument does not parse as a SocketAddr. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6710-6722)
Allowed origins and allow-public-listen options in WebSocketSecurity. (crates/agiworkforce-app-server/src/lib.rs:39-48)
Desktop Settings: confirmed path to the AGI CLI binary. (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:368-376)

working: Host implementation DeveloperSessionHost for the CLI exists and is large (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:2341; file is 14315 lines).

Stdio and authenticated WebSocket transports exist; the WebSocket needs a non-empty token, rejects a read-only token equal to the owner token, and accepts the owner token only in a header. (crates/agiworkforce-app-server/src/lib.rs:51-76, :138-160)
Protocol version 8 with 7 still answered; legacy clients without a version get 7. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:32-45)

Cloud Code sessions for the repository are listed as threads and readable, in Managed privacy mode only (CloudClient::admit refuses Local and BYOK sessions before any network request); list failure returns an empty list. (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:64-110; apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:366-373)
Writer lease: one process writer identity is created at host construction; tests assert thread/writer_changed notifications. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:112, :766, :12794-12833)
Checkpoints and rewind are served by the host (see F099-99 S99.14).
incomplete: Cloud threads are read-only here: no turns (the refusal also covers thread resume and turn steer). (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:22-26; apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:2948, 4893)
Visible labels and exact behaviour of VS Code and Desktop screens against the host were not opened: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief line reference apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1629 points into thread_summary construction; it matches the shared-session summary. Brief reference developer_session.rs:509 lands in AppServerRequest/Response types, not a session-state type. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:495-545)
not_available: Web, Chrome and Mobile do not talk to this host directly: no direct caller found in the files opened. [inferred]
Cloud-session turns cannot run through the local host. (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:22-26)

established.statement: One coding-session service owns session state for every client. Status in the brief: platform done.
The wire protocol is stable and shared by the CLI and VS Code; every v8 method is additive.
Local, own-key and managed cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local session to another boundary.

acceptance_criteria: A thread started through the host from one client appears in thread/list from a second client for the same folder.
Only the writer-lease holder can send turn/start; another client must take over or release first, and thread/writer_changed is emitted.
A client announcing an unsupported protocol version is refused at initialize with error code -32005.
A WebSocket server started without AGI_APP_SERVER_TOKEN does not start.

A cloud thread (id prefix cloud:) appears in the list only when the account privacy mode is Managed, the user is signed in and the repository matches, and turn/start on it is refused with the continue-on-web message. In Local or BYOK mode no cloud threads are listed or read. (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:366-373)
A turn with more input items than the limit is rejected with an invalid-request error.
inferred: Trust mode (local, byok, managed) shown on every thread summary is the visible provider label AGENTS.md requires. [inferred] (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1625-1630)
proposed: [proposed] Publish the protocol as a documented page generated from the method constants so client authors do not read Rust.
[proposed] Let Web or mobile attach to the same host through the relay with a documented capability list.

steps.what_happens: Client starts or spawns the CLI app-server (stdio, or WebSocket on loopback with a token).
initialize handshake checks protocol and runtime version.

thread/list reads saved local sessions from the CLI session store and merges cloud sessions for the repository. The cloud half of the merge calls our servers only in Managed privacy mode (admit check); in Local or BYOK mode it is skipped.

turn/start sends the user input to the agent session, which calls the model provider chosen by the session's privacy mode (local, own key or managed). The provider call path itself was not opened: unknown.
Output and approval events stream back as notifications; the client answers approval/respond.
