features.summary: Cloud code runs in an isolated remote sandbox, but only when the server cutover flag AGI_E2B_EXECUTION is 1, a sandbox key and a compute price are set, and the plan includes AGI Code (Basic or above). A cloud browser and a cloud virtual computer do not exist; the cloud browser is declared unavailable.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides managed isolated sandboxes where the model runs code and where coding sessions run, billed by compute seconds. It also records that a cloud browser and a cloud computer are not built.
purpose.why_it_exists: Running untrusted code needs isolation, metering and limits. Users without a local setup still want code execution in the cloud.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid users of AGI Code on the web and users whose chat uses the code-execution tool; operators who enable the sandbox.
problems_solved: Running generated code safely away from the user's machine.
Charging for sandbox seconds and refusing when no price exists.
Keeping credentials out of the sandbox (egress proxy rules).
use_cases: A Basic user opens a Code session on the web and runs a repo task.
A chat turn runs a Python snippet in the sandbox when the execution tool is on.
On a deployment where the flag is off, the code session is refused with 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment. Use the desktop app for local code.'
A user asking the agent to drive a cloud browser gets the built-in browser or the user's own Chrome instead.

where_to_find_it: Web: the Code workspace at /code and /code/[sessionId] (apps/web/app/code/[sessionId]/page.tsx); '/code/computer' titled 'Your computer · Code' sends tasks to the user's own computer, not a cloud computer (apps/web/app/code/computer/page.tsx).
Desktop: coding sessions run locally (see F102-05, F102-06).
Visible entry label on the web nav: unknown.
prerequisites: Signed-in account.

A plan that includes AGI Code: sandbox count above 0 and a coding-agent daily budget above 0 (billing-catalog.ts:836-839 planIncludesAgiCode); Free has 2 sandboxes but budget 0, so it does not include Code. basic and above do (budget 100 cents/day for basic).
Server: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, E2B_API_KEY set and a priced compute rate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-28).
Managed compute private beta not switched off (AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA; default on, apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:55-58).
screens_and_controls: Code session creation (POST /api/code/sessions), network access choice (Isolated, Trusted hosts, Full internet) and extra hosts; full internet refused while credentials would enter the sandbox (cloud-code-session-open.ts:62-100).
journey: 1. The user starts a Code session.

2. The server checks the deployment gates, workspace policy and managed-compute access; the plan and session count are then enforced when the session is created (cloud-code-session-service.ts:1243-1245).
3. The server provisions a sandbox after reserving compute funds.
4. The user or agent runs code; output returns.
5. Idle sandboxes are reclaimed by a cron (vercel.json:54).
feedback_and_outputs: Errors: 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment. Use the desktop app for local code.'; 'Managed compute is temporarily unavailable. Use Local or BYOK in the meantime, or try again shortly.'; 'Your plan does not include managed Code sessions' (cloud-code-session-service.ts:1245).
Code-run route says 'Running code is not available on this deployment.' (chat code-runs route.ts:76).
settings: Network access, runtime id and extra hosts per session.
Server env names: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION, E2B_API_KEY, AGI_E2B_COMPUTE_MICROUSD_PER_SECOND, AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA (apps/web/.env.example:384-386, :435).

working: Gates: cutover flag is exactly '1'; provisioning is ready only with flag, key and a resolvable compute price (gate.ts:16-28). The weaker e2bExecutionEnabled is key OR flag (gate.ts:9-14).

Session open refuses when provisioning is not ready or beta is off, then checks egress rules, harness credentials, workspace code gates and managed compute access (cloud-code-session-open.ts:37-155); the plan (planIncludesAgiCode) and active-session count are enforced afterwards in createCloudCodeSession (cloud-code-session-service.ts:1243-1245).
Runtime fails closed: refuses to provision without a compute rate or funds reservation (apps/web/lib/e2b/runtime.ts:801, :886, :941).

Chat tool loop returns 'Tool ... is not available.' for execution tools when the cutover is off (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2802-2808); code-runs route answers service unavailable (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/code-runs/route.ts:76).
Idle sandbox reclaim cron and stuck code-turn reaper (vercel.json:54, :58).
Cloud code turns run as a durable workflow (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-code-turn-workflow.ts:143).
incomplete: The brief says that with the sandbox off, code runs on the provider-native interpreter; the code only shows the execution tools becoming unavailable when the cutover is off. Provider-native fallback was not found: unknown.

The chat code tool also uses a sandbox (billing-catalog.ts:834-839 comment), but the chat execution gate is only the cutover flag (tool-loop.ts:2802; code-runs/route.ts:76) with no planIncludesAgiCode check there, so which plans may use the chat execution tool is not stated by the code read (billing-catalog.ts:834-839; tool-loop.ts:2802; code-runs/route.ts:76).
disconnected_or_disabled: Sandbox is off by default: the example environment ships AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=0 (apps/web/.env.example:384).

Cloud browser is declared but disabled: BROWSER_SESSION_CAPABILITIES.cloud has available:false and the reason 'The cloud browser is not available yet. Run this in the built-in browser, or in your own Chrome through the AGI extension.' (packages/contracts/types/src/browser-session.ts:34-59).
not_available: Cloud browser runtime (S102.09) and cloud virtual-computer runtime (S102.10): missing in the ledger (audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:3171-3172; audit/missing/102-runtime-inventory.md).

The Chrome extension's cloud agent client sends a task to a cloud agent and receives tool calls back through a tool handoff (toolHandoff, apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:402, :512, :525); it is not a cloud browser. Its head (lines 1-20) only shows imports.
'/code/computer' ('Your computer · Code', 'Send a task to Cloud on your own computer') targets the user's own computer (apps/web/app/code/computer/page.tsx:5-6).

established.statement: Cloud code runs in an isolated remote sandbox. Status: partial (off unless AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1; turn it on in production).
The product runs a browser in the cloud that the agent can drive. Status: missing.
The product runs a virtual computer in the cloud that the agent can operate. Status: missing.
Sandbox compute must be priced; provisioning fails closed otherwise.

acceptance_criteria: With AGI_E2B_EXECUTION unset or 0, opening a Code session returns the 'not enabled for this deployment' error.
With flag 1 and key but no compute rate, provisioning is not ready and no sandbox is created.
A Free-plan user is refused with 'Your plan does not include managed Code sessions'.
With everything on, a Basic user can open a session and the cap on active sessions equals the plan's sandbox count.
With the flag off, a chat turn that calls an execution tool receives 'is not available'.
The cloud browser capability reports available false with the stated reason.
inferred: Local and own-key users keep code execution on their own computer (error text points to the desktop app) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Turn the sandbox on in production once pricing is configured, as the brief says.
[proposed] Decide whether the cloud browser and cloud computer are on the roadmap; the contract already reserves a 'cloud' browser session kind.

steps.what_happens: The web client asks to open a session.
The server checks deployment gates, workspace policy and spend; the plan check follows in createCloudCodeSession.
The server reserves compute funds and creates the remote sandbox through the sandbox vendor.
Code runs in the sandbox; provider credentials stay behind an egress proxy.
Results return to the server and client; sandbox seconds are settled.

features.summary: AGI Mobile stores chats in an encrypted SQLite database whose 256-bit key sits in device secure storage, and can run a small model on the phone for free without an account. Onboarding checks the device and recommends a model. The Electron desktop does not run on-device models; only the retained Tauri code checks a local model server.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps mobile data encrypted on the device and runs inference there when the phone supports it. (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:19-30,130-160; packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts)
purpose.why_it_exists: Local mode must work without an account, keep work on the device and make no hidden cloud calls. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 7.1)
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users who want private, free, offline chat.
problems_solved: Readable chats if the phone is lost (encryption).
Needing an account or payment for basic chat.
Not knowing whether a device can run a model.
use_cases: Chat on a plane with no network.
Finish onboarding and download a recommended model.
Check tokens per second in Performance settings.

Mobile Settings, Performance: 'Device Tier', 'Benchmark This Device', 'Show performance chip in chat' (performance.tsx:594,940,1077).
Desktop Tauri build (retained internal): local model server health monitor (App.tsx:746-752).
prerequisites: A supported phone; downloading a model needs storage and network; Local use needs no sign-in (doc: docs/product/requirements.md M-US-001).
The first-run age gate must be passed before onboarding (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts:38-43; ageGate.ts:1-58).
screens_and_controls: 'Recommended' badge, 'Pick a different model', 'Continue without downloading', 'Sign in to use Cloud', 'Continue' and 'Skip for now' (onboarding.tsx:648-810).
When unsupported: '<model> is unavailable on this device.', 'Browse local models', 'Continue without a local model' (onboarding.tsx:684-686,777-794).
Download screen: 'The download continues if you leave this screen.', 'Try again', 'Continue to chat' (onboarding.tsx:880-916).
journey: Open the app for the first time.
Anyone without a confirmed age is sent to the age gate before onboarding (rootRouting.ts:38-43; ageGate.ts:1-58; apps/mobile/app/(public)/age-gate.tsx).

settings: Performance chip toggle; model picker; installed models store (installedModels.ts).

working: Encrypted SQLite through expo-sqlite with SQLCipher enabled (app.config.js:454); key is 32 random bytes in hex kept in secure storage, this-device-only, id agi_sqlcipher_db_key_v1 (db.ts:23-60).
Schema migrations on open using PRAGMA user_version (db.ts:114-128).

An unreadable database (for example restored on another phone without its key) is renamed aside, not deleted, and the person is told (db.ts:76-95); removal of set-aside copies happens only inside the data export and delete flow (services/dsarExport.ts:432-452).

Three-tier local runtime selection: system model, ExecuTorch-based, and GGUF-based; capability detection by platform and RAM (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts; capabilities.ts:1-60; tier3.ts:1-60).
Multimodal local models need enough RAM and verified artifacts (multimodal.ts exports in index.ts).
Onboarding decides the tier and recommended model (onboarding.tsx:158-215).

A first-run age gate precedes onboarding: rootRouting.ts:38-43 redirects any user without a confirmed age to /age-gate, and ageGate.ts:1-58 applies region thresholds (18 in India and Brazil timezones, otherwise ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE).

features.summary: In a Slack channel, when a person mentions AGI again inside a thread where AGI already ran a task for them, the new message continues the same AGI conversation. Answer-mode and direct-message runs keep no session; they rebuild context from Slack history. Web only; desktop shows the same hosted app.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps a Slack thread to one AGI conversation for task-mode runs, so follow-ups add to the same conversation (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-tasks.ts:93-119,167-174). For answers, it re-reads the Slack thread or recent history on each message (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-context.ts:92-122).
purpose.why_it_exists: S106.23 requires each channel thread to map to one persistent agent session so follow-ups continue it. Without it each mention would start a fresh conversation with no memory of the task.
purpose.who_uses_it: A linked Slack user working with AGI in a channel thread.

steps.what_happens: Slack posts an app_mention event with thread_ts; server verifies and queues handling after the response.
AGI resolves the link, mode and creates a run row with channel, message and thread timestamps.
Context is read from Slack's API (thread or history), for task runs as well as answer and DM runs.

When the model route is chosen, the observer looks up an earlier conversation, else inserts one, saves the user message and creates an agent run. A run refused before routing (plan, compute access) gets no agent run, so no agent_run_id is stored and later follow-ups cannot join to it.
The answer is saved as an assistant message and the agent run moves to ready_for_review.

features.summary: Study turns a chat into a tutoring session on one topic. The person picks a topic, a way (Learn it, Practise it, Revise it) and a level, optionally course material from a project and a starting study plan. The server then adds teaching instructions to every turn. Web and desktop (hosted) have a Study page; mobile has Study and learn, Cloud mode only.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks a conversation as a study session and injects a teaching instruction (one idea at a time, hints, worked examples, quizzes and flashcards as artifacts) into each model turn while the session is open (apps/web/features/study/server/study-session-store.ts:86-99, :114-141; apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts:47-68).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S108.23 asks for an education workspace for teachers and learners (classes, assignments, guided study) and S108.24 for curriculum and lesson generation as structured output (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md). The migration says Study is a way of working through a subject, not a second kind of chat (apps/web/db/neon/0247_study_sessions.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners; the shipped flow is learner-side. No teacher, class or assignment feature was found.
problems_solved: Chat answers dump a whole topic; Study makes the model teach one idea, check understanding, and wait (study-session.ts:22-26).

Practice without a quiz tool: quizzes and flashcards come out as artifacts the app renders (study-session.ts:47-56; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/QuizView.tsx, FlashcardsView.tsx).
Finding a session again: sessions are listed and resumable (StudyPage.tsx:128-146).
use_cases: Learn eigenvalues from scratch with a worked example and a check question.
Practise German dative case with short exercises corrected one by one.
Revise a unit using attached course notes from a project and a personal study plan.

where_to_find_it: Web (and desktop via the hosted web app): left navigation item 'Study' to /chat/study (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:144-150; hideable) and a 'Study' row in the composer plus-menu (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:188, :873). Page heading 'Study'.

aliases: Local work to explicit cloud handoff (S110.22)
features.summary: A coding session can run in a managed cloud sandbox on a GitHub repository. A local session can be handed to it from the CLI (agi code handoff) or from VS Code (Code: Continue in the Cloud), and a cloud branch can be brought back with agi resume --teleport or VS Code's Bring the branch in. It works only when managed Code is switched on. Design-to-code and review decks are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs a coding agent in a cloud sandbox on a repository branch, lets the person follow it on web, mobile, CLI or VS Code, approve its steps, open a pull request, and move work between the local checkout and the cloud.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants an explicit local-to-cloud hand-off, a cloud result brought into the local checkout with review, a design implemented in the user's repo and a repository turned into a review deck (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.12, S110.13, S110.22, S110.23). The cloud parity spec says cloud sessions must match Claude's (doc: docs/specs/agi-code-cloud-parity/spec.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers on a plan that includes AGI Code, on a repository hosted on GitHub.
problems_solved: Long coding tasks tying up a laptop
Continuing a terminal session somewhere that keeps running
Getting a cloud branch into the local editor without copy and paste
use_cases: From the CLI: push the branch, run agi code handoff, review what moves, confirm.
In VS Code run 'Code: Continue in the Cloud', type a task, confirm the review.
On web open /code, pick a repository and start a task.
In VS Code pick a cloud session and choose 'Bring the branch in'.

where_to_find_it: Web (and desktop's hosted web app): /code page, button 'Start the task' (apps/web/app/code/page.tsx; apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:131).

VS Code: command 'Code: Continue in the Cloud' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:592-594); the session picker has 'Continue here', 'Bring the branch in' and 'Open on web' (cloudCodeSessions.ts:81, 215-232).
Mobile: Cloud Code sessions list, new session sheet and changes sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/*).
Chrome: not found.
prerequisites: Managed Code switched on for the deployment: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, E2B_API_KEY set, compute priceable (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:6-28).
AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA not 0, false or off (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40-58).

A plan that includes AGI Code (maxSandboxes > 0 and a code harness daily ceiling > 0). It is enforced when a session is created in apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:1244, and the list route only reports it as availability.planEntitled (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/route.ts:57).

VS Code continue: workspace has a git source with a branch (continueInCloud.ts:93-99).
screens_and_controls: CLI review screen listing what moves and what stays, then the prompt 'Hand this session to the cloud?' (lib.rs:3226-3241; code_handoff.rs:322-380).
VS Code modal with question and buttons 'Continue in the cloud' (continueInCloud.ts:21, 119-127).

Web Code page: composer 'Start the task', changes panel, commit, pull request, share, archive (code-surface.ts; features/code/components).

working: Server: open cloud session applies the switches, network and credential checks, workspace feature and code policy gates and the managed-compute access check, then hands the plan to createCloudCodeSession, which refuses a plan without AGI Code (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-open.ts:43-160; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:1243-1244).

CLI: agi code start and handoff with a review, push check and first turn (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3197-3268).
CLI: agi resume --teleport brings a cloud branch and history local (lib.rs:2515-2519; cloud/code_teleport.rs:134-175). The brief says CLI cloud-to-local is missing; the code has it.

Bring-branch-in is a fetch and checkout, not a diff review before applying (context-handoff/index.ts:123-125); only uncommitted local files are confirmed.
CLI hand-off does not carry uncommitted changes (code_push.rs:176-178).
disconnected_or_disabled: Everything is refused unless the sandbox switches are on (cloud-code-session-open.ts:44-46; gate.ts:20-28), and the managed-compute switch is on unless set to 0 (managed-compute-gate.ts:55-58). Changes and commit routes also check e2bProvisioningReady (changes/route.ts:32; commit/route.ts:47).
not_available: S110.12 Design to implementation: no hand-off from a design or prototype to a coding session was found in apps/web/features or apps/web/lib (searches for implement-design phrasing returned nothing); the CLI decision list also rules out a design-to-code handoff (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:466-473).
S110.13 Repository review deck: no code found.
Desktop native hand-off and pull of cloud sessions: the desktop hands a cloud session to VS Code or the terminal by decision (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:342-351).
Chrome and mobile hand-off: not found.

established.statement: The user explicitly hands a local coding session (history, repo state, pending work) to cloud execution and it continues in a cloud session.
A cloud session's result (diff, branch or files) is brought into the local checkout from a product control, with review before applying.

A local session sent to the cloud starts a new cloud session from the pushed branch with a new task, as claude --cloud does; history comes back only when a cloud session is pulled local. VS Code S110.22 is met at parity once cloud sessions are on.
A cloud session's result comes local through the CLI and VS Code; the desktop app adds no native pull.
A cloud session is refused when sandbox switches are off, and when managed compute is switched off.
CLI hand-off sends only a Managed session, and refuses Local or BYOK sessions with an explanation.

acceptance_criteria: With switches off, POST /api/code/sessions returns the 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment' error and the VS Code and CLI actions show a refusal.
With switches on and a plan that includes AGI Code, starting a session on a repository returns a session with a branch.
agi code handoff with unpushed commits stops and tells the user to push first.
agi code handoff from a Local-mode session refuses and names /continue-with-cloud.
agi code handoff of a Managed session shows what moves and what stays, then creates a session; uncommitted changes produce the warning.
agi resume --teleport in a checkout with uncommitted changes refuses and asks to commit or stash.
In VS Code, Bring the branch in with local changes asks before switching and does nothing if declined.
In VS Code, Continue in the Cloud when signed out shows 'sign in to AGI Cloud to continue work in the cloud'.
inferred: The brief's 'review before applying' for S110.23 is met only partly by a dirty-tree confirmation; a diff view of the cloud result before checkout is not present [inferred from index.ts:87-133].
Web should show a visible reason when managed Code is off; the sessions list returns availability.deploymentEnabled and planEntitled for that (code/sessions/route.ts:57-62) [inferred use].
proposed: [proposed] Add a review step (diff summary) before Bring the branch in.
[proposed] Show the same what-moves and what-stays review on web and mobile when they gain a hand-off.
[proposed] Treat design-to-code as a record-or-build decision per app, as the CLI has already ruled it out.

steps.what_happens: CLI reads the local checkout and session, checks pushed commits, and builds the hand-off record from the saved session.
CLI shows the review, asks for confirmation, then posts the record to /api/code/sessions/handoff.

The server validates the record, maps the GitHub remote, applies the switch, network, credential, workspace, policy and managed-compute gates, opens a sandbox session on the branch, and createCloudCodeSession refuses a plan without AGI Code.
The sandbox clones the pushed branch and runs the coding agent; steps and approvals are stored.

To bring work back, the CLI or VS Code fetches the cloud branch from GitHub into the local checkout.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The cloud agent model comes from the CLI --model, default.cloud_model, or an automatic coding route chosen for the plan (lib.rs cloud_code_model, about line 3170-3195); VS Code uses resolveCloudCodeAgentModel from the plan (continueInCloud.ts:116-125). access_and_usage.account: Signed in to AGI Cloud on every surface (CLI CloudClient::connect, continueInCloud.ts:101-106).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace code policy gate for act open_cloud_session and for extra hosts (cloud-code-session-open.ts:119-136); GitHub App access for private repositories (code_handoff.rs:282).
access_and_usage.subscription: Plan must include AGI Code: planIncludesAgiCode is true only when maxSandboxes > 0 and the daily code harness ceiling > 0 (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:839-840); several plans have both at 0 (for example the one at billing-catalog.ts:585-596) and so lack it. The check is enforced on create in createCloudCodeSession (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:1243-1244), which also applies max concurrent sandboxes (getPlanMaxSandboxes); the list route only reports it as availability.planEntitled (code/sessions/route.ts:40-62). Sandbox lifetime comes from the plan (getPlanSandboxTtlMs, billing-catalog.ts:808; getPlanMaxSandboxes at 801); a daily code harness ceiling exists per plan (getPlanCodeHarnessDailyCeilingCents, billing-catalog.ts:827). The same entitlement check also guards GET /api/code/repositories/branches (route.ts:61) and GET /api/github/repositories (route.ts:176), so a non-entitled plan cannot even list repositories.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Managed compute access is evaluated per request and metered as sandbox compute (cloud-code-session-open.ts:138-148); max task length is CLOUD_CODE_LIMITS.task for VS Code (continueInCloud.ts:78-84), and the CLI uses TASK_LIMIT = 8_000 characters and TITLE_LIMIT = 120 (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_handoff.rs:9-10).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: The cloud agent needs a coding-capable route for the plan; not further established.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Full internet or extra egress hosts are refused for agents whose credentials would enter the sandbox; only Trusted hosts or Isolated are allowed (cloud-code-session-open.ts:73-92).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode never reaches the cloud on its own: CLI hand-off is refused for Local and BYOK sessions until the user forks into Managed with /continue-with-cloud and sends the reviewed draft (code_push.rs:71-93). The error text for web is 'Use the desktop app for local code.' (cloud-code-session-open.ts:46). Local coding on desktop needs no paid plan [inferred from AGENTS.md section 6 boundaries].

doc.summary: The web app (apps/web) is a Next.js 16 App Router site plus the server API (apps/web/app/api) that every other app and third parties call. It hosts Cloud chat, accounts, billing, admin and marketing pages, and it is the UI the public Electron desktop loads. Sign-in is Clerk behind an identity port. Web is Cloud-only (Free and paid plans); Local is not available on web, and the public Electron Desktop, which shows this web app, answers every turn in the cloud (only the retained internal Tauri build has Local); BYOK is not on web.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `apps/web` is two things in one deployable: (1) the Next.js web application (marketing pages, sign-in, chat, projects, artifacts, settings, billing, admin) and (2) the server API under `apps/web/app/api` (88 top-level route folders) that Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and third parties call. [code] (apps/web/app/api; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:29 describes the API as 'the HTTP surface under apps/web/app/api that the other six and third parties call').

**Users.**
- Visitors: public marketing, legal, help, pricing and download pages. [code] (apps/web/app)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Provider.** Clerk, accessed only through the identity port `getIdentityProvider()` so the provider can be swapped by environment plus one adapter. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts:11-24; packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:9-11; adapters `clerk.ts`, `clerk-sessions.ts`)

**Web sign-in screens.** `app/login` (combined log-in or sign-up entry `AuthEntryScreen.tsx`), `app/signup` (with `TermsGate`), `app/auth/*` (callback, sso-callback, reset-password, update-password, desktop, device, chrome-extension). [code] (apps/web/app/login, app/signup, app/auth)

**Middleware.** `proxy.ts` takes the identity middleware from the port. Public API routes served without identity are only `/api/health`, `/api/download`, `/api/models`, `/api/waitlist/public` and the OG image. Product routes and `/api/(.*)` run through the identity session. [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:155-164, 170-200)

**How other apps sign in.**
- Browser-origin tokens: the token's authorized party (`azp`) decides the bound surface; `chrome-extension://` origins bind to `chrome`, other origins to `web`. Mobile mints tokens from a Clerk JWT template that carries a surface claim. A token with neither binds to nothing and the plan gate fails closed. [code] (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:53-67)
- Desktop (Electron) and Chrome carry a web-minted token and may refine the surface by header `x-agi-surface`. [code] (free-chat-surface-policy.ts:31-33, 97-112)
- CLI and VS Code: device code flow (`api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `/token`, `/approve`, `/refresh`) and API keys; the page `app/device-auth`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/device; apps/web/app/device-auth)
- Desktop sign-in handoff: `/api/auth/desktop/grant` and `/redeem`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop)

**Account rules checked on the chat route.** Terms version standing, adult (18+) eligibility, MFA/passkey policy, IP allow list, CSRF and rate limits are checked in the auth gate. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:5-35)

**Anonymous use.** A guest chat route (`api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/guest`) exists with bot challenge, per-device and per-IP daily caps (defaults 20 and 100 messages) and spend caps; it is available only when bot protection is ready and the flag `guest.chat` is enabled. [code] (apps/web/lib/guest-chat/config.ts:3-30; guest-chat-access.ts:15-33)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The product names three modes. Here is what the web app does with each. Implementation status is separate from verification status; no run is recorded in the documents read, so every row is unverified by execution.

| Mode | Web in a plain browser | Web inside the Electron desktop host | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:cloud (managed Cloud) | Supported and the only inference path. Free and all paid plans can use managed chat. | Same hosted UI | [code] (billing-catalog.ts:346 `managed_chat: CLOUD_CHAT_TIERS`; free-chat-surface-policy.ts:97-112 maps `web` to `managed_chat`) |
| mode:local | Not supported. Local calls need the desktop host bridge; with no bridge `startLocalChat` throws `DesktopHostUnavailable`. | Not supported. The public Electron Desktop refuses every local-inference command and answers in the cloud; `hostHasLocalMode` is true only when the host shell is `tauri` (the retained internal build), and only that shell's bridge reaches `local_chat_start`. | [code] (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/runtime-client.ts:621-646; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:680-692; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3242-3244, 3366-3367) |
| mode:own-key (BYOK) | Not supported. Web never stores a provider key; BYOK belongs to the CLI and VS Code. | Same: Desktop chat takes no provider keys | [code] (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:224); [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:44 'Must not: expose BYOK/free env-key chat or pretend Local compute is available in-browser without a connected host') |

**Local to own-key crossing.** Web contains the handoff dialog and preview logic for a Local conversation moving to a BYOK model as an explicit fork (`routeLocalToByokSend`, `LocalByokHandoffDialog`). This is code for the consent step; it does not mean web holds keys. [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:81-103; WebChatPage.tsx:412) Whether the BYOK target is reachable from web at all is [unknown].

**Free vs subscribed on web.**
- plan:free: managed chat, tools, projects, memory, skills, cloud sync. Not included: connectors, remote control, AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API, developer surfaces. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:322-361)
- Paid plans (ids `basic`, `pro` labelled Premium, `max`, `max_15x` labelled Ultra, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`): `connectors` from all paid; `agi_work`, `deep_research`, `image_generation`, `managed_api`, `developer_surfaces` from `pro` up; `video_generation` only `max_15x` and `enterprise`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-232, 346-361)
- Plan ids `local-only` and `byok` exist as free-of-charge plan tiers; they carry no managed Cloud capability. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:168-179, 296-299)
- Paid acquisition is staged: checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time switch opens it (`AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1` forces it open). [code] (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-52; checkout route.ts:300-308) The doc says the same. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:19-24)
- Kill switch: env `AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA`; unless set to 0, false or off the gate allows managed compute; when off, chat returns 403 `public_launch_blocked`. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40,50-83)

**Subscription system.** Entitlements are resolved on the server (`lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts`, `effective-subscription-service.ts`) and returned by `api:GET /api/me`; usage accounting is in `managed-usage-accounting-service.ts` and `credit-service.ts`. Clients do not compute quotas. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:20; apps/web/lib/services); [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Data ownership across surfaces')

**Free inference pools.** `apps/web/config/free-pools.json` lists promo pools with terms review fields (`reviewedBy` is null in the first entry read). [code] (apps/web/config/free-pools.json:1-30)

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
The intended unified product is one experience across six apps over one contract layer, with Local, own-key and Cloud as separate trust boundaries. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md; ARCHITECTURE.md)

| Area | Unified intent | What web does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat UI | Shared `unified-chat` package | Uses `unified-chat` pieces but keeps a very large web-only screen, `features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx`, plus its own store `shared/stores/web-chat-store.ts` [code] |
| Modes | Local, own key, Cloud everywhere it fits | Cloud only in a browser; no Local (the public Electron Desktop is cloud-only); no own-key [code] (see Modes) |
| Local-free promise | Local inference on desktop and mobile needs no paid plan | Web has no local inference, and the Electron-hosted web UI offers none either: the public Electron Desktop reports no local models. Only the retained internal Tauri build has a Local row [code] (host-bridge.ts:680-692) |
| Plan names | One AGI Subscription | Server plan ids differ from labels: `pro` is shown as Premium, `max_15x` as Ultra [code] (billing-catalog.ts:192-206) |
| Developer work | Host-owned runtime for Desktop Code, CLI and VS Code | Web has its own cloud code sessions (`api/code/sessions`, `lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts`); the matrix marks terminal use and git as absent on web [code]; [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:414-444) |
| Screen and device tools | present on desktop | Web cannot capture the screen; terminal absent [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md:344, 434) |
| Copy about other apps | One truth | Web marketing and settings copy states availability of other apps from `surface-status.ts`, so those labels must be edited there [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts) |

Web is also the policy owner for entitlements, usage and moderation for all apps, so it carries server logic the other apps only consume. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services)

key_facts.fact: apps/web is both the Next.js web app and the server API that all other apps and third parties call.
Stack is Next.js 16 App Router with React 19; routing middleware is proxy.ts exporting proxy, not middleware.ts.
Sign-in uses Clerk behind an identity port; default provider is clerk, selected by env AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER.

A verified token is bound to a surface from signed claims: chrome-extension origin to chrome, other origins to web, mobile via JWT template claim; no claim means unbound and the plan gate fails closed.
Web chat is managed Cloud only for all signed-in tiers including free; managed_chat capability is granted to free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise.
Web never stores a provider key; own-key (BYOK) belongs to the CLI and VS Code.

Local model chat is not available on web or in the public Electron Desktop, which refuses every local-inference command and answers in the cloud; web's startLocalChat works only when the host bridge shell is tauri (the retained internal build), and without a bridge it throws DesktopHostUnavailable.
Plan ids differ from display labels: pro is labelled Premium, max_15x is labelled Ultra; local-only and byok plan ids exist and are free.
Capability tiers: connectors from any paid plan; agi_work, deep_research, image_generation, managed_api, developer_surfaces from pro up; video_generation only max_15x and enterprise.
Paid checkout requires waitlist or access-code access unless the run-time flag opens upgrades or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1.

doc.summary: The VS Code extension (display name AGI Code, package agi-workforce, version 0.0.2) is a chat and agent panel inside VS Code. It does not run the agent itself: it starts the AGI CLI's local app-server per workspace. It supports Local, own-key and Cloud, but Cloud models need Premium (`pro`) or a higher plan. It is a preview. The Marketplace release is unproven, and the web page marks it Coming soon.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** AGI Code is the VS Code surface (surface:vscode) of AGI Workforce. It gives developers a sidebar chat, an editor-tab chat, and an `@agi` participant in VS Code's own Chat view. It also adds editor helpers: explain, fix, refactor, tests, docs, code review, terminal help, hover, CodeLens and inline completions. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:2-4, 62-70; apps/extension-vscode/README.md)

**Who uses it.** Developers who want an agent scoped to the repository they have open. Chat, agent runs and history are scoped to the workspace folder and run through the AGI CLI on the user's machine. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/README.md:19-24; apps/extension-vscode/docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Purpose)

**Where it sits in the product.** The suite doc calls it the IDE-native developer assistant, workspace scoped. It belongs to the "Host Developer" domain with Desktop Code and the CLI. It is not part of the consumer "Account Cloud" domain. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:35; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:19)

**Platforms.** The web status helper lists macOS, Windows and Linux. The manifest needs VS Code `^1.100.0`, runs in the workspace extension host (`extensionKind: workspace`), and does not support virtual workspaces. [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:45; apps/extension-vscode/package.json:34-39, 107-111)

**Names.** Display name is "AGI Code", marketplace id `agiworkforce.agi-workforce`, publisher `agiworkforce`, pricing field "Free", flagged `preview: true`. Command titles start with "Code:". [code] (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:3,6,31-33; .github/workflows/release-vscode-extension.yml publish job url)

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
**Language and host.** TypeScript, bundled by esbuild into one Node CommonJS file (`out/extension.js`, target node18, `vscode` external). Two browser bundles are built for the webviews: `out/webview/render.js` and `out/webview/dictation.js`. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/esbuild.js:20-60)

**The agent lives in the CLI, not the extension.** The extension spawns `agi app-server` (a local JSON-RPC style process of the Rust CLI) once per workspace root through `LocalRuntimePool` and `LocalRuntimeClient`. That process owns threads, turns, streamed output, approvals, cancellation and session history. Multi-root windows keep one runtime per root. Changing `agiWorkforce.cliPath` disposes the processes. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:2575; src/extension.ts:104-122; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Developer-session architecture)

**Three UI paths share one pool.** The `@agi` chat participant, the sidebar webview (`agi-workforce.sidebar`) and the editor chat panel all use the same `LocalRuntimePool`. [code] (docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md; src/extension.ts:44-58 imports)

**Cloud-backed editor utilities.** Inline completions, code review, suggest-terminal-command, feedback, memory, usage and dictation call AGI web APIs directly with the account token. Completions stream from `<apiEndpoint>/chat/completions` (default endpoint `https://agiworkforce.com/api/llm/v1`). [code] (src/utils/api.ts:1115, 324, 1545; package.json:1214-1218)

**Activation is fault tolerant.** `activate()` guards `setupProviders` and `setupChat` separately, records failures in subsystem health, and falls back to a degraded provider state so the sidebar view always registers. Tests lock this in. [code] (src/extension.ts:76-90, 117-135; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Activation contract)

**Size.** 149 commands are contributed. The extension contributes one Activity Bar container `agi-workforce-sidebar` and one chat participant `agiworkforce.agi`. `src/extension.ts` is 526 lines and `ChatStateManager.ts` is the largest UI file. [code] (package.json contributes; src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts)

**Workspace trust.** In an untrusted workspace the local runtime is not started, and settings such as API endpoint, CLI path, model and inline completion cannot be overridden by workspace settings. [code] (package.json:49-90)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Sign-in is optional for Local and own-key use.** The README says an AGI Cloud account is needed only for Managed Cloud and cloud-backed extras (inline completions, memory, feedback). Local models and provider keys work through the CLI without an AGI subscription. [code] (README.md:35-38; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Quick start)

**Command.** `agi-workforce.signIn` calls `signIn` in `features/surfaces/accountAccess.ts`. If the CLI can start the login (`account/login` over the app-server), the extension opens the verification URL and waits via `account/login/wait`. If the CLI cannot, it falls back to its own device flow. [code] (src/core/commandSetup.ts:1221-1230; src/features/surfaces/accountAccess.ts:27-67; src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:2091-2103)

**Device flow.** The extension requests a code with surface `vscode`, opens a browser approval page (on the user's own computer even in a remote window), and polls for the token. The paths and logic come from the shared `@agiworkforce/client-runtime` package. [code] (src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts:60-110, 190-230; packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts:24, 62-68)

**Where the credential lives.** In VS Code `SecretStorage`. The extension can also borrow the CLI's account token (`account/token`) when it holds none, after checking the owner through `GET /api/me?surface=vscode`. [code] (src/utils/api.ts:300-345, 380-395; src/extension.ts:111-123; README.md Privacy)

**Refresh and sign-out.** Expired sessions renew through the shared refresh endpoint. `agi-workforce.signOut` calls `POST /api/auth/logout`, clears the tier cache and memory cache, and also signs the CLI out. [code] (src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts:127-146; src/core/commandSetup.ts:1243-1256)

**Own-key sign-in.** `agi-workforce.signInProvider <id>` runs `agi login <id>` in a terminal. The id is checked against a strict pattern first because it reaches a shell. The app-server has no login call for providers. [code] (src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:383-404)

**Other credential.** `agi-workforce.setApiKey` stores an AGI API key in SecretStorage. [code] (src/core/commandSetup.ts:1259-1280)

**Provider.** Account identity is the AGI web account (identity handled by the web app; Clerk details are [unknown] from this folder).

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The code names the three modes as trust modes `local`, `byok` and `managed` (Managed Cloud). The chat header names the boundary before a request is sent. [code] (src/features/model-picker/reachability.ts:6; README.md Privacy)

| Mode | Supported | Who | How |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:local | Yes, through the CLI app-server. The runtime schema names Ollama and LM Studio providers. | Anyone, no AGI account or subscription. Free and signed-out users included. | The CLI runs local models on the device. [code] (README.md:35-38; src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:724-731) |
| mode:own-key | Yes (BYOK, bring your own key). | Anyone with a provider key, no AGI subscription. | Keys are held and used by the CLI. Calls go straight to the named provider. `signInProvider` runs `agi login <id>`. [code] (README.md Privacy; src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:383-404) |
| mode:cloud | Yes (Managed Cloud). | Plans that include the `developer_surfaces` capability: Premium (`pro`), Max (`max`), Ultra (`max_15x`), Team (`team`), Team Premium (`team_premium`), Enterprise (`enterprise`). Free and Basic are blocked from managed models. | Models route through AGI servers. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 359; src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:100-109) |

The harness catalog marks `vscode/local-chat` and `vscode/byok-chat` as `unwired`. That flag lags the implementation: the extension code above does run Local and own-key through the CLI. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json:703-725; src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:724-731; src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:383-404)

**Free users.** Free can use Local and own-key. Managed models are refused for Free (the test names this) and Auto is kept off Free. Cloud-backed utilities such as inline completions need an account and a model the cloud picker offers. [code] (src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:67-109; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts:36-60)

**Unresolved tier.** With no known tier the extension treats the account as `byok`, which admits the whole catalog for provider admission by the app-server. [code] (src/integrations/tierResolver.ts:197-221; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts)

**Tier source.** `GET /api/me?surface=vscode` returns the tier and a capability document. The tier is cached for 300 seconds, matching the CLI's own cache. Plan ids the extension accepts include local, byok, free, basic, pro (Premium), max, max_15x (Ultra), team, team_premium, enterprise. [code] (src/utils/api.ts:324, 1409; src/integrations/tierResolver.ts:14-39, 56; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:181-227)

**Boundary rules.** A Local default model is never swapped for a Cloud model. Cloud-only utilities (code review, suggest terminal command, inline completions) refuse and send nothing when the default is Local. Switching provider mid-thread across a boundary starts a new thread. Provider-switch inside one thread needs a plan that allows it (`canSwitchProviderInThread`). The privacy mode allows local only, local plus byok, or all three. [code] (src/core/cloudModelBoundary.ts:12-40; src/integrations/providerSwitchGuard.ts:19-43; src/features/model-picker/reachability.ts:30-34; README.md Privacy)

**Execution boundary.** Local runtime and tools run on the user's machine. Managed Cloud chat, inline completions, memory, usage, feedback, dictation and cloud tasks need AGI servers. Cloud dictation opens a browser page, since a webview has no microphone. [code] (README.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:328)

Whether the free Local use needs the CLI's own sign-in is decided inside the CLI, not here: [unknown] (apps/cli not read in depth).

sections.markdown:

Import counts in `src/` show what is really used: `@agiworkforce/types` in 146 files (plans, model catalog, product names), `cloud-contracts` in 42 files, `local-runtime-contract` in 23, `ide-runtime` in 6, `agent-core` in 4, `client-runtime` in 3, and `routing`, `sync`, `artifacts` and `design-tokens` in 2 to 3 each. `i18n`, `observability`, `utils` have no direct import in `src/` ([inferred] they are declared but may be unused or reached through other packages). `unified-chat` is imported only by `src/webview/render.ts` (markdown plugins, math, assistant fences). [code] (grep of imports, apps/extension-vscode/src)

**Notable reuse.** Device sign-in logic in `client-runtime` is shared with CLI, Desktop and Chrome (surface type `cli|desktop|vscode|chrome`). The managed chat client comes from `cloud-contracts` (`createManagedCloudChatClient`). Memory sync uses `@agiworkforce/sync`. Task classification uses `@agiworkforce/routing`. Terminal, diagnostics and glob helpers come from `ide-runtime`. [code] (packages/client/client-runtime/src/deviceAuthorization.ts:24; src/utils/managedCloudChat.ts; src/memory/accountMemoryClient.ts:9; src/integrations/routingTask.ts:1; src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:13)

**The biggest shared piece is the CLI.** The Rust `apps/cli` app-server is the same engine behind Desktop local sessions. The extension is a client of it. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:76; audit/overview.md:206)

**Model catalog.** Model IDs come from `@agiworkforce/types` (catalog owner: packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts, generated models file). The extension holds no model literal of its own in the code read. [code] (src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts; AGENTS.md section 4)

**Not shared.** The sidebar UI itself is its own webview (`ChatStateManager.ts`, `webviewContent.ts`), not the shared unified-chat React UI. [code] (src/features/sidebar-webview/; grep of unified-chat imports)

**Boundary.** The Marketplace listing is also the contributor's constraint: `README.md` ships in the VSIX, contributor notes do not. [code] (.vscodeignore; README.md header comment)

sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** Code is present and wired: the manifest, activation, sign-in, runtime pool, model picker, tree views and a release workflow all exist. [code] (package.json; src/extension.ts; .github/workflows/release-vscode-extension.yml)

An optional Open VSX job (for VS Code forks) stays off until the variable `OPEN_VSX_PUBLISH` is `true`. [code] (release-vscode-extension.yml)

[code] (src/integrations/cliInstaller.ts:6)

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
The product goal is one consistent experience across six apps. The extension differs on purpose and by gap.

**By design (Host Developer domain).**
- Sessions are workspace scoped and local. They are not synced into Web, Mobile or Desktop chat history. Any move to the cloud is an explicit handoff. [code] (README.md Privacy; docs/CONTRIBUTING-NOTES.md Purpose)
- Chat, history and tools depend on the local CLI process. The other consumer apps use Managed Cloud directly. [code] (src/integrations/localRuntimePool.ts)
- Cloud tasks, projects, schedules, connectors, artifacts and memory show as account tree views, not as the shared web UI. [code] (src/features/*/\*Tree.ts; surface-feature-matrix.md)

**Absent here (per the matrix).** Image, video, research reports, study mode, voice recording, camera, screen capture, skills, plugins, published apps, browser driving, desktop driving, provider Fast mode, in-editor auto-update (the Marketplace updates it), and library artifacts. [requirement] (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md lines 198, 268-348, 368-378, 408, 468, 518, 538)

**Unverified in the matrix.** Search interaction mode, MCP client role, settings and onboarding entry points, context handoff UI, git client role, hooks, account sign-in and config cells. These matrix cells are now outdated in part, see outdated documents. [requirement] (surface-feature-matrix.md lines 218, 238, 258, 388, 428, 448, 558, 588, 598)

**UI.** The editor has its own webview and theme tokens (checked by `check-vscode-theme-tokens.mjs`) rather than the shared React chat, using `unified-chat` only for markdown, math and fence helpers. [code] (src/webview/render.ts:2-12; package.json lint script)

**Plan gate difference.** Managed models need Premium (`pro`) or a higher plan (`developer_surfaces`), while Basic includes managed chat on web. Basic cannot use managed developer models here. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:341-359; src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts:36-45)

sections.markdown:

2. **Entry point.** Read `src/extension.ts` `activate()`; confirm sidebar and runtime pool registration.
3. **Modes.** Read `src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:60-110` and `src/__tests__/modelPickerTierGate.test.ts`. Run that test with the single-test command above, through `scripts/dev/light-job.sh` on the owner's machine.

key_facts.fact: The extension is named AGI Code, package name agi-workforce, version 0.0.2, publisher agiworkforce, preview, pricing Free.
It requires VS Code ^1.100.0 and runs in the workspace extension host; virtual workspaces are not supported.
Entry point is src/extension.ts activate(), bundled to out/extension.js by esbuild (CJS, node18, vscode external).
Chat and agent runs run in a local `agi app-server` process of the AGI CLI, one per workspace root, managed by LocalRuntimePool.

Local models and own provider keys work without an AGI account or subscription; an account is needed only for Managed Cloud and cloud-backed extras. The harness catalog entries vscode/local-chat and vscode/byok-chat are flagged 'unwired' but lag the implementation.

Managed models in the editor need a plan with the developer_surfaces capability: Premium (`pro`), Max (`max`), Ultra (`max_15x`), Team (`team`), Team Premium (`team_premium`), Enterprise (`enterprise`). Free and Basic are blocked.
Tier comes from GET /api/me?surface=vscode, cached 300 seconds (same as the CLI cache); an unresolved tier defaults to byok.
Sign-in uses a browser device-approval flow with surface 'vscode', preferring the CLI's account/login and falling back to the extension's own flow; the credential is kept in VS Code SecretStorage.
Sign-out calls POST /api/auth/logout and also signs the CLI out.
Own-key sign-in runs `agi login <provider>` in a terminal, since the app-server has no provider login RPC.
A Local default model is never swapped for a Cloud model; cloud-only utilities refuse and send nothing when the default is Local.
Inline completions are off by default and send surrounding code to AGI Cloud via <apiEndpoint>/chat/completions (default https://agiworkforce.com/api/llm/v1).
The extension contributes 149 commands, one Activity Bar container agi-workforce-sidebar and one chat participant agiworkforce.agi.
193 Vitest test files exist in src/__tests__, plus native Extension Host suites and webview tests.
Commands: typecheck, test, testWebview, testIntegration, build use the filter agi-workforce.
A release workflow exists (tag v-vscode-X.Y.Z or with channel suffix), verifies the VSIX and publishes via OIDC to the Marketplace; Open VSX publish is off until OPEN_VSX_PUBLISH is true.
Whether the extension is published on the Marketplace is not proven; the surface matrix says the workflow had no runs, and the web status map says Coming soon.
The CLI that the extension needs has no signed release, so VS Code chat works only from a source build.
Sessions are workspace scoped and not synced into Web, Mobile or Desktop chat history; Desktop Code, CLI and VS Code share the Host Developer domain.

Shared packages: types (146 importing files), cloud-contracts (42), local-runtime-contract (23), ide-runtime (6), agent-core (4), client-runtime (3), routing, sync, artifacts, design-tokens; unified-chat only for markdown and math helpers in the webview.
Untrusted workspaces: the local runtime is not started and endpoint, CLI path, model and completion settings cannot be set by the workspace.
Absent in the editor: image, video, research, study mode, voice recording, camera, screen capture, skills, plugins, published apps, browser and desktop driving.
Provider switching inside one thread across providers is allowed only when canSwitchProviderInThread(tier) is true; Auto and unknown providers are always allowed.
Model picker marks models as reachable or 'Needs setup on this machine' using host trust modes local, byok, managed and the privacy mode.
Free plan usage view shows only an upgrade path and no meters in the Account & Usage command.
No verification run was observed for this page; no fact here is executed.

doc.summary: The cli app is "agi", a Rust terminal coding agent (crate agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary). It runs Local (Ollama, LM Studio), own-key and Managed Cloud modes. Sign-in is a browser device code. Managed Cloud needs Premium (`pro`) or higher; Free and Basic fail closed, while Local and own key need no plan. It also hosts the app-server that VS Code and Desktop use. No signed release is published yet.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** `agi` is the terminal coding agent of AGI Workforce. It is a Rust program with a full-screen terminal UI (TUI), a plain line mode (REPL), and a non-interactive `agi exec` / `--print` mode for scripts and CI. Its package description says it is a multi-provider agentic CLI. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:4; apps/cli/README.md:21-28)

**Who uses it.** Developers who work in a repository and want an AI agent in the terminal, including teams that run it in CI/CD. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:21-28). Account features (usage, library, projects, invites) are for signed-in Managed Cloud users only. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:~195-205)

**Role in the product.** The suite doc calls the CLI the "Developer agent surface and Rust engine proving ground", scoped to a workspace or session by default. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:34). The requirements doc lists it fifth in development order, with local transcripts, resume/branch, approvals, shell tools, MCP/plugins/skills/hooks, subagents and review flows. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:1148-1181)

**Developer domain.** The CLI, Desktop Code and VS Code share one host-owned developer-session runtime. CLI sessions are not merged into Web/Mobile/Desktop Cloud chat without an explicit handoff. [requirement] (docs/architecture/overview.md:49; docs/product/requirements.md:1183). The README repeats this: CLI and VS Code share `~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/` and do not join Cloud chat sync. [code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Architecture section)

**Commands.** Primary command `agi`; `agiworkforce` is a backward-compatible alias (second binary). [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:15-21)

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Two kinds of sign-in, both through `agi login`.** [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288)

1. **AGI account (device code).** `agi login` with no provider runs `login_agiworkforce`, which calls `oauth::device_code_login`, saves the grant, and sends a device heartbeat. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1051). The CLI POSTs `api:POST /api/auth/device/code`, `api:POST /api/auth/device/token` and `api:POST /api/auth/device/refresh` on the web origin; the `surface` it sends must be one the endpoint accepts (`cli`, `vscode` or another listed one). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:69-75, 133, 229; apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016-1018). The user opens the verification page `/auth/device` in a browser and enters a code (example `ZED3-E49H`). [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:285-291). The browser target is checked against trusted AGI hosts. [code] (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:309-312 test name)
2. **Own provider key.** `agi login <provider>` prompts for an API key. The accepted list in the error text: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, ollama-cloud, openrouter, nvidia, plus brave or tavily for web search. GitHub Copilot sign-in is refused as unavailable. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288, 1060-1090)

**Where credentials live.** One OS-keyring entry per provider under service `com.agiworkforce.cli.auth`, plus a non-secret index. With `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` they go in an owner-only file. [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92-120, 175). The managed token can also come from env `AGIWORKFORCE_JWT`, then the keyring, then a legacy `~/.agiworkforce/auth.toml`. [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:20-22)

**Account identity.** After sign-in the CLI calls `api:GET /api/me` for the plan tier and email, and caches the tier on disk for 5 minutes (`~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml`, 3-second timeout, trusted `*.agiworkforce.com` HTTPS hosts only). [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:264-275; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:1-50, 195-210). `AGI_AUTH_BASE` overrides the device-grant base for a trusted host. [code] (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:287-292)

**Other commands.** `agi logout` signs out of the account; `agi logout --all` also removes every saved provider key after a confirmation; `agi auth-status` reports state. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7275-7300). The README says the sign-in system behind the account is shared with the web app (the endpoints are in apps/web). [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1016)

**Sign-in not needed for Local or own key.** README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan." Whether a Local session can start with no account at all is not stated in one line of code I opened. [unknown for the no-account case; code-doc] (apps/cli/README.md, Subcommands section)

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
The CLI names its three trust boundaries with `PrivacyMode`: `Local`, `Byok`, `Managed`. Their words for people are "Local", "Your key", "Managed". [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:253-290). Arguments accepted include `local|offline|device`, `byok|cloud-byok|provider`, `managed|agi|agi-cloud|cloud`. [code] (session.rs:~285-294)

| Mode | Meaning in code | Who can use it | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode:local | "no prompt, chat, or file context should leave this device". Providers are Ollama and LM Studio probed on this computer, plus a custom endpoint with no key on a local URL. | Any user, no subscription | [code] (session.rs:~270; apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:69-119; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1835-1855; README: "Local mode and BYOK need no plan") |
| mode:own-key | "selected context may be sent directly to the user's configured provider key". Providers: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, ollama-cloud, openrouter, nvidia, plus brave and tavily for web search (the `API_KEY_PROVIDERS` list, apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1060-1160); user-defined OpenAI-compatible endpoints from `[providers.<name>]` in config.toml are separate | Any user with a key; never gated by plan tier | [code] (session.rs:~272; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-935 comment; apps/cli/README.md custom provider section) |
| mode:cloud (`Managed`) | "selected context may be sent through AGI managed cloud"; requests go to `api:POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions` with a bearer token, an `Idempotency-Key` header and client-surface headers | Premium (`pro`) or higher: `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`. Free and Basic fail closed | [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:501-551; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-945; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 359) |

**Free and subscribed users, in one table**

| Plan | Local | Own key | Managed Cloud in the CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free (`free`) | yes | yes | no. `can_access_model_for_tier` returns false for Free, Basic and BYOK | 
| Basic (`basic`) | yes | yes | no, "Basic can use the economy roster in Web/Mobile/Desktop chat, but not from the CLI" |
| Premium (`pro`) | yes | yes | yes, economy plus pro-additions models |
| Team (`team`) | yes | yes | yes, as Premium roster |
| Max (`max`), Ultra (`max_15x`) | yes | yes | yes, all three slots for Max/Ultra |
| Team Premium (`team_premium`), Enterprise (`enterprise`) | yes | yes | yes |

Source for the table: [code] (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:915-960; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:206-215, 244-253; apps/cli/src/plans.rs:96-104; billing-catalog.ts:359). The capability is named `developer_surfaces`, labelled "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code". [code] (billing-catalog.ts:417)

**Subscription link.** The CLI uses the one AGI subscription system: it reads plan and entitlements from `api:GET /api/me`, plan-capability tables from `packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts`, credit windows (5 hours, week, month) from `packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts`, and a paywall body from the gateway when quota is exceeded (150 percent of tier quota per the code comment). `pnpm check:protocol-types` keeps the CLI plan table equal to the billing catalog. [code] (apps/cli/src/plans.rs:14-16; apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:309-315; apps/cli/README.md Subcommands). Usage accounting itself happens on the server. [inferred]

**Boundary rules.** Account commands (`usage`, `invite`, `library`, `projects`, ...) run only in Managed and refuse in Local and own-key before any request. [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:4, 212, 900-968; README). A Local chat "stays on this device and is not saved to your account history". [code] (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:111, 1487). The gateway base must be a trusted AGI HTTPS host before the bearer token is attached. [code] (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:465-480)

**Fallback chains.** `-m a,b,c` lists models; on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect the next takes over with the provider switched automatically. Whether a chain can cross from Local into own key or Managed without consent is not established here. [code-doc] (README; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs) [unknown for the consent question]

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
**Rust crates shared with the Desktop (Tauri) app.** Path dependencies in apps/cli/Cargo.toml: `agiworkforce-agent-core`, `-app-server`, `-llm`, `-model-registry`, `-mcp`, `-protocol`, `-sandbox-policy`, `-execpolicy`, `-command-registry`, `-utils-image`, `-worktree`. [code] (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:36-46). The Tauri crate also depends on agent-core, execpolicy, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy and worktree. [code] (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32-39). ARCHITECTURE.md says crates/ is "Shared Rust used by both the desktop and the CLI". [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:22)

**Contracts from the TypeScript side.** The CLI compiles in `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json` (model catalog), `managed-usage-limits.ts` (credit windows) and equals `billing-catalog.ts` (plan capabilities) via a check. [code] (model_catalog.rs:25; plans.rs:14; README)

**Protocol types.** `crates/agiworkforce-protocol` exports ts-rs bindings into `packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol`; regenerate with `pnpm generate:protocol-types`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5)

**Other apps that use the CLI as their runtime**

- surface:vscode starts `agi app-server` as the local developer-session runtime (README: used by AGI for VS Code); the extension has app-server references in `apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts` among others. [code-doc + code] (apps/cli/README.md Architecture; grep of apps/extension-vscode/src)
- surface:desktop (Electron) bundles its own `agi` for local coding sessions and talks to it with `DeveloperSessionClient` over stdio. [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md Install section; ARCHITECTURE.md:57-64)
- Desktop workspace terminal: `apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts` consumes `apps/cli/src/app_server/workspace_terminal.rs`. [code] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md DESKTOP-ELECTRON-WORKSPACE-TERMINAL-WIRE-01)
- `agi acp` serves the Agent Client Protocol for Zed and JetBrains. [code-doc] (README)

Nothing under `packages/ui/unified-chat` is used by the CLI; the CLI renders its own terminal UI. [inferred]

| Clippy | `cargo clippy -p agiworkforce-desktop -p agiworkforce-cli --lib -- -D warnings -D unsafe-code` (commands.json:21) |

**Run.** `agi` opens the TUI; `agi exec "..."` or `agi --print` run once; `agi --json-events exec ...` writes one JSON object per event; `agi doctor` checks the setup; `agi app-server` serves the local runtime; `agi remote-control` starts a host. [code-doc] (README) / [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6659)

**CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test --locked -p agiworkforce-cli` under `xvfb-run` on Linux, then the workspace lib tests excluding desktop and cli, the app-server and protocol tests, and MCP tests. [code] (.github/workflows/ci.yml:915-918)

**Test layout.** Unit tests are inline in src modules; integration tests are in `apps/cli/tests/` (app_server_stdio, app_server_websocket, app_server_read_only_token, developer_session_host, json_events_jsonl, broken_pipe, init_managed_trust, terminal_escape_diagnostics, plugins and hooks coverage). TUI snapshot files live in `src/tui/snapshots` (insta). [code] (directory listings; Cargo.toml dev-dependencies)

**Local rules.** On the owner's 16 GB machine, cargo builds and full suites run one at a time through `scripts/dev/heavy-job.sh`. [requirement] (CLAUDE.md, Delegation section). I ran nothing for this page. No run of these commands is recorded in the documents I read. [unknown]

sections.heading: Release state
sections.markdown:
**Implementation status.** The code is broad and connected: the Cargo manifest, command dispatch, auth, managed gateway client, app-server, TUI and REPL are all present (see Folder map). Version is 0.0.1. [code]

**Release status.** [code] (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:6-13) `SURFACE_STATUS` marks only web "Available now"; `cli` is "Coming soon". The public CLI download link is `/download#cli-downloads`. [code] (surface-status.ts:62)

**Pipeline exists, first release unconfirmed.**

- `.github/workflows/release-cli.yml` triggers on tags `v-cli-*` (tag must equal the Cargo version) and on manual runs. A tag run validates, builds six archives (macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Windows x64 and arm64), signs `SHA256SUMS` with a P-256 key held in the protected `cli-release` environment, and publishes a GitHub release. A manual run builds and stops. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/cli-release.md:1-50; .github/workflows/release-cli.yml:1-30)
- The binaries have no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; the signed checksum manifest is the integrity check. [requirement] (cli-release.md)
- `apps/web/public/install.sh` pins a public release key (line 31) and stops with "No signed AGI CLI release is published yet" when GitHub answers 404. [code] (install.sh:31-35, 133)
- The README says the installer stops with that message until the first signed release exists. The surface matrix says "Whether it has ever run is not in this tree." [code-doc] [requirement] (apps/cli/README.md; docs/product/suite.md; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:26). So whether any release is live is [unknown].

**Install channels.** Only the curl installer is advertised; `agi update --install` self-updates; the VS Code extension and Desktop installer bundle or fetch `agi`. Homebrew, npm, WinGet, apt, native Windows installer: none advertised (Homebrew writes to a private tap). [requirement] (cli-release.md, Install channels)

**Verification status.** No document I read records a real end-to-end run of the CLI against production. The audit register records some Electron-to-CLI acceptance work, but it is isolated and not a CLI release check. [unknown / code-doc] (audit/registers/known-flaws.md line 224)

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Only read-only checks were done for this page; run nothing below unless you intend to.

1. Build state: `cargo check -p agiworkforce-cli` and `cargo test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib` (commands.json:143-145).
2. Release state: read `SURFACE_STATUS` in apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts; check GitHub for a `v-cli-*` release; run `bash apps/web/public/install.sh` only on a throwaway machine.
3. Plan gate: read `can_access_model_for_tier` in apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs and `developer_surfaces` in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts; run `agi plans` signed in to see which plans include "Cloud in the CLI and VS Code".
4. Sign-in: run `agi login`, then `agi auth-status`; for own key run `agi login <provider>`.
5. Modes: run `agi --privacy local` (or the `--privacy` argument) and `agi doctor` with Ollama running; see apps/cli/src/local_models.rs probes.
6. Doc drift: compare surface-feature-matrix.md cli rows to `pub mod` lines in apps/cli/src/lib.rs.
7. Guards: `pnpm check:protocol-types`, `pnpm check:llm-operability`, and `node apps/cli/scripts/generate-third-party-notices.mjs --check`.

key_facts.fact: The CLI is a Rust crate named agiworkforce-cli, version 0.0.1, proprietary, not published to crates.io.
Two binaries: `agi` (primary, default-run) and `agiworkforce` (backward-compatible alias).
main.rs only calls agiworkforce_cli::run_to_exit_code(); the real command dispatch lives in src/lib.rs (about 11,000 lines).
Sign-in to an AGI account uses a browser device code against /api/auth/device/code, /token and /refresh on the web origin.
Credentials are stored in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) with an owner-only file fallback when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1.
The CLI has three trust boundaries in code: PrivacyMode Local, Byok, Managed.

Managed Cloud in the CLI requires the developer_surfaces capability, granted to Premium (`pro`), Max (`max`), Ultra (`max_15x`), Team (`team`), Team Premium (`team_premium`) and Enterprise (`enterprise`); Free and Basic fail closed.
Local (Ollama, LM Studio) and own-key modes are never gated by subscription tier, so a Free user can use them.
Managed chat requests go to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions on a trusted AGI HTTPS host with a bearer token and an Idempotency-Key header.
Plan tier is read from GET /api/me and cached in ~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml for 5 minutes with a 3-second timeout.
Account commands (usage, library, projects, invite and others) run only in Managed mode and refuse in Local and own-key mode before any request.
The web release-status table marks the CLI 'Coming soon'; only web is 'Available now'.

A release workflow exists (tags v-cli-*, six archives, signed SHA256SUMS), but the installer says 'No signed AGI CLI release is published yet' on a 404, and the matrix says whether the workflow ever ran is not in the tree.
Binaries carry no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode signature; integrity relies on a signed checksum manifest.
Build and test commands: cargo check/test -p agiworkforce-cli --lib, cargo build --release -p agiworkforce-cli.
CI runs cargo test --locked -p agiworkforce-cli under xvfb-run, then workspace lib tests excluding desktop and cli.
The CLI shares 11 path-dependency crates with the Tauri desktop backend (agent-core, llm, model-registry, mcp, protocol, sandbox-policy, execpolicy, worktree and more).
`agi app-server` is the local developer-session runtime used by VS Code and the Electron Desktop; CLI and VS Code share ~/.agiworkforce/managed_sessions/ and do not sync into Cloud chat.
The model catalog is compiled in from packages/contracts/types/src/models.json; model IDs are not hardcoded in the CLI.
Sandbox: macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap, none on Windows; no in-process fallback; --no-sandbox is the only workaround.
evidence: apps/cli/README.md Runtime requirement and Sandbox defaults sections

key_facts.fact: Voice (push-to-talk) is an optional Cargo feature off by default because cpal links ALSA on Linux.
The CLI has a remote-control command and module, although the surface matrix reports remote control absent for the CLI.
The CLI plan credit windows are read at compile time from managed-usage-limits.ts; plan labels show `pro` as Premium, `max` as Max and `max_15x` as Ultra.
Custom OpenAI-compatible providers are added with [providers.<name>] in ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml; names that collide with built-ins are ignored.
The README claims 35 hook events; I did not verify the count in code.
A multi-model fallback chain (-m a,b,c) switches model and provider on 429, network, 5xx or stream disconnect.
About 4,578 test markers exist under apps/cli/src; this is a grep count, not a run result.
evidence: grep count of #[test] and #[tokio::test] in apps/cli/src

open_questions: Has any signed CLI release ever been published? The tree does not say; the installer reports none and the surface status is Coming soon.
Can Local mode start with no AGI account at all? README says Local and own key need no plan, but I did not find the single code check for the no-account case.
May a fallback chain cross from Local to own key or Managed without a consent step? AGENTS.md requires explicit consent for such moves; apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs was not read.
Product choice: should Free and Basic users get any managed model in the CLI? Code excludes them; billing-catalog sets developer_surfaces to PRO_TIERS.
Are the hook events really 35, and are all three MCP transports connected? Only the README states this.
Do the packages ai/providers folders map to CLI providers? The CLI uses the Rust crate agiworkforce-llm, so provider:<package folder> edges are only approximate.
What real verification (manual run, CI results) exists for Managed mode on production? None is recorded in the documents read.
Does the Desktop (Electron) installer currently ship the CLI binary in a released build, given Desktop is also Coming soon?
