doc.summary: The desktop app is a Mac Electron shell that loads the hosted web app (Managed Cloud chat only) and adds device features: approved folders, Code sessions through a bundled CLI, terminal, browser pane, simulator, computer use and dictation. Retained internal Tauri and an opt-in GPUI native host share the folder. A 2026-10-24 decision note says Tauri will ship as a second public app, but the repository still treats it as internal and the code conflicts with the note; its public status is an owner question. The site still labels Desktop "Coming soon". Release workflow exists; no run is recorded.

sections.heading: What it is and who uses it
sections.markdown:
**Basis summary.** The public Desktop is the Electron app in `apps/desktop/electron`. It opens a window on the hosted web app and adds device powers the web cannot have. [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-15-04; apps/desktop/README.md:1-20).

**Users.** People who want the AGI chat app as a Mac app, plus developers who want AGI Code on local folders (Code sessions, terminal, git, browser pane, iOS simulator pane, computer use, dictation). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseService.ts; apps/desktop/electron/voiceDictation.ts; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md lines 325, 415, 435, 515).

**Three codebases live in `apps/desktop`:**

| Name | Host process | What the window shows | Public? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electron | `apps/desktop/electron` (Node) | The hosted web app | Yes, the public Desktop [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md; ARCHITECTURE.md:43-56) |
| Tauri | `apps/desktop/src-tauri` (Rust) + `apps/desktop/src` (Vite/React) | The Vite app in `src` [code] (apps/desktop/README.md; hostHasLocalMode in packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts) | Retained internal code: the README and AGENTS.md section 5 say it is not a second public product [requirement]. A 2026-10-24 note in D-2026-09-15-04 says the owner chose to ship it as a second public app later, loading the hosted web app (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-99). That conflicts with the code, where the Tauri window shows the Vite renderer, not the hosted web app. Its public status is an open owner question [unknown] |
| GPUI | `apps/desktop/gpui` (Rust, native, no webview) | Native UI over the shared CLI app-server protocol | Opt-in migration host, does not replace either shell [requirement] (apps/desktop/README.md:17-27) |

Product definition: Account-synced Cloud shell plus Desktop Code on the shared host-owned developer runtime [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:32).

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.markdown:
- **Electron main process** in TypeScript, built by `electron/build-main.mjs` into `electron/dist/bootstrap.cjs` (package.json `main`). [code] (apps/desktop/package.json; scripts `build:electron`, `dev:electron`).
- **Window.** `BrowserWindow` with `contextIsolation: true`, `sandbox: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, and a persistent session partition `persist:agi-cloud` so the site login survives restarts. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1104-1116; apps/desktop/electron/config.ts REMOTE_SESSION_PARTITION).
- **Where it loads.** `CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` defaults to the production web origin. A packaged build ignores the `AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` environment variable; only an allowlisted `--agi-cloud-app-origin=` argument can change it (localhost or first-party hosts only). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts, `cloudAppOriginFrom`).
- **One bridge.** `preload.ts` exposes a single object, `agiHost`, to the page. All privileged work goes through `electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts`, which checks a capability grant (`permissionManager.ts`) and contains paths (`pathGuard.ts`). [code] (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts:201; ARCHITECTURE.md:79-91).
- **Code sessions** run in the bundled `agi` CLI (the CLI app-server) started per approved folder; the dispatcher talks to it over JSON lines. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts `startDeveloperSession`, `readyServer`; apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml extraResources `agi-cli/agi`).
- **Packaging.** electron-builder, app id `com.agiworkforce.desktop.cloud`, mac targets dmg and zip, security fuses (no runAsNode, asar integrity). [code] (apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml).
- **Chrome native-messaging host** is the same binary started with `AGI_NATIVE_MESSAGING_HOST=1`. [code] (electron-builder.yml fuse comment).
- **Tauri** is Rust (`src-tauri`) with a React/Vite renderer; `check-wiring.sh` fails drift between the renderer and registered Tauri commands in both directions. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:79-81).

sections.heading: Sign-in
sections.markdown:
**Electron.** Sign-in happens in the user's browser, not in the window. A signed-out window shows a local `data:` screen with Start and Cancel buttons. Start opens the system browser at the web sign-in path with a PKCE-style challenge (random verifier, SHA-256 challenge); a pending sign-in lasts 10 minutes; the shell completes it from a deep link using scheme `agiworkforce-cloud`. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts:1-14; apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:1-40; apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml `protocols`).

The web app's own identity provider is Clerk. The main process only allows navigation through the Clerk host named by this build's publishable key variable `VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (development hosts only) plus first-party hosts. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts `clerkDevelopmentHost`).

**Bundled CLI account.** After the shell is signed in, `developerAccountSync.ts` reconciles the bundled CLI's account (`account/*` calls, device-code approval) with the shell identity before a Code thread starts. Sign-out without a running app-server runs `agi logout --account-only`, which forgets only the account grant and keeps provider keys the user saved in the terminal. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerAccountSync.ts; developerSessionService.ts:1203-1222, 1279-1300; cliAccountStore.ts).

**Required?** The signed-out screen replaces the site's sign-in pages, so chat needs an account [inferred]. Whether Code on a local folder works fully signed-out is [unknown]; the code comment says a thread started before the CLI is signed in is pinned to the user's own provider keys (developerSessionService.ts:2770).

**Tauri** has its own account module (`src-tauri/src/sys/account`) and refresh-token flow; a known flaw says a lost refresh reply revokes the sign-in family (DESKTOP-REFRESH-LOST-REPLY-01 in audit/registers/known-flaws.md:270).

sections.heading: Modes: Local, own key, Cloud
sections.markdown:
| Mode | Electron Desktop chat | Electron Desktop Code (bundled CLI) | Retained Tauri |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode:cloud | Yes. Every chat request is Managed Cloud by construction (hosted web app) [code] (config.ts header comment; dispatcher.ts:3244 comment) | Yes, when the CLI is signed in to the account; the thread takes its model route at start [code] (developerSessionService.ts:2770) | Yes (`AppMode = 'local' \| 'cloud'`) [code] (src/stores/appModeStore.ts:9) |
| mode:own-key | No in chat. The dispatcher refuses on-device inference; own-key chat is not described for Electron [inferred] | Yes via provider keys saved in the CLI terminal, which survive account sign-out [code] (developerSessionService.ts:1203-1213, 2770 comment) | Retained BYOK code in `src/features/byok`, `src/api/byok.ts` [code] |
| mode:local | **No.** Commands in `LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS` return an `unsupported-platform` failure. The device profile reports `localModels: false` [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244-3246, 3366-3368; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:3; dispatcher.ts ~2297) | Local models reachable through the bundled CLI, not through the shell commands [code] (dispatcher.ts:3238-3243 comment) | Yes; local mode only when `supportsLocalAppMode` (Tauri) [code] (src/lib/runtimeEnvironment.ts:21) |

The web app's Local mode row appears only when the host shell is `tauri`: `hostHasLocalMode` returns `bridge?.shell === 'tauri'`, and its comment says AGI Cloud is the Electron shell and offers no on-device model. [code] (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:680-692).

**Free versus subscribed.** The Electron shell code contains no plan check. Plan limits live in the hosted web app and the managed gateway, not in the shell [inferred]. Which plans can use Desktop Code, and what a Free user gets from the bundled CLI, is [unknown]; docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:245 marks plan status on desktop "unverified".

**Requirement mismatch to flag.** The established requirement says local inference on desktop is free of any paid subscription. The Electron chat refuses local inference by decision D-2026-09-15-04 ("Inference stays Managed Cloud"), so that requirement is met on Electron only through local coding sessions in the CLI, and in retained Tauri. [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-95) vs [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244).

MCP: the Electron shell reports `localMcp` from whether the bundled CLI serves MCP; connectors for chat use the hosted account connector service. [code] (dispatcher.ts:2299; docs/architecture/overview.md:136).

sections.heading: Shared code
sections.markdown:
The Electron shell shows `apps/web`, so the whole chat UI is shared with surface:web, and with mobile through the shared contracts. [requirement] (ARCHITECTURE.md:53; docs/architecture/overview.md:24-26).

sections.heading: Differences from the unified experience
sections.markdown:
- **Chat is the web app**, so chat features match surface:web by construction. Gaps are device features the web lacks and web features the shell blocks.
- **No on-device chat models** on Electron (web and Electron chat are Cloud only), whereas mobile and the retained Tauri app offer local inference. [code] (dispatcher.ts:3244; docs/product/suite.md:33).
- **Feature matrix cells for desktop** (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md): present for projects, library, tasks, skills, memory, voice dictation, terminal, git, diff viewer, computer use, BYOK settings (Tauri), deep research (Tauri `src`), media tools (Tauri Rust). Absent: study mode, video generation, local MCP in chat (public Electron reports `localMcp` through the CLI separately), hosted app publishing in the window, renderer browser automation (deleted). Unverified: search mode, camera, plan status, help centre, context handoff. Many "present" cells point to retained Tauri files under `apps/desktop/src`, which the public Electron window does not show [requirement] (matrix line 24 and apps/desktop/README.md), so check the cell path before treating a feature as public.
- **Device registry.** Desktop sends no heartbeat, so a Desktop sign-in never shows in the devices panel (WEB-DESKTOP-DEVICES-NEVER-WRITTEN-01, known-flaws.md:50) [requirement]; `describeDeviceForRegistry` exists in dispatcher.ts:~2290 [code]. Treat the flaw row as possibly stale [unknown].
- **Two continuity domains.** Desktop chats join Account Cloud sync; Desktop Code sessions join the Host Developer domain with CLI and VS Code and are never merged implicitly. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:45; ARCHITECTURE.md:172-176).

doc.summary: The product has three execution modes. Local runs on the device. Own key sends requests straight to the user's provider. Cloud goes through AGI servers, which call providers, and is the only metered, synced path. One shared host list, per-app egress guards, a mobile consent record and CI proofs enforce the boundary. Subscription rules attach to Cloud capabilities only, and they are not one uniform check: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome need the Free-and-up chat capability, while CLI and VS Code need a Pro-tier capability. The Electron Desktop refuses on-device inference by a recorded decision. VS Code does support Local (Ollama, LM Studio) and own key through the CLI app-server and `agi login`, with no AGI account or plan; the harness catalog still marks both unwired, so the catalog lags the implementation. The desktop renderer guard fails open for a host it cannot parse. Two shared contract functions are not called directly by product code (one has no caller; the other has one wrapper caller).

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
AGI Workforce can answer a request in three separate ways. Each one has its own promise about where the data goes. This page maps those ways, says which capability works in which one, and says what stops data crossing from one to the next.

| Mode | Short meaning | Where inference runs | Who pays for inference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode:local | On-device or loopback model. Nothing leaves the device. | The phone (mobile), or a model server on the same machine such as Ollama or LM Studio (CLI, VS Code through the CLI, retained Tauri build) | Nobody. No plan check was found on the mobile Local path. |
| mode:own-key | Bring your own key (BYOK). The device calls the user's own provider directly. | An outside provider, with the user's key | The user, at the provider |
| mode:cloud | AGI-managed access. The device calls AGI servers, which call providers. | AGI servers, then outside providers | AGI, metered against the account's plan |

Why it exists:

- AGENTS.md section 6 says Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud are separate trust boundaries (a line data must not cross without permission). Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to BYOK or Cloud. A Local-to-BYOK move must be an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)
- The product requirement says Local is free of any paid subscription, and that account or sign-in requirements are a separate question from payment. [requirement] (task brief; docs/product/requirements.md:478-486 says Local needs no AGI account)
- A guard fails closed. If the app cannot tell which mode it is in, it must treat the request as Local and block our-cloud egress. [code] (packages/contracts/trust-boundaries/src/egress-policy.ts:5-10). One exception is recorded under Gaps: the desktop renderer guard does not block a target whose host it cannot parse.

Vocabulary:

- **Egress** means data leaving the device.
- **Our-cloud host** means a host name owned by AGI infrastructure: the web app, Vercel, Neon database, Clerk sign-in.
- **Provider label** means the visible name of the outside provider that will receive data.
- **Entitlement** means what the account's plan allows.

Plan names. The code tier names are free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise, plus the zero-price tiers local-only and byok. The labels shown to people are Basic for basic, Premium for pro, Max for max and Ultra for max_15x. This page writes the label and, where a rule is stated, the code tier set. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-16, 166-232, 332-341)

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline, SYS-subscription-entitlements (names assumed from the brief; not opened).

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. The three modes are not the same on every app

The policy table is `docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:36-45`. It says what each app is allowed to offer. The harness catalog says what it marks as implemented. They differ in places, and for VS Code the catalog is the one that lags the code.

| App | mode:local | mode:own-key | mode:cloud | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| surface:mobile | Yes, on-device model (partial in the harness catalog) | No. The remote-chat gate accepts a `byokKeys` flag but never reads it | Yes, after sign-in and provider consent. A `v1LocalOnly` build flag exists that blocks Cloud without an explicit unlock; no released build sets it | [code] (apps/mobile/services/remoteChatGate.ts:3-14; packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json, profile mobile/local-chat) |
| surface:web | Code paths exist for `local:` model ids and a Local-to-BYOK fork. Policy says Web has neither. Reachable in a plain browser: [unknown] | Same as left | Yes | [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts:55-65; apps/web/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts:181-239); [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:38) |
| surface:desktop (public Electron shell) | Refused. The shell rejects every local-inference command. The code names decision D-2026-09-15-04 (chat is Cloud-only) as the reason; local coding reaches local models only through the bundled CLI | Not offered for chat | Yes. It loads the hosted web app | [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3235-3244, 3366-3367) |
| surface:desktop (retained internal Tauri build) | Partial | Implemented, with a Local-to-BYOK fork | Yes | [code] (harnesses.json profiles desktop/local-chat, desktop/byok-chat; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/llm.rs:1211-1215). AGENTS.md section 5 says Tauri is internal code, not the public Desktop. |
| surface:cli | Partial. Models served on loopback | Implemented | Implemented; Cloud models need Premium (pro tier set) or higher | [code] (harnesses.json cli profiles; apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:5-6; apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:925-960) |
| surface:vscode | Yes, through the CLI app-server, with Ollama and LM Studio servers. No AGI account or plan needed. The harness catalog marks it `unwired`, which lags the extension | Yes, through the CLI: the extension runs `<cli> login <provider>`. No AGI account or plan needed. The harness catalog marks it `unwired`, which lags the extension | Implemented; Cloud models need Premium (pro tier set) or higher | [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:~720-745; apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:~383-404; apps/extension-vscode/README.md:~35-38; harnesses.json:703-725 vscode profiles) |
| surface:chrome | Policy says no. A local `chrome/browser-task` profile exists | No | Yes | [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:45); [code] (harnesses.json chrome profiles) |

### 2. Which mode a request is in

- **Mobile.** One persisted value, `appMode`, is `local` or `cloud`. Default is `local`. Every write passes one admission function, so the value cannot become `cloud` unless the signed-in account's provider-sharing permission is current. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts:17-51, 60-66; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/cloudModeDoor.ts:94-102)
- **Desktop (Tauri renderer).** `useAppModeStore` holds `local` or `cloud`. `selectPrivacyMode` maps `local` to the `local` privacy mode and everything else to `managed`. The guard treats anything not `managed` as private, and an exception while reading it also counts as private. A browser build with no Tauri forces `cloud`. [code] (apps/desktop/src/stores/appModeStore.ts:28-33, 45, 104-106; apps/desktop/src/stores/privacyBoundary.ts:3-8)
- **Server.** Each provider call is classified by `trustModeContract(mode)`: where content rests, whose key pays, what may serve as fallback. An unreadable mode is treated as the strictest mode. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/trust-mode-contract.ts:50-80; apps/web/lib/server/trust-boundary-crossing.ts:90-100)
- **A conversation keeps its mode.** On mobile, a Local conversation refuses Cloud models and a Cloud conversation refuses local models, with a message telling the person to start a separate chat. [code] (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2285)

The shared contract names the toggle as two values, `local` and `cloud`. BYOK is a sub-mode of the local position, not a third toggle value. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/sessions/execution-profile.ts:1-20)

### 3. The egress guard

The guard is a replacement for `fetch`. It reads the mode, looks at the host, and throws before any network call when the rule says no.

1. One shared, platform-free list of our-cloud hosts and one matcher live in `@agiworkforce/trust-boundaries`. The list holds the web domain, the Vercel domain, the Neon domain and four Clerk domains. Matching is by suffix, ignores case and ignores a trailing dot. [code] (packages/contracts/trust-boundaries/src/egress-policy.ts:32-64)
2. BYOK provider hosts are deliberately absent from the list, so a direct call to the user's own provider is never blocked. [code] (egress-policy.ts:25-29)
3. **Desktop guard.** In private mode it extracts the host; if the host is on the list it throws `EgressBlockedError`; otherwise it calls `fetch`. It fails open when the host cannot be parsed: `extractHost` returns null on a parse error (for example a relative URL), and the guard throws only for a non-null host on the list. A relative-path request in private mode is therefore not blocked by this guard. [code] (apps/desktop/src/lib/egressGuard.ts:23-45, 56-67)
4. **Mobile guard.** It treats Cloud as open only when `appMode` is `cloud` and the account's provider consent is current. Otherwise it blocks any our-cloud host (the shared list plus the hosts from the configured API and signalling URLs) before network I/O, except exact carve-outs. Reading either mode fails closed to Local. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:72-126, 336-357)

   | Carve-out in Local mode | What it allows | Conditions |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Signed-in account controls | Terms acceptance, age-eligibility check, account deletion status and deletion, cancel-deletion schedule, identity step-up for deletion only, data export | Exact API origin, a Bearer token, an allowed method and path, no query string; some fix the body (egressGuard.ts:215-253) |
   | Withdrawal controls | List schedules, set one inactive, list unfinished runs, pause one run, revoke the Ask from Siri token | Bearer token, fixed body and limited query keys (egressGuard.ts:280-303) |
   | Content report | One POST the person chose to send | Its own Send tap, no query, not while a withdrawal is in progress (egressGuard.ts:136, 193-201, 343-347) |

   Sign-in and session refresh do not pass through this guard. They run through the auth SDK, so they reach the sign-in hosts in either mode. [code] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:28 states this; egressGuard.ts has no sign-in path)
5. All mobile API calls go through `apiFetch`, which calls `guardedFetch`. Product analytics goes through it too, and is switched on only in Cloud. [code] (apps/mobile/services/api.ts:329-342; apps/mobile/services/productAnalytics.ts:30-35)

### 4. The consent step into Cloud on mobile

- Entering Cloud triggers a native alert titled "Share with AI providers?". It names every provider the app can route to and offers Allow, Not now and Details. Details opens the provider list page and then asks again. [code] (apps/mobile/services/providerConsent.ts:81-90, 270-287)
- Allow writes a record under `agi:cloud-provider-consent:v1` holding the account owner id, the provider ids covered, the time and the surface. [code] (providerConsent.ts:58-62, 224-244)
- The consent counts as current only if it belongs to the signed-in account, covers every provider now in the list (a new provider means the question is asked again), and no withdrawal is in progress. [code] (providerConsent.ts:208-217)
- Declining leaves the app in Local. [code] (cloudModeDoor.ts:57-73)
- Withdrawing writes a marker first, so a crash mid-way still closes Cloud on next launch. It returns the app to Local, then pauses schedules and running tasks, and turns off Ask from Siri. If pausing could not finish, a toast says tasks may still run. [code] (providerConsent.ts:159-175, 247-257; cloudModeDoor.ts:151-176)

### 5. Moving a Local chat to a provider

There is no single mechanism. Each app does it differently.

| App | Mechanism | What the person sees | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| surface:mobile | None. A Local chat cannot continue in Cloud. The only crossing is a manual copy of selected chats' text, from the Data controls screen, while in Cloud mode | One alert showing counts and limits, buttons Cancel and Sync to Cloud. No secret scan or payload preview was found in the code read | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:145-235) |
| surface:web | If the active chat is Local and the chosen model is a direct own-key provider, sending opens a consent dialog instead of sending. Regenerate is refused with an explanation | Choose context items (last 10 messages plus the outgoing prompt), see the redacted preview, confirm. The shared preview builder redacts secrets with a scanner, hashes the exact payload, sets `consentRequired: true`, and marks the preview `blocked` when it finds secrets and `blockOnFindings` is on (default on). [code] (packages/platform/utils/src/privacyHandoff.ts:111-167)

The written requirement lists eight steps for a crossing: user action, context selection, secret scan, payload preview, provider label, retention and cost disclosure, consent, new branch preserving the original. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:7.4, lines 135-146)

### 6. What crosses and what does not

- Local chats do not reach AGI servers through the guarded network path. Sign-in traffic and on-device model downloads are outside that path (see Gaps).
- Own-key traffic goes to the provider and never to our hosts. Our servers do not see it. [code] (egress-policy.ts:25-29)
- Cloud is the only path that writes to the shared chat store and the only metered path. [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:73-75)
- Server-side semantic decisions refuse Local and own-key sessions before any transport exists. [code] (apps/web/__tests__/trust-boundary.test.ts:241-302)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Plan catalog.** Tiers and capability sets: [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-364). Labels: basic is Basic, pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra.

| Capability | Plans that include it |
| --- | --- |
| managed_chat, chat_tools, projects, memory_personalization, skills, cloud_sync | plan:free, plan:basic, plan:pro, plan:max, plan:max_15x, plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise |
| connectors, remote_control | PAID_TIERS: plan:basic and every higher plan (not free) |
| agi_work, deep_research, image_generation, managed_api, developer_surfaces, slack_app, artifact_connectors | PRO_TIERS: plan:pro and every higher plan (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise) |
| video_generation | plan:max_15x and plan:enterprise only |
| team_admin | plan:team, plan:team_premium, plan:enterprise |
| enterprise_controls | plan:enterprise |

plan:local-only and plan:byok are in the catalog as free tiers with unlimited projects and custom MCP servers and zero sandboxes and scheduled tasks. They hold none of the capabilities above. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-178, 583-616)

**Rules that bind the modes**

1. Local needs no plan. Mobile Local chat has no account, plan or entitlement check on its path. Only an on-device age confirmation, a downloaded model and the app's own gates apply. VS Code Local and own key likewise need no AGI account or plan. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2290, 2373; rootRouting.ts:30-60; apps/extension-vscode/README.md:~35-38)
2. Cloud requires sign-in. On mobile it also requires the current provider consent and the cloud feature flag; a build with `v1LocalOnly` set blocks Cloud without an explicit unlock. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2349-2385; remoteChatGate.ts:3-8)
3. An app is mapped to a plan capability before a Cloud chat is served: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome use `managed_chat`; CLI and VS Code use `developer_surfaces`; the open API uses `managed_api`. A token bound to no app gets no capability and fails closed. This means the same Free or Basic account gets Cloud chat on four apps and none on CLI and VS Code. It is not one uniform subscription check, which departs from the requirement that every app connects to one subscription system with one set of access rules; whether this is intended is [unknown]. [code] (apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts:42-52, 96-113)
4. The CLI hides every managed model from Free, Basic and own-key accounts. Local and own-key models are never gated by tier. [code] (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:925-960)
5. The capability handshake grants a capability only if all four layers grant it: model, tier, surface, settings. A missing grant fails closed. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/capability-handshake/registry.ts:45-70; capability-handshake-service.ts:112-125)
6. A credential found in a payload refuses the provider call in every mode, including Cloud. Own-key mode refuses a route that would use the platform key. Local refuses every fallback unless a person approved it. [code] (trust-boundary-crossing.ts:86-134)
7. Operator kill switch `AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA` can refuse Cloud compute for everyone. It is on unless set to `0`, `false` or `off`. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:39-53, 61-70)
8. Transitions: tightening a mode needs no approval; loosening always does. This rule is written as `refuseTrustTransition`. No product code calls it (see Gaps). [code] (trust-mode-contract.ts:123-137)
9. Own-key and Local conversations never fall into managed routing silently on the server: `fallback-leaves-trust-boundary` and `platform-key-not-permitted` refusals exist. [code] (trust-boundary-crossing.ts:24-29, 120-134)
10. The declared tier policy lists which provider surfaces a tier may use, and Free lists only managed cloud. No code reads that field. So the rule "own key is a paid feature" is not enforced from it. [code] (model-catalog.ts:1088, 1245, 1401; grep found no reader)

| Situation | What happens | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mode cannot be read (mobile) | Treated as Local; our-cloud request blocked | [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:87-98) |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Statements marked [requirement] come from project documents. Statements marked [proposed] are suggestions of this page, not decisions.

1. **Local is free and needs no account.** [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:478-486). The mobile code matches this. The Electron code does not match the stated requirement that desktop local inference is free of a subscription: it removes local inference from the public Desktop by a recorded decision (D-2026-09-15-04, cited at dispatcher.ts:3235-3241). Whether the founder wants that decision reversed is not settled in the code. [unknown]
2. **A crossing needs eight things.** User action, context selection, secret scan, payload preview, provider label, retention and cost disclosure, consent, a new branch that preserves the original. [requirement] (requirements.md:7.4). The web fork dialog covers most of these; retention and cost disclosure were not found in the dialog. The Tauri fork lacks a provider label and does not block on secrets. The mobile manual copy shows counts and limits only.
3. **Every crossing should be one code path.** [proposed] `refuseTrustTransition` already states the rule (loosening needs an approval), and `evaluateProviderEgress` already enforces key attribution on the server. A single client-side helper that every app's fork dialog must call, and a guard that fails when a dialog is built without a provider label, would turn the written rule into an enforced one.
4. **Plan rules should be read from one table.** [proposed] Own-key use is declared as paid in a tier policy field that nothing reads. Either enforce it or delete it. The product statement says own key and local models are not subscription features, which is the behavior the CLI code has.
5. **One subscription rule across apps.** [requirement] (task brief: every app connects to one subscription system). [proposed] Decide whether CLI and VS Code Cloud chat should keep a Premium-and-above rule while the other four apps allow Free; if yes, record it as a decision, if not, align `free-chat-surface-policy.ts`.
6. **Fail closed on an unparseable host.** [proposed] The desktop renderer guard could block a private-mode request whose host it cannot determine, or resolve relative URLs against the page origin first.
7. **Docs follow code.** [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 2: prose is rank 6). The trust-boundaries table should be edited where it disagrees with the code. For VS Code the policy table agrees with the code and the harness catalog profiles for VS Code Local and own key are the entries to correct.

sections.heading: How to verify
sections.markdown:
Nothing below was run by this pass. These are the commands and files to use.

1. **Shared host list.** `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/trust-boundaries test` runs `egress-policy.test.ts`. Check that a BYOK provider host is not on the list.
2. **All surface proofs together.** `pnpm check:trust-boundaries` (script `scripts/check-trust-boundaries.mjs`). It runs the web, extension, mobile, VS Code, types, Rust routing and Rust send-message proofs, then fails if a Tauri crate pulls in a remote crash reporter.
3. **Mobile only.** Run `trust-boundary.test` in `apps/mobile` in small chunks (the project notes the test runner can hang and exhaust memory). Look at the cases named Local content-report consent, Cloud Mode permission, withdrawal and age check.
4. **Desktop renderer.** `pnpm check:desktop-local-egress` fails a bare `fetch` in the renderer. `pnpm check:rust-egress-boundary` checks the Tauri crate. Add a case for a relative URL in private mode to see the fail-open behaviour.
5. **Plan rules.** Read `BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS`, `PAID_TIERS`, `PRO_TIERS` and `BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS` in `billing-catalog.ts`. For a live account, call `GET /api/me` and read the capability handshake document (`granted`, `deniedBy`, `denialReasons`).
6. **By hand (human check, as the project prefers).** In the mobile app: (a) stay in Local, send a message, confirm no request to the web hosts appears in a proxy; (b) switch to Cloud, confirm the alert names the providers; (c) decline, confirm the app stays Local; (d) withdraw, confirm Cloud closes and schedules pause. In the web app: start a Local chat if reachable, pick an own-key model, confirm the dialog appears with the provider name.
7. **Open questions to settle by running:** whether the web build can reach the Local path at all; whether the main chat route calls the server crossing check; whether an own-key plan is needed on any app.

A green result of any of these says nothing about a build a person installed. The guards read the working tree, not a commit (AGENTS.md section 12).

key_facts.fact: One shared, platform-free list of our-cloud hosts (web domain, Vercel, Neon, four Clerk domains) is the single source for every device guard. Matching is suffix-based, case-insensitive and trailing-dot tolerant.
BYOK provider hosts are deliberately not on the our-cloud list, so direct own-key calls are never blocked.

The mobile guard treats Cloud as open only when appMode is cloud and the signed-in account's provider consent is current. Otherwise any our-cloud host throws EgressBlockedError before network I/O. It fails closed when mode, consent or withdrawal state cannot be read.
In mobile Local mode only three classes of request reach our servers: signed-in account controls, withdrawal controls, and one content report the person sends with its own Send tap.

The desktop renderer egress guard fails open for a target whose host cannot be parsed: extractHost returns null on a parse error and the guard throws only for a non-null host on the our-cloud list. A relative-path request in private mode is not blocked by this guard.

The mobile consent alert is titled 'Share with AI providers?' and names every provider the app can route to. Consent is stored per account with the provider ids covered, and is not current if a new provider has been added or a withdrawal is in progress.

Every write to the mobile app mode passes one admission function, so the mode cannot be Cloud without current consent. Declining keeps Local. Withdrawal returns to Local, pauses schedules and runs, and turns off Ask from Siri.

A mobile conversation keeps its mode. A Local chat refuses Cloud models and a Cloud chat refuses local models; there is no in-app continuation from Local to Cloud. The only crossing is a manual, confirmed copy of selected chats' text, done in Cloud mode.
Mobile has no own-key mode. The remote-chat gate accepts a byokKeys flag and never consults it.
The mobile remote-chat gate has a v1LocalOnly build flag; when set, Cloud is blocked without an explicit unlock. No released build sets it.
Mobile Local chat needs no AGI account or plan on its path; the router lets a signed-out user into the app after onboarding and an on-device age confirmation.

The public Electron Desktop shell refuses every local-inference command with 'unsupported-platform'. The code names decision D-2026-09-15-04 (desktop chat is Cloud-only) as the reason, and says local coding sessions reach local models through the bundled CLI. This conflicts with the stated product requirement that desktop local inference is free.
The desktop renderer guard reads the privacy mode; anything not 'managed', or an exception while reading it, counts as private. A script fails any renderer file that calls fetch directly.

The shared preview builder redacts secrets, hashes the payload, sets consentRequired true and marks the preview blocked when findings exist and blockOnFindings is on (default on). The Tauri own-key fork passes blockOnFindings false and no provider label; the folder-to-Cloud sheet passes true and the label 'AGI Managed Cloud'.

On web, sending from a Local chat to a direct own-key model opens a consent dialog instead of sending, and regenerate is refused. The dialog shows 'Local to Direct BYOK' with the provider name and says the Local thread is unchanged.

The Tauri Rust command llm_create_byok_fork stores only the already-approved messages as a new own-key conversation and leaves the Local conversation untouched; it does not itself check that consent was given.

The server mode contract defines Local as device storage, no key, fallback refuse; own key as user-provider storage, user key, same-boundary fallback; managed as managed-cloud storage, platform key, sync across devices.
refuseTrustTransition (loosening a mode needs approval) is exported but no product file calls it; only a support-claims file names it.

evaluateProviderEgress refuses a provider call that carries a secret, uses a platform key under an own-key conversation, or uses an unapproved or boundary-leaving fallback; every decision produces an audit event. Its only direct product caller is buildProviderEgressGateResponse in managed-compute-gate.ts, which three product files use (artifact completion, experiential-free completions route, free-quota turn).

Code plan tiers are free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise (plus local-only and byok at zero price). Labels shown to people: basic is Basic, pro is Premium, max is Max, max_15x is Ultra. PAID_TIERS means basic and above; PRO_TIERS means pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise.

Plan capabilities: chat, tools, projects, memory, skills and sync are in every tier from free; connectors and remote control are PAID_TIERS; AGI Work, deep research, image generation, managed API and developer surfaces are PRO_TIERS; video only max_15x and enterprise.

Which plan capability a Cloud chat needs depends on the calling app: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome need managed_chat (all tiers from free); CLI and VS Code need developer_surfaces (PRO_TIERS); the open API needs managed_api. A token bound to no app gets none. So a Free or Basic account gets Cloud chat on four apps and not on CLI or VS Code: not one uniform subscription check.

Plan limits by tier: Free has 5 projects, 5 uploads per day, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 2 sandboxes, 0 scheduled tasks and no coding-agent budget; Basic has 3 scheduled tasks and 5 sandboxes; Premium (pro) has 5 scheduled tasks and 10 sandboxes. local-only and byok tiers have 0 sandboxes and 0 scheduled tasks.

AGI Code (cloud coding) is included when a plan has both a sandbox allowance and a daily coding-agent budget above zero, which starts at Basic. This differs from the PRO_TIERS rule for CLI and VS Code Cloud models.
Every product tier allows web search and voice. Free has no manual model selection, no image or video generation, and 10 voice minutes per month.
The tier policy declares which provider surfaces each tier may use (Free: managed cloud only), but no code reads that field, so own-key use is not blocked by it.

Mobile live voice, web search, deep research, cloud code execution and Cloud-side memory are reached only in the Cloud branch of the send path. Turn-based speech capture on mobile requires an on-device recognizer and refuses otherwise.
Mobile Cloud sync, product analytics and Cloud memory run only in Cloud mode; the mobile sync engine also needs an account epoch.

The CLI discovers local models on loopback addresses (Ollama and LM Studio defaults) and never gates local or own-key models by plan; it hides every managed model from Free, Basic and own-key accounts.

VS Code supports Local through the CLI app-server (local model list for Ollama and LM Studio) and own key through the provider sign-in command that runs the CLI login. Neither needs an AGI account or plan; only Cloud models need a Premium-or-higher plan. The harness catalog marks vscode/local-chat and vscode/byok-chat as unwired, which lags the implementation.
CI runs check:trust-boundaries (seven surface proofs plus a no-remote-crash-reporting check on the Tauri crate) and check:rust-egress-boundary. This pass ran none of them.

The harness catalog marks mobile Local, desktop Local and CLI Local as partial, marks VS Code Local and own key as unwired (a flag that lags the extension, which supports both through the CLI), and records Cloud as implemented on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

doc.summary: One AGI Subscription system serves all six apps. The account row resolves to a plan tier (own paid row, then team seat, then Free). Tier tables give capabilities and credit allowances (5-hour and weekly rolling windows, plus a billing-period total). A database reservation gates each managed turn. Stripe sells plans on web; mobile sells nothing in v1. Paid sales sit behind an access-code gate. Apps read /api/me, but CLI, VS Code, mobile, Tauri desktop and Chrome add local plan logic. Local and own-key plans carry no managed usage and no payment; which apps actually offer Local or own-key is set by the trust-boundary document, not by the plan catalog. Local needs no account on Mobile (after an on-device age confirmation), the CLI or VS Code; Electron Desktop chat and web have no Local mode.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
**AGI Subscription** is the single system that decides what a signed-in account may do in the cloud and how much managed AI it may spend. It exists so Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome never keep separate plan rules. [requirement] (docs/product/commercial.md:74-81: one user has one `subscriptions` row and one billing owner; the same entitlement applies to every surface).

Plain terms used below:
- **Plan tier**: the stored plan name (`free`, `basic`, `pro`, `max`, `max_15x`, `team`, `team_premium`, `enterprise`, plus `local-only` and `byok`). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:5-15)
- **Credit**: the only usage unit customers see. 1 credit = $0.005 of provider cost (5,000 microUSD). [requirement] (docs/architecture/credits.md:7-16)
- **Entitlement**: the answer to "what plan does this account hold right now, and is it paid up". [code] (apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts:217-228)
- **Window**: a time slice with its own cap: rolling 5-hour, rolling weekly, and the billing period (monthly). [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts:31-85)

What it does not govern: local inference and BYOK (the user's own provider key). Plans `local-only` and `byok` carry zero managed credits in every window, product limits of zero sandboxes and zero scheduled tasks, and they are absent from the cloud chat capability tiers, so managed chat, cloud sync and projects are denied to them. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:20-24, 33-34; billing-catalog.ts:322-336, 583-616). That is the code basis for "local inference needs no payment". Mobile Local mode never asks the server for a plan. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts, function `refreshTier` returns early unless app mode is `cloud`). Local needs no account. On Mobile the root routing sends a signed-out user through the on-device age confirmation first, then onboarding and the app, with no sign-in required. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts:30-60; apps/mobile/app/index.tsx:9-12). The CLI and VS Code need no account for Local either. Electron Desktop chat has no Local mode. Sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mobile mode. [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:45-60). See SYS-local-inference.

A plan tier existing is not the same as a mode being available on an app. See "Rules: access, plans, modes".

Public names differ from stored ids: `pro` is shown as Premium and `max_15x` as Ultra. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:191-208). Old ids `hobby` and `pro_plus` fold to `basic` and `max`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:1029-1041)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Who is the account, and what plan does it hold
`resolveEntitlementBundle` is the one entry point. Order: (1) the user's own paid, entitled `subscriptions` row; (2) a team seat in an organization whose owner subscription is entitled, whose plan is seat-bearing and whose seat rank is within `licensed_seats`; (3) the user's own lapsed or free row; (4) none. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts:376-413)

A status counts as entitled only if it is `active` or `trialing`. Any other status collapses the effective plan to `free`. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/subscription-entitlement.ts:3-17). Enterprise also tolerates `past_due` and `unpaid` unless the contract is in read-only collection. [code] (subscription-entitlement.ts:19-43)

Access ladder: rank 2 `active`/`trialing` gets managed execution, plan features, purchased-credit spend and plan change; rank 1 `incomplete`/`past_due` gets none (billing portal only); rank 0 everything else. Unknown status ranks 0. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/subscription-access-policy.ts:16-28, 55-79)

### 2. Asking "may this account use X"
- **Capabilities** are static tables keyed by tier: `BILLING_PLAN_CAPABILITY_TIERS` and `canUseBillingPlanCapability`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:302-372)
- **Product limits** (projects, storage, concurrent turns, sandboxes, scheduled tasks, attachments) come from `BILLING_PLAN_PRODUCT_LIMITS`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:580-731)
- Apps get both through `GET /api/me`, which returns `plan` (tier, display name, status, period end, `effective_tier`, `subscription_source`, `billing_owner`), `feature_flags`, a `capability_handshake` document, and attachment and message limits. [code] (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:250-345)
- The handshake is built from four layers: model, tier, surface, settings (operator kill switches, account and workspace switches). A capability is granted only if every layer grants it. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/capability-handshake-service.ts:114-132, 353-383)

### 3. Spending: reserve, run, settle
Every managed turn calls `reserveManagedUsageRequest`. It checks the organization spend cap, resolves the plan allowance (catalog version and revenue context from the open credit period), applies promotion caps, then calls a database function that takes a per-user lock and decides in one place. Variants: normal plan windows, `extra_usage` funding, and per-app artifact runtime. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:738-878)
The turn then settles through `finalizeManagedUsageRequest`, which also writes `provider_cost_events`. [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:1140-1190; docs/product/commercial.md:298-306)

Order of funding: plan windows, then bonus credits (soonest expiry first), then purchased credits only when a plan limit is hit and usage credits (extra usage) are on. A turn that crosses a cap finishes on the plan; the next one goes to credits. [requirement] (docs/architecture/credits.md:44-50; docs/product/commercial.md:239-258)

### 4. Free accounts use a separate ledger
Free turns are admitted by `free-trial-service` against `free_daily_usage_reservations` and `website_auto_economy_trial_usage`, using the same Free numbers from the limits table. [code] (apps/web/lib/services/free-trial-service.ts:40-46, 394-409; apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:91-92, 119-138). The paid ledger helpers return a zero budget for Free (`isFreeSubject`), so Free admission depends on the Free ledger only. [code] (apps/web/lib/server/managed-usage-policy.ts:98-115)

### 5. Buying
- **Web**: `POST /api/checkout` creates a Stripe Checkout subscription session; the Stripe webhook writes the subscription and credit period. [code] (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:494-529; apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts:1-100)
- **Top-ups** (extra credits) via `/api/billing/top-up`, only on an active paid plan billed by Stripe, Apple or Google. [code] (apps/web/app/api/billing/top-up/route.ts:150-168)
- **Mobile stores**: compiled out in v1. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2)
- **Sales gate**: before checkout, an account with no live paid subscription needs waitlist access. [code] (checkout/route.ts:297-310)

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
### Plans, prices and allowances (code is the source)
Prices (monthly, USD): Free 0; Basic 7; Premium (`pro`) 20; Max 100; Ultra (`max_15x`) 200; Team 25 per seat (240 a year); Team Premium 125 per seat (1,200 a year); Enterprise by contract. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-231). India prices exist for Basic through Ultra and Team. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:189-217)

| Plan (id) | 5-hour credits | Weekly | Monthly | Flagship weekly cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free (`free`) | 200 | 1,500 | 2,000 | none |
| Basic (`basic`) | 10 | 100 | 400 | none (the flagship cap exists only for Premium, Max, Ultra and per-seat team plans) |
| Premium (`pro`) | 50 | 500 | 2,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Max (`max`) | 250 | 2,500 | 10,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Ultra (`max_15x`) | no cap (null) | 5,000 | 20,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Team (`team`, per seat) | 50 | 500 | 2,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Team Premium (`team_premium`, per seat) | 250 | 2,500 | 10,000 | 30% of weekly |
| Enterprise | unlimited flag; all window numbers are zero but the plan is treated as uncapped | | | |
| Local-only, BYOK | 0 | 0 | 0 | none (no managed usage) |

Source: [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:20-85, 250-292; ratio 0.3 at line 27). Matches docs/architecture/credits.md:29-42. Enterprise: `unlimited: true` makes the plan credit allowance Infinity, and the ledger allocation uses an uncapped constant. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:82-84, 284-290; apps/web/lib/server/managed-usage-policy.ts:95-102). Catalog versions 1 to 4 all point at the same table today, so grandfathering is a mechanism, not yet a difference. [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:89-96)

Allowances are scaled by the revenue the subscriber's channel and currency produce versus a US web subscriber (store commission, card fees, included tax). [code] (billing-revenue.ts:96-148). A zero cap means zero allowed usage; a null cap means no cap. [requirement] (commercial.md:108-123)

### Capabilities by plan
[code] (billing-catalog.ts:322-364)
- Free and up: managed chat, chat tools, projects, memory, skills, cloud sync.
- Basic and up: connectors, Remote Control.
- Premium and up (incl. team plans, Enterprise): AGI Work, Deep Research, image generation, managed API, developer surfaces (CLI and VS Code cloud), Slack app, artifact connectors.
- Ultra and Enterprise only: video generation.
- Team, Team Premium, Enterprise: team admin. Enterprise only: SSO, SCIM and admin controls.
- Local-only and BYOK: none of the above (not in the cloud chat tiers).

### Product limits (examples)
Free: 5 projects, 1 concurrent turn, 2 sandboxes, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 0 scheduled tasks, 5 attachment uploads a day. Max: 5 concurrent turns, 15 scheduled tasks. Ultra: 10 concurrent turns, 25 scheduled tasks. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:617-690). Free daily caps: 1,000 message writes, 100 conversation creates, 25 MiB egress, 10 emails, 200 vector queries. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:484-490)

### Tables (names seen in code)
| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| table:subscriptions | one row per user: plan_tier, status, period dates, stripe_subscription_id, stripe_price_id, apple_original_transaction_id, google_purchase_token, plan_catalog_version [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:39-55; checkout/route.ts:280-285) |
| table:token_credits | credit period balance (allocated, used, top-up portion, catalog version) [requirement] (commercial.md:225-232) |
| table:credit_transactions | the usage ledger: `deduction`, `purchase`, `refund` rows with `amount_microusd`, `metadata.is_overage`, `metadata.is_flagship` [code] (rolling-usage.ts query; top-up/route.ts:190-196) |
| table:managed_usage_requests | one row per reservation with idempotency key and `is_overage` [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:919-939) |
| table:provider_cost_events, table:cogs_adjustments | cost of goods ledger [requirement] (commercial.md:298-322) |
| table:billing_disputes, table:billing_refund_requests | disputes and refunds [requirement] (commercial.md:189-223) |
| table:free_daily_usage_reservations, table:website_auto_economy_trial_usage | Free ledger [code] (free-trial-service.ts:647-660) |
| table:organizations, table:organization_members | seats: licensed_seats, licensed_premium_seats, seat_type, premium_paid_through [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:62-93; team-seat-entitlement.ts:18-36) |
| table:beta_invites, table:beta_redemptions | access codes [code] (waitlist/access/route.ts:34-48; billing-waitlist-access.ts:47-53) |
| table:waitlist | per-plan waitlist joins [code] (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/route.ts GET) |
| table:mobile_iap_transactions, table:mobile_app_transactions | store purchase records [code] (mobile-iap-ledger-service.ts:158-203) |

### Periods and windows
- 5-hour and weekly windows are **rolling**: spend in the last 5 hours or 168 hours. They refill as old spend leaves, not at a fixed clock time. [code] (rolling-usage.ts; quota text in billing-catalog.ts:922-941)
- The monthly total follows the subscription billing period, not a calendar month. [code] (managed-usage-period.ts:46-75)
- Allowance does not roll over; purchased credits carry across renewals; bonus credits expire after 90 days; Japan purchases expire after six months. [requirement] (credits.md:44-50; commercial.md:231-236)

### Top-ups and extra usage
Two different rates, not to be confused. A top-up buys 50 credits per $1 paid (before discount). A credit is defined as $0.005 of provider cost, so $1 of provider cost is 200 credits. The code keeps them as two separate constants (TOP_UP_UNITS_PER_USD = 50 in billing-topups.ts; CREDITS_PER_USD = 200 in credits.ts). They have not been reconciled, and neither the code nor docs/architecture/credits.md says whether the gap is a deliberate markup or a defect. [code] (billing-topups.ts:5; credits.ts:2-4) [requirement] (credits.md:5-30) [unknown] Packs $20, $50, $100, $250, $1,000; discounts 0, 5, 10, 20, 30 percent; auto-reload an extra 5 percent; purchase min $20, max $1,000, $2,000 a day; auto-reload threshold 100 to 100,000 credits (default 500). [code] (billing-topups.ts:5-14). Extra usage (usage credits) must be switched on in Settings > Billing for purchased credits to be spent. [requirement] (commercial.md:247-251)

### Configuration names (purposes only)
- STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: Stripe API and webhook signature. [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:12-13)
- STRIPE_PRICE_* (for example the Basic monthly USD price): Stripe price ids per plan, interval and currency. [code] (apps/web/lib/pricing.ts:54-57)
- AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1: forces paid upgrades open. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts:28-30)
- AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA: incident kill switch for managed compute. [code] (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40)
- Flag `billing.upgrades_open`: runtime operator switch for the sales gate. [code] (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/billing-upgrades.ts:3)
- Flag `billing.usage_promotions`. [requirement] (credits.md:54-55)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
### Which apps offer which mode
The plan catalog lists `local-only`, `byok` and every other plan as selectable on web, desktop and mobile. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:235-247). That is only visibility in the plan table; Local is offered only on Mobile, CLI, VS Code and the retained Tauri build, not on web or the public Electron Desktop chat (see SYS-local-inference). It does not mean a mode runs on that app. The trust-boundary document sets the real mode support: [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:45-60)

| App | Local | Own key | Cloud (subscription) |
|---|---|---|---|
| surface:mobile | yes, on device | not offered | yes; needs the account's current consent to share with AI providers |
| surface:web | no | no | cloud only |
| surface:desktop (public Electron) | chat: no (rejects local-inference commands); local coding sessions run the bundled CLI and may use a local model or a provider key | chat: no key accepted; coding sessions via CLI yes | chat is cloud only |
| surface:cli | yes | yes (`Byok` tier; enforcement left to the user) | managed models need a subscription |
| surface:vscode | yes | yes | subscription required for managed models |
| surface:chrome | no | no | cloud only |

The CLI tier enum has its own `Byok` variant whose enforcement is the user's responsibility, so local and BYOK CLI use is not gated by the account tier. [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:184-200)

In mobile Local mode, the egress guard blocks every managed-cloud host except account controls, withdrawal controls and a content report the user chooses to send; sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mode. [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:47-49)

### Rules by mode
| Mode | Subscription rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| mode:local | No plan or payment needed. Mobile Local does not call `/api/me`. Plan id `local-only` has zero managed credits and no sandboxes. Needs no account. Offered only on Mobile (after the on-device age confirmation), CLI, VS Code, desktop coding sessions and the retained Tauri build; not on web or Electron Desktop chat. | [code] (store.ts `refreshTier` guard; billing-catalog.ts:583-599) [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:45-60) |
| mode:own-key | `byok` plan: zero managed credits; user pays the provider. Not offered on mobile or web. | [code] (managed-usage-limits.ts:34) [requirement] (trust-boundaries.md:46, 56-57) |
| mode:cloud | Needs sign-in. Free uses the Free ledger; paid plans use the reservation system. Managed Free is public alpha for signed-in users. | [requirement] (commercial.md:8-14, 20-29) |

A Local-to-cloud move is a separate trust-boundary decision. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6)

### Plan resolution rules
1. Own entitled paid row wins over a seat. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:395-398)
2. A seat applies only if the org plan is seat-bearing (per-seat or contract), the member's join-order rank is within `licensed_seats`, and the owner subscription is entitled. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:104-120, 139-143)
3. Premium seat type depends on `premium_paid_through` and `licensed_premium_seats`. [code] (team-seat-entitlement.ts:18-75)
4. Plans below rank 2 resolve to Free. [code] (subscription-entitlement.ts:12-17)
5. If the seat lookup fails for a workspace member and the caller asked for strictness (`/api/me`), the call throws instead of reporting Free. [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:258-264, 401-409) [requirement] (CLI comment tier_cache.rs:696-700)

### One billing owner
The source is read in this order. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:47-67)
1. No row reads as `none`.
2. A malformed Stripe subscription id, or ids from more than one of Stripe, Apple, Google, reads as `unverified`; every billing action fails closed.
3. A valid Stripe subscription id reads as `stripe`; an Apple id as `apple`; a Google token as `google`.
4. No such ids and a `free` tier reads as `none`.
5. No such ids but a valid Stripe customer id reads as `stripe`.
6. Otherwise (a non-free tier with no store id, no Stripe subscription id and no Stripe customer id) it reads as `manual`: organization-managed or granted by hand.

`/api/me` reports `manual` for any seat holder. [code] (me/route.ts:304-307)
Handoff: a second channel loses while the owner is still entitled; once the owner is terminal the new purchase takes over and clears the other ids. [requirement] (commercial.md:86-99). Store rows expire three days after the paid-through date. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:31, 83-107)

### Sales gate and waitlist
- Applies to an account with no live paid subscription. It needs `billing.upgrades_open` on (or env override), or any row in `beta_redemptions`. Otherwise checkout returns HTTP 403 with the waitlist code. [code] (checkout/route.ts:297-310; billing-waitlist-access.ts:38-66)
- The flag reads closed on any failure. [code] (billing-upgrade-gate.ts:10-34)
- Existing paid accounts keep entitlements; Free users need no code for Free managed usage. [requirement] (commercial.md:57-72)
- Access codes open acquisition only; they grant no plan or trial. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/admin-surfaces.md:145). Redeemed through `validate_and_redeem_invite_code`. [code] (apps/web/app/api/waitlist/access/route.ts:44-48)
- Observation: the gate query counts any `beta_redemptions` row for the user, not only rows from billing-upgrade invites. [code] (billing-waitlist-access.ts:47-53) [inferred] that a beta-program redemption also opens checkout.
- Mobile v1 sells nothing. When store purchase turns on, it opens with no waitlist or code. [requirement] (commercial.md:66-70)

### What happens at a limit
The database refuses a reservation with a decision; the server maps it to HTTP and a code. [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts, `reservationError` and `PLAN_LIMIT_WINDOWS`)
| Decision | HTTP | Code | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| declined (period used up) | 402 | `insufficient_credits` | add credits or upgrade or wait |
| extra_usage_required | 402 | `extra_usage_required` | turn on usage credits |
| session_limit | 429 | `rolling_five_hour_limit_reached` | wait for refill, credits, or upgrade |
| weekly_limit | 429 | `rolling_weekly_limit_reached` | same |
| flagship_weekly_limit | 429 | `flagship_weekly_limit_reached` | choose a standard model |
| artifact_limit | 429 | `artifact_runtime_limit_reached` | per-app cap, other chats unaffected |
| organization spend cap | 402 | `organization_spend_cap_reached` | admin |
| anything else | 503 | `billing_unavailable` | retry |
Free codes: `free_trial_token_budget_reached`, `free_trial_model_only`, `free_trial_feature_unavailable`; plan lacks capability: `plan_upgrade_required`. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:884-921)
Recovery action: Free gets Upgrade; paid self-serve plans whose block is cleared by credits get Add credits; accounts not billed by Stripe, Apple or Google are told to wait or ask whoever manages the plan. [code] (work-usage.ts:22-39, 78-94; managed-usage-request-service.ts:86-104)
The next upgrade ladder is Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra; Team and Enterprise have none. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:32-37, 847-860)

### Plan changes
Upgrade goes through `/api/upgrade` with immediate proration; a tier upgrade starts a new billing period and carries usage and purchased balance. Downgrade is the Stripe portal only; the smaller allowance applies at the next renewal while tier gates drop at once. [requirement] (commercial.md:144-170). Disputes set `past_due`, revoke the period's remaining credits and restore them on a win; refunds revoke the refunded share. [requirement] (commercial.md:187-206)

### Trials
No plan in the catalog sets `trialDays`, so catalog trials do not exist today; a trial can still arrive through a referral. [code] (billing-catalog.ts:166-231 has no `trialDays`; checkout/route.ts:431-438, 454)

### Plans granted by hand
A `subscriptions` row with a paid tier and no store id, no Stripe subscription id and no Stripe customer id is the `manual` source. [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:56-66). The mobile review account is meant to get its plan this way. [requirement] (docs/runbooks/mobile-store-first-release.md:92, 179, 431). The tool or admin route that writes such a row was not found. [unknown]

sections.heading: Differences between apps
sections.markdown:
### How each app reads the same entitlement
All five client apps call `GET /api/me` (the surface is passed as a query value) and use `plan.effective_tier`, `plan.tier`, `plan.status` and `capability_handshake`. Usage meters come from `/api/usage`.

| App | How it reads the entitlement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| surface:web | Server code resolves the bundle directly and enforces on every managed route; billing screens in `features/billing`. | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:384; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:399-460) |
| surface:desktop | The public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so it uses web's resolution. The Tauri code is retained internal code, not the shipped Desktop; it calls `/api/me?surface=desktop`, then uses `canUseBillingPlanCapability` and shared model lists. | [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5) [code] (apps/desktop/src/services/cloudAccountAuth.ts:693; apps/desktop/src/services/desktopCloudEntitlements.ts:1-71) |
| surface:mobile | Zustand tier store, persisted; refresh only in cloud mode; reads tier, status, source, period end, handshake, attachment and message limits. Defaults to Free until the first refresh; `planCheckOf` reports `confirmed`, `checking` or `unconfirmed`. | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts `refreshTier`; planCheck.ts) |
| surface:cli | Caches the tier and handshake in `~/.agiworkforce/cache/tier.toml` for 300 s; fetch timeout 3 s; reads usage from `/api/usage`. | [code] (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:31-35, 734-826; usage_summary.rs:11-32) |
| surface:vscode | Same 300 s cache in extension global state; plan comparison table built from shared catalog functions. | [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/tierResolver.ts TIER_CACHE_TTL_MS; features/account-auth/planComparison.ts:1-90) |
| surface:chrome | Fetches `/api/me?surface=web` and answers capability questions with the shared `resolveCapabilityDocumentDecision`. Cloud only. | [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts:20-92) [requirement] (commercial.md:29; trust-boundaries.md:60) |

### Where an app checks plans in its own way
Rows 8 and 9 describe the retained Tauri build, which is internal code and not the public Desktop (the public Desktop shows the hosted web app). They are listed because they are still in the repository.

| # | App | Place | What it does differently |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | surface:cli | apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:184-252 | Own `UserTier` enum including `Byok`; own `tier_rank` and `managed_auto_routing_tier` (Team grouped with Pro; Max, Ultra and Team Premium with Max; Free, Basic and BYOK with free). |
| 2 | surface:cli | tier_cache.rs:677-710, 734-826 | A fresh cache is returned without a network call; a lower fetched tier never replaces a higher cached one, so a downgrade can lag. |
| 3 | surface:cli | apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:22-31 | Own copies of entitled and payment-failed status lists and of the workload labels. |
| 4 | surface:vscode | integrations/tierResolver.ts `coerceTier` | Own tier whitelist and legacy alias map (`hobby`, `pro+`, `pro_plus`), plus a `local` tier. |
| 5 | surface:mobile | apps/mobile/src/features/billing/subscriptionSource.ts | Own terminal-status set (copy of the server's) and own source labels. |
| 6 | surface:mobile | settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:155; model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:293 | Direct comparison `=== 'free'`. |
| 7 | surface:mobile | store.ts | Falls back to `effectivePlanTier(plan.tier, plan.status)` when the server omits `effective_tier`. |
| 8 | surface:desktop (retained Tauri code only) | apps/desktop/src/stores/auth.ts:796 | Sets `subscriptionStatus` locally to `none` for Free and `active` for everything else, without reading the server status. This is a client-side display value. |
| 9 | surface:desktop (retained Tauri code only) | src-tauri/src/core/llm/llm_router.rs:757, 842 | A routing hint, not an entitlement check: `free`, `basic` or `hobby` count as a budget plan when choosing a route. |
| 10 | surface:chrome | features/side-panel/freePlanNotices.ts; cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts | Free-plan notices and a free-trial gateway client of its own (contents not read). [unknown] |
| 11 | surface:web | many files (about 300 reference plan tiers under apps/web) | Direct `isFreeBillingPlanTier` checks for example in top-up route, LLM route, pricing page, voice allowance. |
| 12 | all | Free vs paid | Free is admitted through a separate ledger (free-trial-service) from paid reservations. |

### Mobile purchase state
`nativePurchases: false` means no purchase, upgrade, top-up or restore control, no store connection and no Play Billing permission. It is fixed per build, never switched by OTA update or server. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:1-14). Server-side store verification, catalog and notification routes exist for when it is turned on. [code] (apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap/*). Mobile shows web billing links for Stripe or manual sources and store links for Apple or Google. [code] (subscriptionSource.ts:44-58)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
| Situation | Behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Usage database cannot answer a reservation | HTTP 503 `billing_unavailable`; no model call (fails closed) | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:283-300) |
| Organization policy or spend lookup fails | 503 `billing_unavailable` | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:331-365) |
| Plan catalog lookup fails | falls back to the current catalog, logs a warning | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts:598-612) |
| Rolling usage read fails (display and limit-context paths) | logs a warning and treats usage as 0 (fails open for those reads) | [code] (apps/web/lib/server/rolling-usage.ts, `getRollingUsage` catch) |
| Operator sales switch unreadable | gate stays closed | [code] (billing-upgrade-gate.ts:10-34) |
| Waitlist access check errors | checkout refused with 503 | [code] (checkout/route.ts:299-306) |
| Billing owner unverifiable | all Stripe billing actions refused with a conflict | [code] (subscription-billing-owner.ts:58, 129-136) |
| Subscription lookup fails at checkout | 503, no session created | [code] (checkout/route.ts:286-293) |
| Stripe already bills this customer | 409 conflict | [code] (checkout/route.ts:415-428) |
| Webhook: rate limit or bad signature | rejected before processing | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:34-52) |
| Webhook: event already done | 200 `Event already processed` | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:56-69) |
| Webhook: same event still processing | 503 with `Retry-After: 10` | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:60-66) |
| Webhook: handler throws | whole event rolled back (one transaction), marked failed, HTTP 500 so Stripe retries | [code] (stripe-webhook/route.ts:71-93) |
| Out-of-order Stripe event resurrecting a canceled row | refused | [requirement] (commercial.md:184-186) |
| Seat lookup fails for a workspace member | `/api/me` errors rather than report Free; other paths log and fall back to the user's own row | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:401-409) |
| Owner seat type lookup fails | entitled at the Standard seat | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:360-374) |
| Seat member ledger cannot be provisioned | logged; entitlement still returned | [code] (entitlement-resolution.ts:198-208) |
| CLI tier fetch fails or times out (3 s) | no tier returned; caller uses its configured default; HTTP 401 clears cache and asks for re-login | [code] (tier_cache.rs:790-826) |
| Mobile refresh fails | keeps cached tier, returns false | [code] (store.ts `refreshTier` catch) |
| Idempotency key reused | 409 `idempotency_in_progress`, `idempotency_replay` or `idempotency_conflict` | [code] (managed-usage-request-service.ts `reservationError`) |

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Established requirements, then proposals.

**Requirements the code already follows**
- One account, one subscription row, one billing owner, one entitlement for all surfaces. [requirement] (commercial.md:74-81)
- Credits are the only customer unit; plan numbers live only in `managed-usage-limits.ts`. [requirement] (credits.md:85-87)
- Model and provider names are never hard-coded in consumers; usage cost comes from the registry and rate card. [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4; credits.md:20-25)
- Local and own-key use stays usable without managed usage. [requirement] (commercial.md:79-81)
- Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters (owner decision recorded in project memory; the UsageSection test holds it). [unknown] whether this is enforced on every app; only the web test is named.

**Proposals (not decisions)**
- [proposed] Move CLI, VS Code and Tauri status lists, tier ranks and alias maps to one shared function in `@agiworkforce/types` and generate the Rust copy through the existing protocol-type export, so there is one place to change a plan.
- [proposed] Have `/api/me` (or the handshake) carry a ready-made `is_free` and `is_paid` field so apps stop comparing to the string `free`.
- [proposed] Limit the sales-gate redemption query to invites of the billing-upgrade kind, so a beta redemption does not silently open checkout, if that is not intended.
- [proposed] Record a documented, audited operator path for plans granted by hand, so the `manual` source has a known writer.
- [proposed] Make the CLI cache honour a lower fresh tier from the server after a cancellation, or document the up-to-5-minute lag as accepted.
- [proposed] Make the plan catalog surface visibility match real mode support, or document that it is plan visibility only, so a reader does not take `local-only` as available on web.
