key_facts.fact: Plan tiers are local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; pro is shown as Premium and max_15x as Ultra.

The plan catalog marks every plan, including local-only and byok, selectable on web, desktop and mobile. This is visibility in the plan table, not mode support: Local is offered only on Mobile, CLI, VS Code and the retained Tauri build.

Mode support by app: mobile has Local and Cloud (no BYOK); web is Cloud only; public Desktop chat is Cloud only and rejects local-inference commands; Chrome is Cloud only; CLI and VS Code support subscription, BYOK and local models.
local-only and byok get zero managed usage in every window, are absent from the cloud chat capability tiers (managed chat, cloud sync, projects denied), and have zero sandboxes and scheduled tasks.
Enterprise has unlimited managed usage: unlimited true with zero window numbers, plan credit allowance Infinity, and an uncapped ledger allocation constant.
The CLI has its own Byok tier whose enforcement is left to the user, so local and BYOK CLI use is not gated by the account tier.

Local needs no account: a signed-out Mobile user passes the on-device age confirmation, then onboarding and the app; CLI and VS Code need no account for Local; Electron Desktop chat has no Local mode. In Mobile Local mode the egress guard blocks managed-cloud hosts except account controls, withdrawal controls and a user-sent content report; sign-in SDK calls reach auth hosts in either mode.
Monthly USD prices: Basic 7, Premium 20, Max 100, Ultra 200, Team 25 per seat, Team Premium 125 per seat; Enterprise is contract priced.
1 credit equals $0.005 of provider cost (5,000 microUSD); credits are the only usage unit shown to customers.

A top-up buys 50 credits per $1 paid (TOP_UP_UNITS_PER_USD) while a credit is $0.005 of provider cost (200 credits per $1 of cost, CREDITS_PER_USD). The two constants are kept separate and not reconciled; whether the gap is a deliberate markup or a defect is not established. Minimum $20, maximum $1,000, $2,000 a day; auto-reload threshold 100 to 100,000 credits.

Per-plan credit windows (5-hour / weekly / monthly): Free 200/1,500/2,000; Basic 10/100/400; Premium 50/500/2,000; Max 250/2,500/10,000; Ultra none/5,000/20,000; Team 50/500/2,000 per seat; Team Premium 250/2,500/10,000 per seat.
Ultra (max_15x) has no 5-hour cap (null); a zero cap means zero allowed usage.
Flagship-model usage is capped at 30% of the weekly allowance on Premium, Max, Ultra and per-seat team plans; Basic and Free have no flagship cap.
The 5-hour and weekly windows are rolling sums over the last 5 and 168 hours of credit_transactions deductions; rows tagged is_overage are excluded.
The monthly window follows the subscription billing period; periods over 45 days (yearly) are cut into monthly slices anchored to the start date.
Entitlement resolves in one function: own entitled paid row, then team seat, then own lapsed or free row, then none.
Only active and trialing statuses are entitled; any other status collapses the effective plan to free. Enterprise also tolerates past_due and unpaid unless collection is read-only.

Apps ask for entitlement through GET /api/me, which returns plan, effective_tier, subscription_source, billing_owner, feature flags and a four-layer capability handshake (model, tier, surface, settings).

Capabilities by tier: connectors and Remote Control from Basic; AGI Work, Deep Research, images, managed API, developer surfaces from Premium; video only Ultra and Enterprise; team admin on team plans and Enterprise.
Every managed turn reserves usage through a per-user database function and is refused with a typed decision (402 or 429 codes) or 503 billing_unavailable when billing cannot answer.
Funding order is plan windows, then bonus credits, then purchased credits only when usage credits are on; a turn that crosses a cap finishes on the plan.

Free accounts are admitted through a separate Free ledger (free_daily_usage_reservations and website_auto_economy_trial_usage); the paid ledger helpers give Free a zero budget. Free product limits include 5 projects, 0 custom MCP servers, 0 connector tools, 0 scheduled tasks, 5 daily attachment uploads and 2 sandboxes.

Checkout is gated: an account without a live paid subscription needs billing.upgrades_open on (or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1) or any beta_redemptions row; otherwise POST /api/checkout returns 403 with the waitlist code. The flag reads closed on any error.

A subscription has one billing owner. A malformed Stripe subscription id or ids from more than one channel read as unverified and fail closed. With no store id and no Stripe subscription id: free tier reads none; a valid Stripe customer id reads stripe; otherwise a non-free tier reads manual. Store rows expire 3 days after paid-through.

The Stripe webhook rate-limits and verifies the signature, dedupes by event id (200 if done, 503 with Retry-After 10 if still processing), runs the handler and idempotency mark in one transaction, and returns 500 on failure so Stripe retries.
Mobile v1 sells nothing: storePurchases.json has nativePurchases false, compiled per build; mobile only refreshes the tier in cloud mode.
CLI and VS Code cache the account tier for 300 seconds; the CLI keeps a higher cached tier over a lower fetched one and times out the fetch at 3 seconds.
Team seat entitlement comes from the organization owner's subscription, limited by join-order rank within licensed_seats; /api/me reports subscription_source manual for seat holders.
The offline licensing verifier (TypeScript package and Rust crate) is not wired into any app runtime.
Catalog versions 1 to 4 all map to the same allowance table; a subscription records the version it was sold under.
No plan in the catalog sets trialDays, so trials come only from referrals.
Access codes open acquisition only and grant no plan or trial.

Apps with their own plan logic include the CLI tier enum, the VS Code alias map and mobile direct free comparisons. The retained Tauri code (not the public Desktop) derives subscription status locally and uses a free/basic/hobby budget-plan routing hint, which is not an entitlement check.

doc.summary: One AGI account, held by an identity provider (Clerk today, behind a swappable port), signs in on every app. Web signs in with email, code, password, passkey or provider buttons. Desktop hands off to the browser with a one-time code. Mobile signs in natively. CLI, VS Code and Chrome link through device codes or the web session. Every sign-in meets terms and 18-and-over checks; the minimum age is 18 everywhere today. Local use needs no account.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
**What it is.** Authentication proves who a person is. Identity ties that person to one account that all six apps share. The product keeps the identity provider behind a small interface (a "port") so the provider can change without touching routes or pages. [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11) names `clerk` as the default provider; `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` selects it. Web code asks `getIdentityProvider()` and never builds a client itself [code] (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts).

**Why it exists.** One account lets chat history, plan and devices follow the person across Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. It also gives the server one place to enforce account status, terms, the 18-and-over rule and revocation.

**What it is not.** Sign-in is not payment and not entitlement. Plans, quotas and usage are a separate subsystem (the AGI Subscription system); sign-in only supplies the account id those rules attach to. [inferred] from the sign-in routes carrying no plan check (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/approve/route.ts, token/route.ts). Local inference on mobile and desktop is not gated by payment; whether it is gated by an account differs by app (see Differences between apps).

**Credential families, in one table.**

| Family | Used by | Issuer | Lifetime found in code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity-provider session cookie and session token | Web (and Desktop window, which shows hosted web) | Clerk | Provider-side lifetime [unknown]; product cap 30 days from creation by default (configurable) |
| Identity-provider native session token plus a signed "surface proof" token | Mobile | Clerk (mobile token template) | Provider-side [unknown] |
| Identity-provider token bound to the extension origin | Chrome | Clerk via `syncHost` | Provider-side [unknown] |
| Developer token (JWT signed by the web app) plus rotating refresh token | CLI, VS Code (and the retained Tauri desktop build) | Web app, after browser approval | Access 7 days, refresh 30 days |
| `sk_live_` / `sk_test_` API keys | Programmatic callers | Web app | Out of scope here |

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Sign-in service
The provider is Clerk [code] (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11; apps/web/proxy.ts:17-18 imports the port). Web middleware `proxy` wraps every session route with `identityMiddleware.withSession`, passing an **authorized-party allowlist**. If the allowlist cannot be resolved, the proxy answers 503 instead of running unverified, because a provider skips the origin check when the list is empty [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:192-224, 340). The proxy also sends a signed-out visitor from a protected product route to `/login?redirectTo=...` when no session cookie exists, but `/chat` itself stays past that check; it serves guest Cloud chat only while the `guest.chat` feature flag is on (and bot protection is ready), otherwise guest chat is off [code] (apps/web/proxy.ts:324-330; apps/web/lib/guest-chat/guest-chat-access.ts; config.ts).

Enabled sign-in providers come from `AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS` (`google`, `github`, `microsoft`, `apple`; default Google and GitHub; `passkey` is a flag in the same list) [code] (packages/client/client-runtime/src/authProviders.ts; apps/web/features/auth/authProviderConfig.ts).

### 2. Web sign-in steps
1. `/login` or `/signup` render the same entry screen (apps/web/app/signup/page.tsx calls `AuthEntryScreen`) [code].
2. `AuthFlow` runs a step machine: `email` -> `password` | `code` -> `second_factor` -> `new_password` | `notice` [code] (apps/web/features/auth/authContract.ts, AuthFlow.tsx). Methods are `password`, `email_code`, `passkey`; provider buttons and enterprise SSO redirect through `/auth/sso-callback` [code] (authContract.ts; IdentityAuthAdapter.tsx:296-301, 649-655). Code length is 6, resend cooldown 30 s, minimum password 8 [code] (authRoutes.ts constants in authContract.ts).
3. On sign-up the person types an age first; under 18 is refused before any provider call [code] (apps/web/features/auth/useSignupAgeGate.ts; packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:1).
4. Both flows end at `/login/complete` or `/signup/complete`, a server page that checks in order: a live session exists (else a stale-session recovery screen, not a redirect, to avoid a loop); account is allowed (locked, recovery, suspended, deleted are refused with a notice); primary email confirmed; adult-eligibility decision (`ineligible` shows a refusal, `unconfirmed` asks for age); Terms acceptance; then redirect to a safe destination [code] (apps/web/app/login/complete/page.tsx:41-120).
5. `postAuthDestination` sends the person to the requested path, or a new chat; sign-in loop paths and `/` map to new chat [code] (apps/web/features/auth/postAuthDestination.ts).

### 3. Desktop hand-off to the browser (public Electron app)
The desktop window never shows a password field. A signed-out window shows a data page with Start and Cancel buttons [code] (apps/desktop/electron/signInScreen.ts). Steps:
1. Shell makes a random 32-byte **verifier**, keeps it in memory only, and computes its SHA-256 **challenge** [code] (apps/desktop/electron/browserSignIn.ts:39-41).
2. Shell opens the system browser at `https://<cloud origin>/auth/desktop?challenge=...`. The pending attempt lives 10 minutes [code] (browserSignIn.ts:13, 47-53).
3. The page `/auth/desktop` needs a web session; if none, it sends the person to `/login` and back. It then POSTs the challenge to `api:POST /api/auth/desktop/grant` (CSRF required, rate limit `device-link`, refused for developer-token callers) and gets a one-time code stored hashed with a 60-second life [code] (apps/web/app/auth/desktop/DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx; apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop/grant/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/desktop-sign-in.ts:7, 33-47). If a passkey is required for the account, the page detours to the account-security verify page first [code] (DesktopSignInHandoff.tsx).
4. The browser navigates to the deep link `agiworkforce-cloud://sign-in?code=...&challenge=...` [code] (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-sign-in.ts; host-bridge.ts:4).
5. The shell checks the link's challenge against its pending one. Any mismatch, reuse, relaunch or cancel yields `expired`. On match it loads `/auth/desktop/complete#code=...&verifier=...` in the window [code] (browserSignIn.ts `readBrowserSignInLink`).
6. That page (only runs if the host bridge reports browser sign-in support) POSTs code and verifier to `api:POST /api/auth/desktop/redeem`. The server marks the grant consumed only if the code hash and `sha256(verifier)` match and it has not expired, then asks the identity provider for a **sign-in ticket** valid 60 s, which the page exchanges for a session in the window [code] (DesktopSignInComplete.tsx:73-84; desktop-sign-in.ts:50-67; redeem/route.ts).
7. The window's persistent partition is `persist:agi-cloud` [code] (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:24).

The retained Tauri desktop code instead uses the CLI-style device-code flow (`apps/desktop/src/services/desktopNativeSignIn.ts` imports `requestDeviceAuthorization`, `pollDeviceAuthorization`) [code]. It is internal, not the public desktop [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 5).

### 4. Mobile native sign-in
The app wraps everything in `ClerkProvider` with Clerk's secure token cache [code] (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:58-59, 994). Sign-in screen steps are `email`, `password`, `code`, with email-code, password, passkey-adjacent second factors, Apple and other providers via `useSSO` and `useSignInWithApple` [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/components/MobileSignIn.tsx:5-7, 46). On iOS the app shows either both Apple and other providers or none (App Store rule 4.8) [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/loginProviders.ts). A native token has no web origin, so each API call carries the session token as Bearer plus a second "surface proof" token from a Clerk template, sent in `SURFACE_TOKEN_HEADER` [code] (apps/mobile/services/authSession.ts; apps/mobile/src/integrations/clerk.ts:79-146). The server admits such a pair only if both tokens lack an origin claim, name the same subject and the proof binds a known surface [code] (apps/web/lib/server/native-session-token.ts).

### 5. CLI and VS Code device linking (RFC 8628 device grant)
1. Client calls `api:POST /api/auth/device/code` with `surface` of `cli`, `vscode`, `chrome` or `desktop`. Server stores a pending row and returns `device_code` (UUID), a short `user_code` (XXXX-XXXX), verification URL, interval 5 s, lifetime 900 s [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/code/route.ts:24-31, 80-120; grant-policy.ts).
2. Client opens `/auth/device?user_code=...&surface=...`. The signed-in person sees the client name and scopes (`account:read`, `managed-cloud:use`) and approves or denies with `api:POST /api/auth/device/approve` [code] (apps/web/app/auth/device/page.tsx; approve/route.ts).
3. Approval is refused when: caller is itself a developer-token session; the account's device sign-in setting is off (403 `DEVICE_SIGNIN_DISABLED`, 503 if unreadable); Terms need re-acceptance; the 18-and-over decision is not confirmed [code] (approve/route.ts:45-190).
4. Client polls `api:POST /api/auth/device/token`. Answers: `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied`, `expired_token`, `account_unavailable`, `terms_acceptance_required`, age refusal, or tokens. On success the server consumes the code and inserts a hashed refresh token in a new family, in one transaction [code] (token/route.ts:70-250).
5. Access token is a JWT (issuer `agiworkforce-api-gateway`) valid 604800 s; refresh token is 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, valid 30 days [code] (developer-token.ts:9-11; device-refresh-token.ts:5-22).
6. `api:POST /api/auth/device/refresh` rotates the pair; a replayed old refresh token marks the whole family compromised and revokes it [code] (refresh/route.ts, refresh-token-family.ts `finishFamilyAsCompromised`).
7. CLI stores the grant in the OS keyring (service `com.agiworkforce.cli.auth`), or an owner-only file when `AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1` [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:92, 175, 778). VS Code stores it in `SecretStorage` under `agiWorkforce.accountToken` [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:220-229).
8. Sign-out calls `api:POST /api/auth/logout` with the access token and/or refresh token; it revokes the token id and the whole session family [code] (apps/web/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts; apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:451-485).

### 6. Chrome extension link to the web session
The extension does not run its own sign-in form. `openClerkSignIn` opens `<web origin>/sign-in?redirectTo=/auth/chrome-extension` in a tab; `/sign-in` is a permanent redirect to `/login` [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/clerkAuth.ts:216-223; apps/web/next.config.ts:155). The page `/auth/chrome-extension` only reports signed-in or signed-out and tells the person to return to the side panel [code] (apps/web/app/auth/chrome-extension/page.tsx). The extension's Clerk client uses `syncHost` (the web origin from `CLERK_SYNC_HOST`) so it mirrors the web session, and requires a token whose `azp` claim equals the extension's own origin [code] (clerkAuth.ts:84-92, 129-135). Cookie changes on the sync host (`__client_uat*`) trigger a re-read, so signing out on the web signs the extension out [code] (clerkAuth.ts `watchSyncHostSession`). Extension sign-out also DELETEs the synced web session by id [code] (clerkAuth.ts:247-280). A dev-only bearer in `chrome.storage.local` exists in development builds [code] (freeTrialClient.ts:371, 409).

### 7. Session length
- Product cap: any session older than `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME_HOURS` is refused and ended. The value is an environment setting; when unset or invalid it defaults to 720 h (30 days), measured from creation, not last use. The provider's own idle expiry also applies and renews on use [code] (apps/web/lib/auth/session-policy.ts:3, 12-19, 35-60; api-auth.ts `assertSessionWithinAbsoluteLifetime`).
- Provider-side idle length is a Clerk dashboard setting, not in the repo [unknown].
- User-selectable idle sign-out: Security settings hold a `session_timeout` value (minutes). A browser-side timer, `useSessionTimeout`, signs the person out after that much inactivity, with a warning 2 minutes before. It is a browser timer only; the server never reads it, and the mobile app does not enforce it [code] (apps/web/shared/hooks/useSessionTimeout.ts; apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx). The page 70-qa/start-here/where-things-stand.md records the fixed behaviour as off unless the person picks a limit (15 minutes is one choice; one person stayed signed in for 62 minutes). The checked-in hook I read still falls back to 60 minutes when no value is stored, so the shipped default is [unknown] until that fix lands; confirm against the build you test.
- Device grants: access 7 days, refresh 30 days (above).

### 8. 18-and-over step
`ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE` is 18 [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:1). The minimum age is 18 everywhere today. The mobile gate has a per-region table (India, Brazil, default) and every entry is 18; the gate floors each threshold at `ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE` [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/ageGate.ts:25-26, 50, 69-70). The server stores only an outcome (`eligible` or `ineligible`), the minimum it was judged against and how it was reached; never the age [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0425_adult_eligibility.sql; adult-eligibility.ts). A decision counts only while its minimum is at least the current one. `api:GET /api/eligibility` reads state; `api:POST /api/eligibility` submits evidence (`declared_age`, `age_checked_on_device`, `platform_age_signal`) [code] (apps/web/app/api/eligibility/route.ts). An `ineligible` outcome is final until support reviews it [code] (adult-eligibility.ts comment). Confirmed state is cached 5 minutes per server instance [code] (adult-eligibility.ts:55).

### 9. Linked devices and sign-out everywhere
- Every non-web surface registers with `api:POST /api/devices/heartbeat` (rate limit `device-heartbeat`, CSRF), which upserts `table:device_registrations` keyed by user, surface and install id and links the credential family and identity session id [code] (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts). CLI calls it after login [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1052; device_registry.rs:6).
- `api:GET /api/settings/devices` lists them; `api:DELETE /api/settings/devices/{deviceId}` unlinks one (options `lost` and `logoutAll`), `PATCH` renames, `POST` stops remote work [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts:431-433).
- `api:GET /api/settings/sessions` lists provider sessions and ends any past lifetime; `api:DELETE /api/settings/sessions/{sessionId}` ends one; `api:DELETE /api/settings/sessions` is **sign out everywhere**: CSRF, step-up proof (`session.revoke_all`), revokes every other provider session, then the current one, and revokes every device refresh credential; sends a security notice; on partial failure answers 502 with counts so the caller can retry [code] (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:189-274).

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Every authenticated API request** passes, in order: token verification (developer token, then identity-provider token with authorized-party check, then native token plus surface proof), absolute session lifetime, account status (`active` only; `locked`, `recovery_pending`, `suspended`, `banned`, `deletion_scheduled`, `deleted` are refused; fail-closed after one retry), account security (passkey or step-up where required), MFA policy for workspaces, and IP allow-list [code] (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:452-480; account-status.ts:1-10; docs/security/security.md:345 [requirement]).

**Token-class restrictions.**
- A surface token used as a Bearer is refused (`surface_token_as_bearer`) [code] (api-auth.ts:365-368).
- A developer-token session may not approve a device or grant a desktop sign-in; it needs an interactive session [code] (approve/route.ts:45; desktop/grant/route.ts).
- API keys work only on endpoints that declare an API-key scope [code] (api-auth.ts:437-447).

**Terms.** Device approval, device token and refresh each re-check Terms acceptance; a poller keeps its approved code and waits while the person accepts on the web [code] (token/route.ts:155-170).

**18-and-over enforcement points (server).** Enforced: `/login/complete`, device approve, device token and refresh, product page layouts (chat, tasks, code, workspace, quick-ask, admin, welcome), the LLM chat-completions gate, embeddings, audio transcription, speech, live voice sessions, image and video generation, and mobile intents [code] (grep of `adult-eligibility` and `requireAdultEligibility` across apps/web/app and apps/web/lib). Not enforced on every API route: settings, billing, export and deletion deliberately stay reachable [code] (require-adult-eligibility.ts comment). An unreadable decision refuses, never admits (503) [code] (adult-eligibility-gate.ts).

**Modes and plans.**

| Mode | Account needed to sign in? | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| mode:local (mobile) | No account. The device asks for age first (18 everywhere; the per-region table holds 18 for every entry) before any screen; sign-in appears only when the person chooses Cloud | [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts:38-60; ageGate.ts:25-26, 50, 69-70) |
| mode:local (CLI, VS Code) | No account; local models and BYOK work without `agi login` | [code] (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1013, "Run `agi login` for your AGI account, or `agi login <provider>` to use your own API key") |
| mode:own-key (CLI, VS Code) | Provider API key saved in keyring or SecretStorage; no AGI sign-in required | [code] (auth.rs API_KEY_PROVIDERS; extension-vscode utils/api.ts:228-237) |
| mode:cloud (all) | AGI account, adult-eligibility confirmed, Terms accepted; plan rules then apply elsewhere | [code] (device/approve, token routes; llm auth-gate.ts:282) |

Entitlement and quota decisions are not made by the sign-in code. Device scope `managed-cloud:use` says only "subject to plan and workspace permissions" [code] (device/code/route.ts:41-46). See SYS-chat-turn-pipeline for how a turn is gated after identity.

**Trust boundary.** Signing in must not silently move a Local chat to Cloud or BYOK [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 6). On mobile, sign-in and session refresh run through the provider SDK and reach the provider hosts in either mode; only the listed account controls pass the egress guard in Local [requirement] (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:47).

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
Everything here is [proposed] unless a requirement is cited.

- [requirement] Local, BYOK and Managed Cloud stay separate trust boundaries; sign-in never reroutes Local work (AGENTS.md section 6).
- [requirement] Local inference on mobile and desktop must not need a paid plan. Whether it needs an account is open; today mobile Local needs none (see Rules).
- [proposed] State the provider-side session idle length in code or a doc owned by `docs/security/security.md`, so engineers need not open the provider dashboard.
- [proposed] Give the Chrome extension a stated signed-out behaviour in one place.
- [proposed] Make Mobile "sign out all accounts" wording say it affects this device only, and link to account-wide sign-out.
- [proposed] Apply the 18-and-over gate through one shared function at the API layer rather than per route, so a new route cannot forget it.

key_facts.fact: The identity provider is Clerk by default, selected through a port; `AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` can name another provider but only `clerk` is implemented.
Web proxy returns 503 for session routes if the authorized-party allowlist cannot be resolved, instead of authenticating without the origin check.

A signed-out visitor to a protected product route is redirected to /login with redirectTo, but /chat is exempt from the cookie check. Guest Cloud chat on /chat exists only while the guest.chat feature flag is on; web has no Local mode.
Desktop sign-in uses a PKCE-like hand-off: the shell keeps a random verifier in memory, sends its SHA-256 challenge to the browser, and redeems a one-time code with the verifier.
The desktop pending attempt lives 10 minutes; the server grant and the sign-in ticket live 60 seconds; the grant is stored only as a hash.
The desktop deep link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud and the host is sign-in.
Redeem is accepted only in a desktop host that reports browser sign-in support, so a grant opened in an ordinary browser fails.
CLI, VS Code and (in the Tauri build) desktop link through an RFC 8628 device grant: code issued with 900 s life and 5 s poll interval, approved on /auth/device, exchanged at /api/auth/device/token.
Device access tokens are web-signed JWTs valid 7 days; refresh tokens are 32 random bytes stored as SHA-256 hashes and valid 30 days, rotated on use.
A replayed refresh token marks its whole family compromised and revokes it.
Device approval is refused for developer-token callers, when the account has device sign-in switched off, when Terms need acceptance, or when no current 18-and-over decision exists.
Mobile Cloud calls send the Clerk session token as Bearer plus a Clerk-template surface proof in a separate header; the server admits a native token only with a matching proof.
Mobile root routing requires a device-level age gate before any screen, then lets signed-out users stay in the app; sign-in screens open only on request or when a ended session is owed.
The Chrome extension reuses the web session through Clerk syncHost, requires a token whose azp equals the extension origin, and opens /sign-in which redirects to /login.

The minimum account age is 18 on every surface and in every region. The mobile gate has a per-region table (India, Brazil, default) in which every entry is 18, and it floors each threshold at ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE. The server stores only outcome, minimum age, method and time, never the age.
An age decision made under a lower minimum no longer counts and the person is asked again; an ineligible outcome stands.

Server-side 18-and-over enforcement covers login-complete, device grant, product page layouts, LLM chat, embeddings, transcription, speech, live voice, image and video generation and mobile intents, not every API route.
Sign out everywhere is DELETE /api/settings/sessions: it needs CSRF and a step-up proof, ends all other provider sessions, then the current one, and revokes every device refresh credential.

Product session cap is measured from session creation, on top of the provider's idle expiry. SESSION_ABSOLUTE_LIFETIME_HOURS is an environment setting that defaults to 720 hours (30 days) when unset or invalid.

A user-selectable idle sign-out (session_timeout in Security settings) is a browser-side timer in useSessionTimeout that the server never reads and mobile does not enforce. The checked-in hook falls back to 60 minutes when no value is stored; 70-qa/start-here/where-things-stand.md records the fixed behaviour as off unless the person picks a limit, so the shipped default is not established.
The provider-side session length is not in the repository.
evidence: apps/web/lib/auth/session-policy.ts comment says the provider's expiry renews on use

key_facts.fact: Linked devices are rows in device_registrations created by POST /api/devices/heartbeat and managed through /api/settings/devices.
CLI credentials sit in the OS keyring (service com.agiworkforce.cli.auth) or an owner-only file when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING=1; VS Code uses SecretStorage.
apps/cli/src/trust/identity.rs is workspace identity for trust grants (git remote key), not account sign-in.
CLI logout posts to /api/auth/logout, which revokes the token id and the whole session family, or the family named by a refresh token.
Enabled web sign-in providers come from AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS among google, github, microsoft, apple; default google and github.
Sign-in, device approval and token issue do not check a plan; plan gating happens after identity.
No document in the repository was found recording a real run of these sign-in flows.

doc.summary: Local inference runs a model on the user's device. It works on Mobile (Apple and Google system models, plus downloaded ExecuTorch and llama.rn models), and in the CLI and VS Code through Ollama and LM Studio. Public Desktop and Web refuse it, and the Chrome extension has none (it reports localModels false). No account or plan is needed on Mobile or the CLI. Mobile Local chats are plain text. They have no tools or web search and are not synced. Chat content never goes to AGI servers, but Mobile Local mode still lets a few signed-in account controls (terms, age check, account deletion, data export) reach AGI servers, and it passes any non-AGI host, although Mobile has no own-key mode; that is a boundary gap, not a feature.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
Local inference means the model answers on the user's own machine. The prompt, the files and the answer are not sent to AGI servers or to an outside model provider. It is the "Local" trust boundary, one of three. The others are BYOK (bring your own key) and Managed Cloud. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:111, docs/product/requirements.md:478-492)

Why it exists:
- Local mode must need no AGI account and no hidden cloud call. It must fail closed: if a feature needs remote compute, the app says so and offers a fork. It must not route silently. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492)
- Local and BYOK must stay useful without paying AGI. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:84)
- The brief for this page adds that local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription. Account or sign-in is a separate question from payment.

**Execution boundary in one line.** Local chat on Mobile runs entirely on the device. Chat content, files and telemetry are not sent to AGI servers. The network is used for the one-time model download from a third-party host, and the egress guard also lets through a short list of signed-in account controls (see Rules) and any non-AGI host (Mobile has no own-key mode, so this is a boundary gap, not a feature). In the CLI and VS Code, a model server on the same computer does the work. Public Desktop (Electron) has no Local chat at all. The Chrome extension has no local inference. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:24-35, :317-327; see Rules and Differences below)

Related pages: SYS-chat-turn-pipeline (the Cloud turn path), and any page on AGI Subscription entitlements.

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### Mobile (surface:mobile, mode:local)

**Four runtimes in three tiers.** The shared package `@agiworkforce/local-llm` picks the tier at send time. [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts:105-146, packages/platform/local-llm/src/types.ts:1-3)

| Tier | Runtime | What it is | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `foundation_models` (iOS) | The Apple system model, already in the OS. No download. | Native module reports it available. The Swift code checks iOS 26 or newer. [code] (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIFoundationModels.swift:22-23) |
| 1 | `aicore` (Android) | The Google system model, reached through the ML Kit GenAI Prompt API. No download. | Native module reports available. [code] (apps/mobile/native/android/AGICoreModule.kt:10-22) |
| 2 | `executorch` | Model files (`.pte`) run by react-native-executorch. | Device RAM at least 3500 MB, or RAM unknown and the module is present. [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/capabilities.ts:4, :75-76) |
| 3 | `llama_rn` | A GGUF file run by llama.rn. | Always marked available. Needs a model path. [code] (capabilities.ts:77, selector.ts:127-129) |

Selection order in `localGenerate`: it refuses if the device is thermally throttled. Then it uses Tier 1 when the chosen model is the system model. Then Tier 2 when the model has an ExecuTorch preset. If Tier 2 throws, it falls back to Tier 3 when a file path exists. Otherwise it fails with "No local model is ready. Download a local model first, or join AGI Cloud when it is available." [code] (selector.ts:105-146)

**Which models can be picked.** The picker lists catalog entries marked `shipsInV1`, and filters again by what the platform can run. The catalog is a hand-written list in `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts`, not the generated model catalog. Today four entries ship: a default text model ("AGI Standard"), a small lite model ("AGI Lite"), the Apple system model and the Google system model. The vision and other entries have `shipsInV1: false`, so they are not selectable on Mobile. [code] (catalog.ts:34-35, :152-153, :178-179, :197-198, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:102-111, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/catalogSelectability.ts:20-28). For exact model names and sizes read `packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts`. Do not copy them from this page.

**What a person must do first.**
1. Pass the age gate. It runs before everything, including Local Mode. The answer is held on the device, from an OS age range or a typed age. [code] (apps/mobile/app/index.tsx:12-14, apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/ageGate.ts:98-106, apps/mobile/__tests__/age-gate-guards-cloud-not-local.test.ts:8-24)
2. Finish onboarding. It shows a short first-run disclosure to accept, with managed cloud off. Then it asks for a name and work description (optional), detects the device tier, and offers a model. The person can skip the download and go to chat. [code] (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:299-312, :395-398)
3. Download a model, unless they use a system model. The default is a multi-GB download. The Apple and Google system models need no download, but only work where the OS offers them. [code] (service.ts:168, installStore.ts:152-176)
4. Without a ready model the chat tab shows "Download a model to chat" or "No compatible local models", and the send is stopped. [code] (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:721-745, :1494)

**How a download works.** [code] (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts)
- ExecuTorch models: `tier2LoadModel` fetches the model, tokenizer and tokenizer config through `react-native-executorch-expo-resource-fetcher`. The source URLs are Hugging Face addresses in the catalog. Files land in `<documents>/react-native-executorch/`. (installStore.ts:497-524, catalog.ts:5-6, modelStoragePaths.ts:4)
- GGUF models: `downloadModel` requires HTTPS, a 64-hex SHA-256, and a safe file size. It resumes from a `.partial` file, then checks the SHA-256 in chunks. Files land in `<documents>/models/<id>/model.gguf`. (modelDownload.ts:97-143, :293-330)
- Before the first byte: the device must be online, and on Wi-Fi unless the person turned on "Download over cellular". Free disk must cover the size plus 256 MB. (modelDownload.ts:190-230, installStore.ts:379, :521)
- After: model folders are excluded from iCloud and device backup, and kept in Documents so the OS does not purge them. (modelDownload.ts:80-91)
- Each install is recorded in the `installed_models` table of the on-device encrypted database. (storage/migrations.ts:49-60, storage/db.ts:25)
- On startup, records whose files are gone are dropped so the app offers Download again. (services/executorchModels.ts:81-100)

**A Local turn.** In `sendMessage`, the mode comes from the conversation, or from the model id (cloud-managed ids mean cloud, everything else is local). A Local chat refuses cloud models, and a cloud chat refuses local models. It never switches silently. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2255-2282, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/conversationMode.ts:7-9)
The Local branch then:
- builds the history, adds the local system prompt, resolves the model reference, and calls `localGenerate` with an abort signal; (chatExecutionStore.ts:3036-3098)
- streams tokens, splits out any thinking tags, records speed and memory, and commits the answer into the local on-device store; (chatExecutionStore.ts:3135-3230)
- returns before any cloud code (consent, entitlements, web search, tools, sync) runs. (chatExecutionStore.ts:3232-3236 vs :2374-2390)

### CLI (surface:cli, mode:local)
The CLI does not download models. It probes servers the person already runs: Ollama at `http://localhost:11434` and LM Studio at `http://localhost:1234/v1`, or a configured base URL. It lists installed models with `agi models scan` and checks a model is installed before a turn. [code] (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:6-8, :54-73, :244-330, apps/web/app/local/page.tsx:25-31) Run it with `agi --provider ollama --model <model>`. [code] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:195-196)
First-run onboarding has "Local model, no account needed". It never shows the cloud login in that path. [code] (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:264, :387, :839-851)
The session privacy mode is `Local`, and its description says no prompt, chat or file context should leave the device. [code] (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs:255-290)

### VS Code (surface:vscode, mode:local)
The extension has no model runtime of its own. It starts the local `agi app-server` from the AGI CLI and asks it for local models, then shows them in an "On this device" group. The CLI must be installed, and the workspace must be trusted. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:714-745, src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2034-2060, README.md:23-38)

### Desktop (surface:desktop)
Public Desktop is the Electron shell and is Cloud-only for chat. The dispatcher returns `unsupported-platform` for every command in `LOCAL_INFERENCE_COMMANDS` before permission handling, and the device profile reports `localModels: false`. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3237-3244, :3365-3367, :2298, packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:3-10) A Desktop coding session runs the bundled CLI, which can use a local model. [code] (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3239-3241, docs/architecture/desktop.md:113-115)

### Chrome extension (surface:chrome)
No local inference. Its device heartbeat to the cloud bridge sends `capabilities.localModels: false`. The words "ollama" and "lmstudio" in its side panel are only provider icon ids. [code] (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39, apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10938, :10943)

sections.heading: Data and state
sections.markdown:
**Mobile.**
- Local conversations and messages live in the on-device SQLite database `agi_mobile.db`. It uses a SQLCipher key kept under the storage id `agi_sqlcipher_db_key_v1`. [code] (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:22-25)
- A Local chat session is labelled `executionAuthority: local_device`, `storageScope: local_device`, `syncPolicy.syncEligible: false`. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/sessionLabeling.ts:66-80)
- Cloud sync is only queued when the mode is cloud. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2950-2957)
- Table `installed_models` columns: id, display_name, runtime (`local` or `cloud`), format (`gguf`, `safetensors`, `mlx`, `onnx`, `pte`), size_bytes, sha256, local_path, installed_at, last_used_at, capabilities. [code] (storage/migrations.ts:49-60, storage/installedModels.ts:5-12)
- The store `useModelInstallStore` persists `allowCellularDownloads`, which defaults to false. The "Download over cellular" choice is shown in onboarding and in Settings, Storage. [code] (installStore.ts:379, :383, modelDownload.ts:192)
- Model files: `<documents>/models/<safe-id>/model.gguf` and `<documents>/react-native-executorch/`. Both are excluded from backup. [code] (modelStoragePaths.ts:3-5, modelDownload.ts:79-91, :102-105)
- Memory, personalization and past-chat context for Local chats come from the local settings store and on-device memory. They are not the account memory. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2789-2820, apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/pastChatContext.ts:117-124)
- "Delete all local chats" appears in Data controls when the app mode is Local. [code] (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:449-470)

**Chat turn metadata** saved on the answer: `localMode`, `localModelId`, `localRuntime`, `localModelName`, tokens per second. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:3178-3194)

**CLI.** Local-boundary memory goes to a separate file, so Local content never mixes with BYOK or Managed memory. [code] (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:35-42) Local base URLs are read from the CLI config (`config.base_url`). [code] (local_models.rs:55-67)

**Desktop and Web.** No local model state is stored. The unused web types `LocalModelSettings.baseUrls` are only normalised, with loopback required. [code] (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/inference.ts:150-165)

**Server-side.** A Local Mobile chat writes nothing to AGI tables. The CLI device heartbeat records `localModels` in table:device_registrations column `local_models_available`, but the CLI only sends it in Managed mode. The Chrome extension also sends a heartbeat, always with `localModels: false`. [code] (apps/web/db/neon/0207_device_registrations.sql:40, apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:64-80, apps/cli/src/device_registry.rs:172-177, apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-373, apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39)

sections.heading: Rules: access, plans, modes
sections.markdown:
**Account / sign-in, by surface.** This is separate from payment.

| Surface | Account needed for Local chat? | Where the code says so |
|---|---|---|
| surface:mobile | No. A signed-out user reaches the app. Routing only forces onboarding and the age gate. A signed-out user is not sent to sign-in unless a session just ended. | rootRouting.ts:44-60 [code] |
| surface:cli | No. Local first run skips cloud login. The README says Local mode and BYOK need no plan. | onboarding.rs:839-851; README.md:335-337 [code] |
| surface:vscode | No. An AGI Cloud account is only for Managed Cloud and cloud extras. The CLI does the local work. | README.md:35-38 [code] |
| surface:desktop | Not applicable. Local chat is not offered. Sign-in (Clerk) is needed for the Cloud chat that Desktop does offer. | docs/architecture/desktop-local-runtime.md:11-17 [requirement], dispatcher.ts:3365-3367 [code] |
| surface:web | No local inference. | no code found [inferred] |
| surface:chrome | No local inference. Heartbeat reports `localModels: false`. | deviceHeartbeat.ts:33-39 [code] |

**Payment / plan.** No plan, entitlement or quota check sits on the Mobile Local branch. The entitlement call `ensureCloudEntitlementsReadyForRequest` and the consent call `ensureCloudSendConsent` are in the cloud branch only. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2374-2390, :3036-3232) The mobile model list contains no plan lock for local models. A model is `locked` only for an environment or cloud tier reason, and local entries never get one. [code] (service.ts:85-95, :168) The CLI states that Local needs no plan. [code] (apps/cli/README.md:335-337) The "Free plan" has no bearing on Mobile Local. Subscription accounting is therefore not applied to Local turns. No local usage is reported to an AGI Subscription system. [inferred] from the absence of any usage call in the Local branch.

One payment-linked rule exists in Web code: the composer hides the "Local models" row when the user's plan is Free (`!freePlan && localModels.available`). It is only reachable on a host whose shell is `tauri` (see Differences). [code] (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:1043, :1766, packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:690-692) This conflicts with the requirement that local inference is free of any paid subscription. See Gaps.

**Trust-boundary rules.**
- A Local chat never takes cloud models, and a cloud chat never takes local models. Mobile gives an error and asks for a separate chat. [code] (chatExecutionStore.ts:2263-2282)
- **Mobile egress guard in Local mode.** The guard's message says Local Mode is "on-device + BYOK only", although Mobile has no own-key mode, and it blocks calls to our managed-cloud hosts before any network I/O. [code] (apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts:24-35, :300-327) It lets four kinds of request through:
  - A content report the user chose to send (POST to the report path only), except while a withdrawal is in progress.
  - Signed-in account controls (`authControl`): terms acceptance, the age check that opens Cloud, account deletion status, scheduling and cancellation, the identity check for deletion only, and the data export. The code comment says none carries chat content and these rights must not depend on sharing with AI providers. The age check must pass before Cloud opens, so blocking it would keep Cloud shut. Paths and methods are listed in `SIGNED_IN_ACCOUNT_CONTROLS`, and some requests must match a body rule (for example the age check carries only age evidence). A bearer token is required (per the finding checked at egressGuard.ts:210-244; the bearer test itself was not re-read).
  - Withdrawal controls (`withdrawalControl`): list schedules, set one inactive, list unfinished runs, pause a run, revoke the Ask from Siri token. Each only stops work.
  - Any non-AGI host, passed on to `secureFetch`. The guard's comment calls this BYOK direct-to-provider, but Mobile has no own-key mode, so this is a stale comment and a boundary gap, not a feature.
  So a Local-mode phone can still contact AGI servers for these account controls when the person is signed in and uses them. It does not send chat content, files or telemetry. [code] (egressGuard.ts:210-244, :300-327)
- CLI: Local, BYOK and Managed are session privacy modes. A Local session refuses cloud calls (`CloudError::NotManaged`), and sub-agents get no off-device route. [code] (cloud/client.rs:368-373, apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:39-45)
- CLI and Rust base URLs for local servers must be loopback. Non-loopback is shown as `blocked`. [code] (local_models.rs:104-110, :152-155, apps/web/app/local/page.tsx:34 says the same in marketing)
- TypeScript contract: a local server URL must be on this machine, or the request is refused. [code] (inference.ts:171-205)
- Local to BYOK or Cloud is a fork, not a mode flip. The original Local thread stays Local. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:115, docs/product/suite.md:62)
- VS Code: a Local default model is never replaced by a cloud model. Cloud-only commands send nothing and say so. [code] (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/cloudModelBoundary.ts:12-47)

**Features in Mobile Local mode.**

| Feature | Works? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Streaming text chat, with thinking text split out | Yes | chatExecutionStore.ts:3052-3115 [code] |
| Local system prompt | Yes | stores/chat/localSystemPrompt.ts:3-12 [code] |
| Chat mode and style prompts | Yes (added to history) | chatExecutionStore.ts:2774-2780 [code] |
| Projects: instructions and sources | Yes, local projects | chatExecutionStore.ts:2758-2772 [code] |
| Memory, personalization, past-chat context | Yes, from device stores | chatExecutionStore.ts:2789-2822 [code] |
| Image attachments | Text only: on-device OCR text goes in. The model cannot see pixels. | chatExecutionStore.ts:1241-1262 [code] |
| Document attachments | Added as context; kept on the device | chatExecutionStore.ts:2471-2473, :2685-2705 [code]; whether parsing is fully on-device is [unknown] |
| Vision models | Not selectable in v1 | catalog.ts shipsInV1 false [code] |
| Tools, connectors, web search, code execution | No. The Local branch returns before they run. Settings show "Cloud only" for the account switches. | chatExecutionStore.ts:3232-3236; capabilities/index.tsx:318 [code] |
| Image and video generation | No, `requires_cloud` | resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:252, resolveMobileVideoGenerationRequest.ts:107 [code] |
| Live voice | No, turn based only | liveVoiceAvailability.ts:17-25 [code] |
| Cloud sync and account history | No | sessionLabeling.ts:66-80 [code] |
| Share preview | Local chats can be previewed from the local store | share-preview/index.tsx:107-117 [code] |

Auto model modes also work in Local: they pick between installed models and the system model by tier. [code] (localModelRuntime.ts:44-85)

sections.heading: Differences between apps
sections.markdown:
| Surface | Local inference? | Runtime | Who supplies the model | Sign-in | Payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| surface:mobile | Yes | Apple system model, Google system model, ExecuTorch, llama.rn | App downloads it, or the OS already has it | Not needed | None found |
| surface:cli | Yes | Ollama or LM Studio (by default `localhost`) | User installs the server and pulls the model | Not needed | None ("needs no plan") |
| surface:vscode | Yes, through the CLI app-server | Same as CLI | User | Not needed for Local | None found |
| surface:desktop (Electron, public) | Chat: No. Coding sessions: Yes, through the bundled CLI. | CLI runtimes | User | Cloud chat needs Clerk sign-in; Local coding needs none known | Not established for Local coding |
| surface:desktop (Tauri, retained internal) | Code exists (Ollama commands) | Ollama | User | Not examined | Not examined |
| surface:web | No (browser has no host) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| surface:chrome | No. Heartbeat sends `localModels: false`. | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |

Notes:
- Public marketing says Local runs "in the CLI" with Ollama and LM Studio, costs $0, and needs no account. It describes Mobile with softer words ("built to keep the conversation, memory, and files on the device"). [code] (apps/web/app/local/page.tsx:25-70, :95-105)
- Web has full local-chat UI code that is gated to a host whose `shell` is `tauri` (`hostHasLocalMode`). Electron is explicitly excluded in its own comment. I found no Rust handler for `local_model_servers`, `local_model_list`, `local_chat_start` or the other four commands in the Tauri app, so I believe that path has no working backend today. [code] (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/host.ts:36-47, packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:690-692) and [inferred] (grep over apps/desktop/src-tauri, crates, apps and packages found these command names only in the web client, tests and the contract).
- The web local-chat path refuses attachments, sends text only, and does not call the cloud completions route or save the turn to the account. [code] (apps/web/features/chat/lib/local-turn.ts:43-60, :80-90)

sections.heading: Failure handling
sections.markdown:
**Mobile.**

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No model downloaded | Send is stopped. The tab shows "Download a model to chat" and offers Models. (chat.tsx:721-745, :1494) |
| Selected model gone from disk | Record is dropped, so the model shows Download again. If the chat still points at it: "This Local Mode chat uses a model that is no longer available on this device." (executorchModels.ts:81-100, chatExecutionStore.ts:1293-1294) |
| Offline at download | `offline` error; "Reconnect and try again." (modelDownload.ts:190-197) |
| Cellular without consent | `wifi_required` error naming "Settings, Storage, Download over cellular". (modelDownload.ts:198-208) |
| Not enough disk | `storage_full`, with the needed and free sizes. Needs the file size plus 256 MB. (modelDownload.ts:216-229) |
| Bad checksum | `ChecksumMismatchError` / `checksum_mismatch`. (modelDownload.ts:19-25, imports) |
| Device under 3.5 GB RAM | ExecuTorch and vision models are `unavailable` or `locked`: "This device cannot run this on-device model." (installStore.ts:111-132) |
| Device too hot | `Device is thermally throttled, inference paused.` (selector.ts:43, :113) |
| Out of memory | "This device ran out of memory for the on-device model. Close other apps, or choose a smaller model." (chatExecutionStore.ts:1413-1414) |
| System model off or still preparing | Marked unavailable for this session and the chat moves to a ready model. (localModelRuntime.ts:170-188, installStore.ts:262-290) |
| ExecuTorch fails | Falls back to llama.rn if a GGUF path exists; otherwise the error is thrown. (selector.ts:118-142) |
| Empty reply | "The local model returned an empty response. Try again with a shorter prompt." (chatExecutionStore.ts:3124-3126) |
| Stop pressed | Abort signal reaches the runtime; the turn ends without a committed answer. (chatExecutionStore.ts:3089-3118, :3125) |
| Our cloud host called in Local mode (not on the allow list) | `EgressBlockedError` code `EGRESS_BLOCKED_LOCAL_MODE`, thrown before any network I/O. (egressGuard.ts:24-35, :300-327) |

Removal of a model while it is answering is refused with "This model is replying now. Try again when it finishes." [code] (modelDownload.ts:69-76)

**CLI.** An unreachable server reports `not reachable ... Start Ollama` or `Start the local server and load a model`. A model not installed gives the list of what is installed, and tells the user to run `agi models scan`. Several providers holding the same model name give an error asking the user to pick a provider. [code] (local_models.rs:171-206, :294-330, :114-139)

**Desktop.** Any local-inference command gets `unsupported-platform` with the text that Desktop answers every conversation in the cloud. [code] (dispatcher.ts:3242, :3365-3367)

**VS Code.** With no local model: the picker says "No local models found. Start Ollama or LM Studio and load a model". A cloud-only utility with a Local default sends nothing and says so. [code] (ChatStateManager.ts:2047-2055, cloudModelBoundary.ts:34-47)

sections.heading: How it should work
sections.markdown:
These are established requirements, not statements about the code. Where code differs, the Gaps section says so.

- Local needs no AGI account, keeps storage on the device, makes no hidden cloud call, and fails closed when a feature needs remote compute. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492)
- Local and BYOK stay useful without paying AGI. [requirement] (docs/product/suite.md:84)
- A Local thread stays Local. Crossing to BYOK or Cloud is a visible fork with consent. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:115, docs/product/suite.md:55-62)
- A local model that cannot call tools should have tool use hidden or disabled for that route. [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:299)
- Brief for this page: local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription. Sign-in is a separate question. [requirement] (task brief; no repository document located that states "desktop" in this sentence)
- Competitor behaviour was not examined for this page. [unknown]

[proposed] If Desktop is meant to offer Local chat, it needs a decision record that replaces D-2026-09-15-04. Then a real handler for the six commands is needed, with no `!freePlan` gate on the web row. Until then, product copy must say Desktop reaches local models only through coding sessions.

sections.heading: Gaps
sections.markdown:
Implementation status (is the code there and connected) is kept apart from verification status (has anyone run it). Nothing here was run by me. I did not run the repository's tests, apps or builds.

| # | Gap | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Desktop vs requirement.** The brief says local inference on desktop is free of a paid subscription. Public Desktop (Electron) has no Local chat. It is refused by design in the dispatcher, per founder decision D-2026-09-15-04. Local models on Desktop exist only through a coding session that runs the bundled CLI. | [code] (dispatcher.ts:3237-3244, :3365-3367), [requirement] (docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:78-86) |
| 2 | **Web local-chat code with no backend.** The composer, the `useLocalModels` hook, `runLocalTurn` and the six command names exist, but no handler for them was found in the Tauri Rust code or Electron. The `hostHasLocalMode` gate lets only a `tauri` shell through. | [code] and [inferred] (see Differences) |
| 3 | **Free-plan gate in that Web code.** `!freePlan && localModels.available` hides the Local row for Free-plan users. If a host ever supports it, this ties Local to a paid plan. | [code] (ComposerFooter.tsx:1043, :1766) |
| 4 | **No checksum for ExecuTorch downloads in app code.** The installed record stores `sha256: null` and delegates the fetch to the library. Only GGUF downloads are verified by the app. | [code] (installStore.ts:187-205, modelDownload.ts:97-107) |
| 5 | **Catalog is not generated.** AGENTS.md says model IDs live only in the generated catalog. The local on-device catalog is a hand-written TypeScript list with URLs and hashes. Whether the model-id guards exempt it was not checked. | [code] (packages/platform/local-llm/src/catalog.ts), [requirement] (AGENTS.md section 4) |
| 6 | **Local text chats only.** Tool use, web search, vision and live voice are not available in Mobile Local. Local image text is OCR only. | [code] (see Rules) |

| 9 | **Mobile v1 vision models are not shippable.** `qwen`-family vision entries have `shipsInV1: false`, so the premium Auto profile falls back to the default text model. | [code] (catalog.ts:59-60, localModelRuntime.ts:57-62) |
| 10 | **Mobile Local mode is not fully offline from AGI.** The requirement says Local makes no hidden cloud call. The guard lets signed-in account controls (terms, age check, account deletion, scheduling, step-up, data export) reach AGI servers, and passes any non-AGI host (Mobile has no own-key mode, so that is a boundary gap, not a feature). The account controls are user-driven and carry no chat content by the code's own comment, so this is a narrow, visible exception rather than a hidden chat route. Whether product copy and the first-run disclosure state it was not checked. | [code] (egressGuard.ts:24-35, :210-244, :300-327), [requirement] (docs/product/requirements.md:480-492) |
| 11 | **Verification.** I found test files for these paths (listed in How to verify) but I did not run them, and found no document recording a real device run of local chat. | [unknown] |

key_facts.fact: Public Desktop (Electron) refuses every local-inference command with unsupported-platform and reports localModels false; its chat is Cloud-only.
The six refused commands are local_model_servers, local_model_list, local_chat_start, local_chat_cancel, local_model_settings_read and local_model_settings_write.
Desktop coding sessions run the bundled CLI, which can use a local model; this is the only way local models reach public Desktop.
Mobile has four local runtime names: foundation_models (Apple), aicore (Google), executorch, and llama_rn, grouped into tiers 1, 2 and 3.
ExecuTorch (tier 2) needs at least 3500 MB RAM, or unknown RAM with the module present; llama.rn (tier 3) is always marked available.
Four catalog entries ship on Mobile v1 (default text, lite text, Apple system model, Google system model); vision entries are not shippable.
The on-device model catalog is a hand-written TypeScript list, not the generated model catalog.
Mobile model downloads come from Hugging Face over HTTPS; GGUF files are SHA-256 verified, resumable, Wi-Fi only by default, and need free disk of file size plus 256 MB.
ExecuTorch downloads are fetched by the react-native-executorch resource fetcher; the app records sha256 null for them, so it does not verify a checksum itself.

Model files are stored under documents/models/<id>/model.gguf and documents/react-native-executorch/, excluded from backup; installs are recorded in the installed_models table of the on-device encrypted SQLite database.
Mobile Local chat does not require sign-in: routing sends a signed-out user to the app after the age gate and onboarding, and the Local send branch has no auth check.
The age gate runs before everything on Mobile including Local Mode, and the answer is held on the device.
Mobile Local turns carry no plan, entitlement or consent check; those calls are in the cloud branch only.
A Mobile Local chat refuses cloud models and a cloud chat refuses local models, with an error asking for a separate chat.
Mobile Local branch returns before tools, web search, connectors and sync; account switches show 'Cloud only'; image/video generation and live voice need cloud.
On Mobile Local, image attachments become on-device OCR text only; the model cannot see pixels.

The mobile egress guard's message describes Local Mode as 'on-device + BYOK only', although Mobile has no own-key mode. The guard throws EgressBlockedError (EGRESS_BLOCKED_LOCAL_MODE) for our managed-cloud hosts before any network I/O, except for an allow list.

In Mobile Local mode the guard still allows signed-in account controls to AGI servers: terms acceptance, the age check that opens Cloud, account deletion status, scheduling and cancellation, the deletion identity check, and data export. The guard comment says none carries chat content. It also allows a user-sent content report, withdrawal controls, and any non-AGI host (a boundary gap, since Mobile has no own-key mode; the guard comment's 'BYOK direct-to-provider' is stale).
Local Mobile sessions are labelled local_device storage with syncEligible false; cloud sync is queued only in cloud mode.
The CLI supports exactly two local runtimes, Ollama (default http://localhost:11434) and LM Studio (default http://localhost:1234/v1); it discovers models but does not download them.
The CLI Local first run needs no account and never shows cloud login; README states Local mode and BYOK need no plan.
CLI Local sessions refuse cloud calls (CloudClient::admit allows Managed only), and the device heartbeat only runs for Managed, so Local does not report to AGI servers.
VS Code has no model runtime of its own; it asks the CLI app-server for local models and shows an 'On this device' group; an AGI Cloud account is not required for Local.
VS Code never swaps a Local default model for a cloud model; Code Review, Suggest Terminal Command and inline completions run only on AGI Cloud and send nothing when a Local model is selected.

The Chrome extension has no local inference. Its device heartbeat to the cloud bridge always sends capabilities.localModels false, and the only 'ollama' and 'lmstudio' strings in its side panel are provider icon ids.
Web has local-chat UI and client code gated to a host whose shell is tauri; no handler for the six local-inference commands was found in Rust or Electron, so the path appears to have no backend.
The Web composer hides the Local models row for Free-plan users (!freePlan && localModels.available), a plan-linked rule in a path that is not reachable on Electron.
The shared local-inference contract requires loopback base URLs, refuses attachments, and hides models under 1B parameters.
Public marketing says Local runs in the CLI with Ollama and LM Studio, costs $0 and needs no account.
Requirement: Local mode needs no AGI account, keeps storage local, makes no hidden cloud call and fails closed.

doc.summary: Models come from one generated catalog (curated JSON compiled into a registry for TypeScript and Rust). Family slots say which generation is live. Auto picks a model per message from plan, task, capability, privacy rules, health and expected cost. Manual choice is plan-gated. Each app warns or falls back when a model lacks an ability. Two resolvers (TypeScript, Rust) share one policy and a conformance fixture. Review update: 8 of 28 live family defaults were promoted without the eval gate, and 27 of 28 family fallback chains are empty. Local needs no account (Mobile after its age confirmation, CLI, VS Code); the Local Mode plan is listed for web, desktop and mobile in the plan table only, and web and the public Electron Desktop have no Local mode.

sections.heading: What it is and why it exists
sections.markdown:
This page covers how AGI Workforce lists models and chooses one for each message. It supports two requirements: the product is **model agnostic** (one experience over many models) and **provider agnostic** (many inference hosts, none required). [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4, §7; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:7-10)

**Plain terms**
- *Catalog*: the list of models with their facts (price, limits, abilities). Hand-edited input is `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json`; the compiler writes the generated files. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:35-58; AGENTS.md:§4)
- *Registry*: the compiled catalog plus routes, harnesses, runtime profiles and Auto policy. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/generated/registry.ts)
- *Family slot*: a named seat such as "the balanced model of one vendor". The slot, not the code, says which generation sits in it. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/model-families.json)
- *Route*: one way to serve a model (a provider host plus a harness, which is the adapter that talks to that host). The same model can have several routes at different prices. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:143-162; docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:36-58)
- *Trust mode*: where a request may run. The code names `local`, `on_device`, `byok` (own key) and `managed_cloud`. The product modes are mode:local, mode:own-key and mode:cloud. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:36)
- *Auto*: the default choice. The router picks a model for every message. *Manual*: the user names a model. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1722-1760)
- *Slot* in Auto policy: a named preference such as a cheap general slot or a coding slot, listed in `routing-policies.json`. There are 47 of them. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json, auto.slots)

The rule is that no consumer keeps its own copy of model data, and a model ID may be a literal only inside the catalog. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§3, §4)

Sources of truth, highest rank first: generated registry and policy JSON, then the resolver code, then tests, then prose. Where this page and a doc disagree, the code wins. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§2)

sections.heading: How it works today
sections.markdown:
### 1. Build the catalog
1. A person edits `packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json` (and the other catalog files: routes, harnesses, gateways, developers, governance, retired models, routing policies, family slots). [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:40-58)
2. `pnpm sync:models` runs the compiler. It checks the output against `schema/registry.schema.json` with Ajv, resolves `family:<provider>/<family>` references to the live model, and writes: `packages/ai/model-registry/generated/registry.json` and `registry.ts`, `packages/contracts/types/src/models.json`, and Rust mirrors in `crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/generated/` and `crates/agiworkforce-model-registry/src/generated/`. [code] (compile.mjs:26-31,40-79,135-146; package.json:386-388)
3. `pnpm sync:models:check` fails when generated files drift. Never hand-edit `models.json`. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4) [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/package.json scripts)
4. Guards fail an inline model-ID literal: `check:model-id-literals` (TS/JS) and a Rust script. [code] (package.json:219; AGENTS.md:§4)

The generated registry today has 394 models, 463 routes, 38 harnesses and 15 runtime profiles (counted by reading `generated/registry.json` for this page; this is a snapshot, not a stable fact). [executed-by-reading, not a test run] 389 models are `live`.

### 2. Capability data per model
Every model carries one fixed vocabulary of 22 capability names (text/image/audio/video in and out, streaming, structured output, function calling, reasoning, image editing, realtime, reranking, tool schema support, computer use, agentic, web search, deep research, code execution, prompt caching). `null` means "not verified" and consumers treat it as not offered. [code] (packages/ai/model-registry/schema/registry.schema.json:729-800)

The registry splits these into **intrinsic** (about the model) and **route-dependent** (needs a provider route or an AGI harness, so never sufficient alone). [code] (registry.schema.json:1027-1050; model-catalog.ts:190-194) The docs say the same: web search, memory, MCP, code execution and computer use are not intrinsic model abilities. [requirement] (AGENTS.md:§4)

Apps read a simpler 13-flag view (`streaming`, `tools`, `vision`, `json`, `thinking`, `computerUse`, `agentic`, `imageGen`, `videoGen`, `search`, `research`, `codeExecution`, `caching`) mapped from the registry names. [code] (model-catalog.ts:172-188) Surfaces must read this metadata, never guess from a model name. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:34)

### 3. Which generation is live (family slots)
`model-families.json` has 28 family slots. Each has an `active` model, a `previous` one, a bounded `fallbackChain` (policy limit 3), a history, and a snapshot of price, capabilities and limits taken at promotion. [code] (model-families.json policy.fallbackChainLimit; families.*) Promotion gates are: provider availability, family identity, lifecycle eligibility, capability coverage, regression thresholds (cost rise limit 25%), registry validation. Preview models never take a stable slot. [code] (model-families.json policy)

Commands: `pnpm models:families` (inspect), `models:families:promote`, `models:families:rollback`, each with `--slot <id> --apply`. [code] (package.json:394-396; AGENTS.md:§4)

Routes and defaults point at `family:<provider>/<family>`, so swapping a model edits only the family file. [code] (routing-policies.json auto.slots, e.g. `modelKey` values of the form `family:...`)

Current state (read 2026-11-24): of the 28 slots, 13 are marked `seeded` (taken from the authored roster, no gate run) and 15 carry a real promotion record. [code] (model-families.json) **Eight active records say the eval gate was not run**: openai/gpt-frontier, gpt-balanced, gpt-fast, gpt-image; (model name), (model name); google/(model name) (different wording, same meaning) and google/gemini-flash-image. At least one says it was made on the owner's instruction. [code] (model-families.json, families.*.active.promotionReason; re-counted by script on 2026-11-24) So several live defaults skipped the promotion gate that AGENTS.md:§4 describes. [inferred]

**Fallback chains are almost always empty.** 27 of 28 slots have a `fallbackChain` of length 0 and one has length 1, though the policy limit is 3. For most families the only recovery from a bad promotion is rollback to the `previous` model, not a fallback chain. [code] (model-families.json, counted by script; packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/families.mjs:374)

To see the live model for a slot, read that file or run `pnpm models:families`; this page does not name models.

### 4. Choosing a model: Auto
The resolver is `resolveAutoRoute` in `packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts`. A request carries: the selection (`auto`, a profile alias, or a model), task type, plan tier, trust mode, current model, and optional rules (US-only, zero data retention, no-training, residency region, workspace model policy, excluded providers and hosts, budget left, health data). [code] (auto.ts:165-376)

Steps for an Auto request:
1. **Refuse early** if the trust mode is not permitted, a mandatory session capability is missing (`mandatory_capability_unavailable`), or the runtime profile does not fit. [code] (auto.ts:1722-1740, 568-612)
2. **Pick a cost band.** Aliases are `auto` (default, computed per task), `auto-economy`, `auto-balanced`, `auto-premium`. For `auto`, the task chooses the band (for example simple chat and general use economy, coding and reasoning premium, long context balanced). Then `resolveRoutingLane` clamps the band by the plan's entry in `tierMaximumProfiles`: free and basic economy, pro balanced, max, enterprise and byok premium. The plan id is first passed through `normalizeTier`, because `tierMaximumProfiles` has no keys for `max_15x`, `team` or `team_premium`; an unknown result defaults to economy. [code] (routing-policies.json auto.aliases, autoProfileByTask, tierMaximumProfiles; auto.ts:1198-1206)
3. **Take the ordered slots** for that task and band, restricted to the plan's allow-list `tierAllowedSlots` (six entries: free, basic, pro, max, enterprise, byok). Free gets three slots. A separate `fallbackSlot` is also chosen per tier from that list. This allow-list, not only the band clamp, decides which models a plan can reach. [code] (auto.ts:1205-1207; routing-policies.json auto.tierAllowedSlots)
4. **Optional reorder stages**: task-family stage (quality floor then cost order; kill switch `AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE`), caller `preferSlots` (reorder only), canary and shadow. [code] (auto.ts:1198-1225; task-family-routing.ts; packages/ai/routing/README.md)
5. **Prefer the conversation's current model** (continuity, protects prompt cache) while it is still eligible, affordable and, under the task-family stage, not more than 2 times the cost of the cheapest candidate that meets the floor. [code] (auto.ts:755, 1840-1900; routing-policies.json auto.continuity)
6. **Walk the slots**: each candidate must pass eligibility; the first dispatchable, affordable one wins. A slot whose model would bill a long prompt at a dearer input tier hands over to a cheaper backup. [code] (auto.ts:1960-2030)
7. **Fallbacks**: if only unhealthy candidates remain, try health fallbacks, then the fallback slot, then a jurisdiction fallback slot, else `no_eligible_route`. The decision lists up to 4 fallback routes, with at most 2 same-model routes before another model. [code] (auto.ts:757-764, 2030-2125)

**Eligibility of one model** (`evaluateEligibility`): the model must be in the account's admitted set, live, not deprecated or past its retirement date, allowed for the plan, allowed by US-only / excluded-provider / no-training / developer-country rules, have a route in the request's trust mode, hold every intrinsic capability the task needs, and meet the task's minimum context. [code] (auto.ts:1340-1430)

**Eligibility of one route** (`routeAdmissionRejections`): not on an excluded host, inside the required region, allowed by the workspace policy, commercial status not blocked (experimental routes cannot serve managed traffic), selectable and live, harness runs on the calling app, zero-retention satisfied if asked, no-training satisfied if asked, harness features the task needs are `implemented`. [code] (auto.ts:1042-1140)

### 5. How routing weighs cost, quality, latency, privacy
| Factor | Where it acts | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy and policy | Admission, a hard filter before any ranking. Trust mode, zero data retention, no-training, region, US-only, developer country, workspace policy | auto.ts:1042-1140, 1340-1430 |
| Quality | Slot order per task and band; per-family `qualityFloor` in the task-family stage | routing-policies.json auto.tasks, auto.taskFamilies; task-family-routing.ts |
| Cost | Inside the floor-meeting set, order by expected cost of the route actually dispatched; routes then rank by expected cents; budget left can skip a model; long-prompt price tiers trigger a backup | docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:78-98; auto.ts:1144-1170, 1623-1690 |
| Latency and health | Routes rank healthy first, then credentialed, then lower observed penalty (failure rate and time to first token in bands), then cost, then the model default route, then route id. Switch `AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH` | auto.ts:859-980, 1144-1160 |
| Cache | A route holding a warm cache is kept unless it costs more than 1.25 times the cheapest | auto.ts:735, 1160-1178 |

The named profiles (Instant, High, Code, Research) carry quality, cost and latency weights, but `weightedScore` is exported and not called by `resolveAutoRoute`; only the profile id is attached to the decision. [code] (packages/ai/routing/src/profiles/index.ts:137-169; auto.ts:1466) So latency has no direct weight in slot ordering today. [inferred]

### 6. Manual choice
If the selection is not an alias, the resolver checks that model alone with the same eligibility rules and returns it as `explicit`. A pinned route (`requiredRouteId`) must be healthy and credentialed or the call fails with `explicit_route_ineligible`. A named model ignores the Auto-only `excludedProviders` list but still obeys excluded hosts, region and developer-country rules. [code] (auto.ts:1750-1850, 150-235 comments) Same-model routes rotate before any substitution. [requirement] (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:55-57)

### 7. Preview
`previewAutoRoute` explains a decision (candidates, admission, reasons) with no upstream call, and shares helpers with the real resolver so it cannot name a different winner. [code] (packages/ai/routing/README.md; auto.ts:2204) It is exposed as api:POST /api/llm/v1/route/preview. [code] (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/route/preview/route.ts:200)
